title: KESK’ten 12 Aralık Tandoğan Mitingine çağrı: "86 milyonun oluşturduğu bütçeden emekçiler pay alamıyor"
content:
Çorum- Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu (KESK), 2027 yılı bütçesinde emekçilere yeterli pay ayrılmadığı gerekçesiyle Çorum’da basın açıklaması düzenledi. KESK Eş Genel Başkanı Ahmet Karagöz’ün katıldığı açıklamada, bütçenin emekçilerden yana hazırlanması çağrısı yapılırken, 12 Aralık’ta Ankara’da düzenlenecek mitinge katılım çağrısında bulunuldu.

KESK Eş Genel Başkanı Ahmet Karagöz, Eğitim Sen Örgütlenme Sekreteri İzzet İldeş ve KESK’e bağlı sendikaların yöneticilerinin katılımıyla Kadeş Barış Meydanı’nda basın açıklaması düzenlendi. “Sermayeye değil, emekçiye bütçe”, “Gün gelecek devran dönecek, AKP halka hesap verecek” ve “Kurtuluş yok tek başına, ya hep beraber ya hiçbirimiz” sloganlarının atıldığı açıklamaya KESK’e bağlı sendikaların şube başkanları ve üyelerinin yanı sıra Yeni Parti İl Başkan Yardımcısı Garip Özgür, Emek Partisi İl Başkanı Muharrem Özünel, DEM Parti İl Başkanı Hasan Satılmış ve Çorum Emek ve Demokrasi Platformu Sözcüsü Av. Ahmet Özdel de destek verdi.

Basın açıklamasında konuşan Karagöz, AKP’nin 25 yıl önce yasaklar, yoksulluk ve yolsuzlukla mücadele vaadiyle iktidara geldiğini ancak bugün ülkenin ağır sorunlarla karşı karşıya olduğunu söyledi. Karagöz, 86 milyon yurttaşın oluşturduğu kaynakların toplumun geniş kesimlerinin ihtiyaçları doğrultusunda kullanılmadığını savunarak, bütçeden emekçilerin, işçilerin, emeklilerin, çiftçilerin, öğrencilerin ve kadınların yeterli pay alamadığını ifade etti.

Bütçelerin, gelirlerin kimlerden toplandığını ve hangi kesimler için harcandığını gösteren belgeler olduğunu belirten Karagöz, mevcut bütçede sermaye gruplarının, cemaatlerin, tarikatların ve çok uluslu şirketlerin öncelikli olduğunu kaydetti. Toplumun ortak kaynaklarını oluşturmasına rağmen geniş kesimlerin bütçeden yeterince yararlanamadığını dile getiren Karagöz, 12 Aralık’ta Ankara Tandoğan Meydanı’nda KESK, DİSK, TMMOB ve TTB tarafından “Gelirden, vergiden adalet; halk için bütçe, demokratik Türkiye” sloganıyla miting düzenleneceğini açıkladı.

2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerine de değinen Karagöz, bütçede emekçilere yeterli pay ayrılmadığını, buna karşın faiz, rant, savunma sanayisi, silah şirketleri, cemaatler ve tarikatlara kaynak aktarıldığını belirtti. Çocukların okulda tükettiği simit ve ayrandan alınan vergilerin dahi bütçeye katkı sunduğunu belirten Karagöz, okula giden her dört öğrenciden birinin aç olduğunu öne sürdü. Üniversite öğrencilerinin barınma sorunları nedeniyle eğitimlerini bırakıp ailelerinin yanına dönmek zorunda kaldığını kaydetti.

Çiftçilerin ürettikleri ürünleri değerinde satamadığını, borçlarını ödeyebilmek için ürünlerini veya topraklarını elden çıkarmak zorunda kaldığını ifade eden Karagöz, esnafın da ekonomik sıkıntılar nedeniyle kepenk kapattığını, iş yerlerinin iflas ettiğini ve çalışanların işten çıkarıldığını söyledi. Ülkenin insan onuruna yakışır bir yaşam için yeterli kaynaklara sahip olduğunu savunan Karagöz, kaynakların adil dağıtılmadığını dile getirdi.

Emekçilerin yoksulluk, emeklilerin açlık, gençlerin geleceksizlik ve belirsizlik, kadınların ise yoksulluk ve eşitsizlikle mücadele ettiğini belirten Karagöz, bu kesimlerin ihtiyaçlarına yönelik kaynak aktarılmadığını söyledi. Meraların, ormanların ve doğal alanların talan edildiğini, işçilerin iş yerlerinde yaşamını yitirdiğini ifade eden Karagöz, AKP’nin 25 yıllık iktidarı döneminde Türkiye genelinde 39 bin işçinin hayatını kaybettiğini belirterek, işçi sağlığı ve iş güvenliğine daha fazla kaynak ayrılması gerektiğini vurguladı.

2027 yılı bütçe taslağında kaynakların yüzde 20’sinin faize, yüzde 18’inin silah sektörüne ayrıldığını ifade eden Karagöz, ülkede yürütülen barış sürecini değerli bulduklarını ancak savunma ve silah sektörüne yüksek miktarda kaynak aktarılmasını düşündürücü olarak değerlendirdiklerini söyledi. Kaynakların işçilerin, emekçilerin ve emeklilerin talepleri doğrultusunda kullanılmasını istedi.

Kamusal hizmetlerin azaldığını, kurumların ve fabrikaların özelleştirildiğini belirten Karagöz, kamu yatırımlarına daha fazla pay ayrılması, özelleştirmeler yerine kamulaştırmaya kaynak aktarılması çağrısında bulundu. Meraların, doğal alanların ve zeytinliklerin sermayeye açılmasına tepki gösterdi.

Ülkede yoksulluğun yanı sıra yasaklar ve adaletsizliklerle de mücadele edildiğini savunan Karagöz, gazetecilerin, seçilmiş belediye başkanlarının, milletvekillerinin, hak arayan işçilerin ve sendikacıların tutuklu olduğunu, öğrencilerin gözaltına alındığını söyledi.

Asgari ücretin 28 bin lira, emekli maaşının 25 bin 352 lira olduğu, küçük Anadolu kentlerinde kiraların 25-30 bin liraya ulaştığı bir ortamda yurttaşların geçim sıkıntısı yaşadığını belirten Karagöz, insanların kira, fatura ve çocuklarının ihtiyaçlarını karşılamakta zorlandığını söyleyerek, yıllarca prim ödeyerek emekli olan yurttaşların açlıkla karşı karşıya bırakılmaması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Karagöz, konuşmasının sonunda emekliler, işçiler, emekçiler, çocuklarını aç yatırmak zorunda kalan aileler, eğitimini yarıda bırakmak zorunda kalan öğrenciler, ürününü satamadığı için traktörünü ve toprağını elden çıkarmak zorunda kalan üretici köylüler ile esnaf başta olmak üzere “Geçinemiyorum” diyen herkesi 12 Aralık’ta Ankara Tandoğan Meydanı’nda düzenlenecek mitinge davet etti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Belediye meclislerinde başkan seçimine ilişkin yeni usul Resmi Gazete'de
content:
Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı'nın hazırladığı yönetmelik değişikliği 20 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. Düzenleme, belediye meclislerinin kendi üyeleri arasından yaptığı başkan ve başkanvekili seçimlerinin kurallarını yeniden belirliyor.



















9 belediye başkanı AKP'ye geçti




19 Kasım 2026










Yeni oylama usulü




Oylamada basılı birleşik oy pusulası kullanılacak. Üyeler, tercih ettikleri adayın adının yanına mühür basacak. Oy pusulasına elle isim yazılmayacak.




Meclis salonunda en az iki kapalı oy kabini bulunacak. Mühürlü zarflar şeffaf sandığa atılacak. Adaylar oturumu yönetemeyecek, ancak oy kullanabilecek. Her parti grubu ile bağımsızlar birer gözlemci bildirebilecek.



















Ahmet Özer: "Ver belediyeyi gir içeri suçuna sonra bakarız dediler"




11 Kasım 2026










Adaylık ve geçersiz oylar




Adaylık başvuruları, valinin belirleyeceği seçim toplantısının ilk oturumunda meclis başkanlık divanına bildirilecek. Bu oturumdan sonra yeni başvuru alınmayacak. Adaylar her tur öncesi çekilebilecek.




Mühür taşımayan, tanıtıcı işaret içeren ya da birden fazla adaya mühür basılmış pusulalar geçersiz sayılacak. Sandıktan çıkan zarf sayısı oy kullanan üye sayısını aşarsa ilgili tur iptal edilip yeniden oylama yapılacak.




Saklama




Pusulalar ve zarflar, dava süresi dolana kadar saklanacak. Dava açılmışsa mahkeme kararı kesinleşene kadar saklanmaya devam edilecek.







Ne olmuştu?




Düzenleme, oylamada gizliliği ve şeffaflığı artırmayı, adaylık ve oy kullanma süreçlerini standartlaştırmayı ve itirazlarda izlenebilirliği sağlamayı amaçlıyor. Haberde 31 Mart 2024'ten bu yana, 4'ü büyükşehir olmak üzere 117 belediyede yönetimin transferlerle değiştiği belirtiliyor.







(FY)

title: Bir yarış oyunundan kültürel fenomene: Grand Theft Auto'nun ortaya çıkış hikâyesi
content:
Video oyunları dünyasının en çok beklenen yapımlarından Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), 13 yıllık bekleyişin, ertelemelerin ve sızıntıların ardından oyuncularla buluştu.

Bugün milyonlarca insanın merakla beklediği serinin temelleri, 1997 yılında İskoçya'nın Dundee kentinde, DMA Design adlı görece küçük bir oyun stüdyosunda atılmıştı.

Bulmaca oyunu Lemmings ile başarı kazanan stüdyo, başlangıçta Race'n'Chase adını taşıyan bir yarış oyunu geliştirmeyi planlıyordu. Ancak ekibin geleneksel yarış oyunlarından farklı bir deneyim yaratma arayışı, video oyunları tarihini değiştirecek bir fikrin ortaya çıkmasını sağladı.

Serinin yaratıcılarından Dave Jones, dönemin oyunlarından farklılaşmak için geliştirdikleri en önemli özelliğin, oyuncuların kullandıkları otomobillerden inebilmesi olduğunu anlatıyor.

Oyuncuların araç değiştirebilmesi, otomobil çalabilmesi ve şehirde yaya olarak dolaşabilmesi, farklı oyun türlerinin bir araya gelmesine olanak tanıdı.

Geliştirme ekibi başlangıçta oyuncuların hem suçlu hem de polis memuru olarak oynayabileceği bir oyun tasarlamıştı. Ancak polis karakterini yönetmenin oyunculara getireceği kurallar ve sınırlamalar nedeniyle bu fikirden vazgeçildi.

Jones, o dönemde aldıkları kararı, "Bir noktada, 'Biliyor musunuz, kötü adamı oynamak çok daha eğlenceli' dedik, bu yüzden oyunun konusu da bu oldu" sözleriyle anlatıyor.

İlk GTA'nın satışları, stüdyonun önceki başarısı Lemmings'e kıyasla yavaş ilerledi. Jones'a göre bunun nedenlerinden biri, oyunun sunduğu yeniliklerin ancak oynandığında anlaşılabilmesiydi.

İlk oyunun senaryosunu yazan ve tanıtımından sorumlu olan Brian Baglow ise oyunun yıl boyunca satışlarını sürdürdüğünü, oyuncuların birbirlerine tavsiye etmesiyle giderek daha geniş bir kitleye ulaştığını belirtiyor.

Suç ve şiddet temaları nedeniyle İngiltere Parlamentosunda da tartışma konusu olan GTA'nın yasaklanması yönünde çağrılar yapıldı. Oyunun yayıncısı BMG Interactive'in bu tartışmaları bir pazarlama stratejisi olarak kullandığı daha sonra ortaya çıktı.

Kuşbakışı kamera açısı ve iki boyutlu grafikleriyle bugünkü GTA oyunlarından oldukça farklı görünen ilk yapım, serinin kendine özgü mizah anlayışının da temellerini attı.

The Guardian'ın video oyunları editörü Keza MacDonald'a göre GTA'nın Amerikan şehirlerini abartılı biçimde tasvir etmesinde, geliştiricilerinin İskoçya'dan gelen gözlem gücünün önemli bir payı vardı.

MacDonald, "Bu son derece hiciv dolu bir oyun. ABD'nin aşırı bireyci ve aşırı kapitalist yapısını doğrudan hedef alıyor" diyor.

İlk oyunun sınırlı bütçesi ve gerçek markaların lisanslarını kullanmanın maliyeti, geliştiricileri kurgusal markalar yaratmaya yöneltti. Hayali radyo istasyonları, reklamlar ve işletme isimleri zamanla serinin karakteristik özellikleri arasına girdi.

Başlangıçta ekonomik zorunluluklardan doğan bu tercihler, oyuncuların içinde bulunduğu şehrin kendine ait bir kültürü ve gündelik hayatı olduğu hissini güçlendirdi.

Baglow, yaklaşık 30 yıl sonra ilk oyuna ilişkin en fazla gurur duyduğu özelliğin bu kurgusal dünyanın inşası olduğunu söylüyor.

2013 yılında piyasaya sürülen GTA 5, üç gün içinde 1 milyar dolar gelir elde ederek eğlence sektöründe o güne kadarki en hızlı gelir elde eden ürün oldu.

Serinin etkisi yıllar içinde video oyunlarının sınırlarını da aştı. GTA'nın adı sinema filmlerinde ve gündelik konuşmalarda kullanılan bir kültürel referansa dönüştü.

MacDonald, serinin ilk dönemlerinde sinemadan yoğun biçimde beslendiğini, bugün ise sinemanın GTA'dan ne ölçüde etkilendiğinin tartışıldığını belirtiyor.

Jones'a göre serinin bu kadar geniş bir kitleye ulaşmasının nedenlerinden biri, oyuncuların aşina oldukları bir dünyada geçmesi. Fantastik veya bilim kurgu evrenlerinin aksine GTA, oyunculardan yeni bir dünyanın kurallarını öğrenmelerini beklemiyor.

Serinin yeni oyununun hem kapsam hem de gelir bakımından GTA 5'i geride bırakması bekleniyor.

PlayStation ve Xbox, GTA 6'nın kendi dijital mağazalarının tarihinde en fazla ön sipariş verilen oyun olduğunu açıkladı. Oyunun 212 gigabaytlık boyutunun da oyuncuların ön sipariş vererek indirme işlemini önceden tamamlamak istemelerinde etkili olduğu değerlendiriliyor.

Oyuna yönelik ilgi, reklam kampanyalarıyla şehirlerin gündelik hayatına da taşındı. Londra'daki Selfridges mağazasında oyunun kurgusal şehri Vice City temalı bir alan oluşturulurken Miami'de GTA evrenindeki hayali markaların reklamları yayımlandı.

Video oyunları sektörüne yeni bir ekonomik ivme kazandırması beklenen GTA 6'nın yaratıcılarının çalışmaları ise serinin ilk geliştiricileri tarafından da merakla takip ediliyor.

İlk oyunun yapımcılarından Brian Baglow, yeni oyuna erken erişim imkânı bulamadığını ancak diğer oyuncular gibi ön sipariş verdiğini anlatıyor.

Baglow, yaklaşık 30 yıl önce küçük bir ekiple geliştirdikleri oyunun bugün ulaştığı noktaya ilişkin duygularını şu sözlerle ifade ediyor:

"Son 29 yıldır dünyanın geri kalanının bu oyuna âşık oluşunu izlemek büyük bir mutluluktu. Bu oyun çok sayıda insan için çok şey ifade ediyor. Gerçekten harikaydı."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: winter oak
title: Feted or forgotten? A tale of two very different anarchists
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




An important split took place in the French anarchist movement at the very end of the nineteenth century.




This revolved around the question of whether the conviction of Jewish army captain Alfred Dreyfus for treason represented an important question of injustice and institutional anti-semitism or whether, 

au contraire

, the case was irrelevant to the anarchist struggle.




François Jarrige writes in the 

latest issue

 of 

Brasero: revue de contre-histoire

: “The Dreyfus affair, which tore France apart from 1897-1898 onwards, also divided the anarchist milieu”. [1]




In what he terms “an extreme polarisation”, anarchists, “traditionally distrustful of the army and the state, split into convinced 

dreyfusards

 and supporters of a strict indifference to what they considered an internal conflict within bourgeois institutions.




“Sébastien Faure, a major figure in the anarchist movement and co-founder of 

Le Libertaire

, nevertheless managed to drag a number of activists into the active defence of Dreyfus”. [2]




We’ll come back to Faure later, but first I want to relate what Jarrige has to say about one of the anarchists who refused to climb on board the 

dreyfusard

 bandwagon – 

Emile Gravelle (1855-1920)

.




He was the founder of a current in the French anarchist movement called 

naturien

 – there is no real English equivalent but the meaning is nature-loving or nature-based.










This, Jarrige explains, emerged in the Parisian 

quartier

 of Montmartre and was a current that was “critical of industrial society and its goods, idealising prehistorical and primitive living and calling for a return to nature”. [3]




Gravelle, an anarchist painter, illustrator, pamphleteer and activist, was one of the first to formulate such a critique of “progress” and “civilisation”, prefiguring the green anarchism that emerged towards the end of the twentieth century. [4]




An important influence on Gravelle’s understanding of the world was his five-year stay in Buenos Aires, after leaving his home town of Douai in northern France at the age of 30.




Jarrige writes: “At the time Argentina was going through a phase of expansion: political stabilisation after civil wars, the conquest of indigenous lands, the expansion of cattle-rearing on the great plains of the 

pampa

 and a massive influx of European immigrants. This context of brutal modernisation, mixing prosperity and social violence, had a deep impact on Gravelle…




“When he returned to France in 1890 he brought out a pamphlet in which he related his unpleasant experience. In this virulent text, 

La République argentine dénoncée

 (‘The Argentine Republic denounced’), he describes how he had been taken in by the embroidered tales of a ‘shipping agent in the 

rue de Dunkerque

‘, only to discover a reality of misery, exploitation and disillusionment.




“He writes about the diseases, the violence of the 

gauchos

, the insalubrity of the towns and the suffering of immigrants pushed into suicide or madness. This pamphlet, laced with bitterness, also bears witness to a political realization: Gravelle denounces the illusions of progress and the mechanisms of capitalist exploitation”. [5]










Gravelle’s years in South America shaped his understanding of modernity in another way. Through his encounters with indigenous Guarani people he discovered “man, in the midst of nature, happy as a god in the triumphant splendour of its strength and beauty”. [6]




Jarrige says this provided him with “an alternative model to the European ways of living shaped by industry, the growing consumerism and imperialism”. [7]




It fed his rejection of modern urbanisation and his aspiration to a way of life founded on simplicity, autonomy and closeness to nature – “when Gravelle returned to Paris, he was thus no longer simply an illustrator looking for work: he was the bearer of a vision of the world opposed to that of the European civilisation of his age”. [8]




In the early 1890s Gravelle set up home in Montmartre, a bohemian, artistic and anarchic enclave on a hill in Paris. At the time, it was still semi-rural and was imbibed with the spirit of resistance to the new urban order, inherited from the Paris Commune of 1871. 




Says Jarrige: “This landscape in transition, where the industrial smoke of the capital mixed with the last remains of rurality, deeply nourished Gravelle’s anarchist imagination”. [9]




“The rapid transformation of the 

quartier

 under the impact of urbanisation and property speculation reinforced in Gravelle’s mind the idea that modern civilisation destroys the natural conditions of human life. His drawings often show black plumes of factory smoke, collapsed quarries or silhouettes of old windmills.










“

La Butte

 [The Hill] became for him a laboratory where he could observe the advance of industrial modernity, but also a place for imagining alternatives. It symbolised a communalist tradition of protecting natural and public spaces threatened by power”. [10]




In 1894 Gravelle founded a four-page journal called 

L’Etat naturel

 (‘The natural state’), which ran for four issues until 1898. Jarrige explains that this periodical, largely written and illustrated by Gravelle himself, was at the heart of 

naturienisme

, contrasting natural human life with the misery of factory workers, the ugliness of the city and the artificiality of “civilisation”. [11]




When Gravelle started a 

naturien

 group in Montmartre in 1895 it was joined by penniless artists, singers and people who worked on the railways, in a bank or as a cobbler or barrel-maker.




Comments Jarrige: “This very mixed group testifies to the attractiveness of the idea of returning to nature among individuals facing material precarity, the rapid upheavals of urban society and political disillusionment”. [12]




“The 

naturiens

 organised conferences, talks and even banquets which sometimes attracted nearly a hundred people. Their influence rapidly spread beyond Montmartre: groups appeared at the Bastille, in the Latin Quarter and then outside the capital, notably in Toulon and Bordeaux.










“Although they were few in number – with undoubtedly never more than a hundred or so members – the movement built itself around intense publishing activity”. [13]




Journals such as 

Le Bulletin des Harmoniens

 (‘The Bulletin of the Harmonians’), 

La Debâcle sociale

 (‘The Social Disaster’), 

L’Idée libre

 (‘The Free Idea’), 

La Nouvelle Humanité

 (‘The New Humanity’) and 

Le Naturien

 flourished at this time.




Jarrige tells us: “The first of the four issues of the journal 

Le Naturien

 was, moreover, distributed beyond Paris, in Bordeaux, Dijon, Le Havre, Limoges, Marseilles, Montpellier, Roubaix, Saint-Nazaire, Toulon and Tours”. [14]




In its final issue, in 1898, Gravelle questioned the relevance of the insurrections and revolutions usually favoured by anarchists and the “left”.




He insisted: “You could perpetually behead kings, depose emperors and disembowel presidents of the Republic, but the situation will remain the same as long as there are mines, factories and building sites.




“As long as the artificiality that has been established over the centuries is considered as the base of our system of living, there will be exploitation of man by man, there will be despoilment and the ongoing and aggrevated degradation of nature…










“To those who talk of revolution while still wanting to hold on to superfluous Artifice, we say this: you are conserving elements of servitude, you will therefore always be slaves; you think you can seize control of material production to appropriate it for yourselves, but, in reality, this material production which constitutes the strength of your oppressors is quite safe from your covetous regard”. [15]




Gravelle concluded that as long as this industrial system of production existed, the people would never know freedom. “Material Progress is the fruit of slavery”, he insisted. [16]




Jarrige says that this viewpoint, so starkly in contrast with the industrialist Marxist outlook, had a considerable influence on the French anarchist scene, until Gravelle became marginalised around 1898.




In April of that year his girlfriend, said to have been “a fervent 

naturienne

 since the beginning” died in hospital for now-unknown reasons and Gravelle was left in a state of shocked grief. [17]




At the same time, as we have heard, the Dreyfus affair dominated the political scene and by refusing to get involved, Gravelle was cut off from many other anarchists, although he was still involved in the movement until his death in 1920.




He seems to have particularly fallen out of favour because of supposedly “anti-semitic” illustrations, such as that of a French farmer disposing of a human-like vegetable labelled “Rothschild”. [18]










Jarrige does not challenge the “anti-semitic” label, but I would question whether drawing a humorous caricature of a well-known Jewish banker is “anti-semitic” 

per se

 – the figure is certainly not meant to represent Jews 

as a whole

, or even all Jewish bankers, because the name “Rothschild” is specifically written on the forehead.




Is it not more likely that the target of Gravelle’s anger was the Rothschilds 

in particular

 – not “because they were Jewish” but because he knew full well that they were 

enemies of the people

 [19] and bore much responsibility for the industrial-imperial misery and slavery he had been witnessing and denouncing both in France and Argentina?




Going back to the split in the French anarchist movement, the leading 

dreyfusard

 

Sébastien Faure (1858-1942)

 is the subject of another article in the same issue of 

Brasero

.




There Anne Steiner explains that he founded the weekly journal 

Le Libertaire

 in 1895 and then the daily newspaper 

Le Journal du Peuple

 which led the anarchist charge in defence of Dreyfus and against anti-semtitism.




He is also rememberd for founding 

La Ruche

 (‘The Hive’), an experimental “alternative” boarding school which housed forty-odd girls and boys between the ages of six and 16.




Paying due credit to the 

Archives anarchistes

 website, [20] she digs deeper into Faure’s character with reference to the judicial files, released in 2018, which can be consulted 

there

. [21]










In brief, Faure was a disgusting paedocriminal. The records show that in 1903 he was seen approaching three girls aged eight to 12 years old, offering them a few coins for sexual favours; in 1904 he was seen kissing a 12-year-old girl on the mouth; in 1907 he was found in the company of a woman suspected of prostituting her 14-year-old daughter and so on and so forth. [22]




Having been caught molesting little girls in the street in 1917 he fled Paris – taking with him funds from his journal and printing press – but was captured in Marseilles, found guilty and sentenced to six months in jail. At this point it transpired that he had, of course, also been abusing the children at his school 

La Ruche

. [23]




A scandal also soon erupted over his links to disgraced politician Louis Malvy, whose Ministry of the Interior had, during his 1914-1917 term in office, paid subsidies to Faure’s 

La Ruche

 even though it had no legal status. [24]




Denying suggestions that Faure had been let off the hook for his child abuse for so long  because of his links to the state, the former prefect of the Paris police, Emile Laurent,  said that this was not how it had worked.




Faure’s constant paedocriminal activties could not have been proven in court, he insisted, but they allowed the police to exert a certain pressure on the anarchist, such as by ordering him to moderate the terms of his written and oral political statements. [25]










Steiner writes: “All the activists thus learned at this point that Sébastien Faure (

pictured

), child abuser and client of barely pubescent prostitutes, was controlled by the prefect of the police, who was perfectly well aware of his criminal activity. This evoked, even beyond the anarchist movement, a certain 

malaise

 and much questioning”. [26]




But Faure, remarkably, protested his innocence and claimed that he had been framed in a complicated and politically motivated state operation.




Others leapt to his defence and in 1919 backed up his story in a booklet called 

Une infamie. L’affaire Sébastien Faure

 (‘Scandal: The Sébastien Faure affair’).




Says Steiner: “This plea in favour of the old anarchist activist managed to quieten the doubts of those who had been troubled by his conviction and even more so by the evidence at his trial which depicted him as a very unsavoury individual. Until less than than two years later, there was a new affair”. [27]




In 1921 Faure and two other men in their early sixties were caught dragging two little girls, aged 11 and 12, into a flat in Paris, where they sexually abused them for four hours. Other victims were discovered and he was jailed for eight months. [28]




One might have thought that this would have led the French anarchist movement to finally denounce Faure and expel him from their midst.




But no – after his arrest 

Le Libertaire

 and the 

L’Union anarchiste

 published a communiqué in 

L’Humanité

 calling on the whole working class to show solidarity with this “upright and impeccable activist”. [29]










And when he had been jailed, 

Le Libertaire

 of June 17 1921 deplored his conviction for what they termed an “insignificant weakness” and hailed him as “the courageous friend of the working class”. [30]




Their version was again that he was the victim of a police set-up to discredit “the best revolutionary propagandist in the country”. Ignoring his long record of child abuse, they claimed a young girl had been cunningly placed in his path to frame him. [31]




While Faure denied child abuse, he rather gave the game away by dismissing anarchists who disapproved of such behaviour as “bourgeois”. [32]




Steiner relates how the paedocriminal was welcomed back into the anarchist fold after coming out of jail again and in 1925 was able to launch his 

L’Encyclopedie anarchiste

 project with a hundred collaborators who did not seem bothered about his character.




She adds, clearly somewhat outraged, that the “neo-malthusian activist” Jeanne Humbert (

pictured below

) completely misrepresented the facts about Faure in the 1949 biography she wrote about him.




For instance, she depicted the 1917 offence as having involved him touching and rubbing himself against 

women

 in the street, when it was really 

ten-year-old girls

.




“Regarding the 1921 conviction, it’s even worse, as she describes the abused little girls as ‘debauched minors’, children of a ‘precocious vicefulness'”. Humbert also insisted that Faure did nothing to shock anyone not “blinded” by conventional morality. [33]










I was interested, surprised even, to see that the profile of Faure on French 

Wikipedia

 

mentions

 that accusations of his paedocriminality were confirmed by the judicial archives made public eight years ago – and that it points readers to the 

Archives anarchistes

 site. [34]




It adds that he was a Freemason. “Sébastien Faure was initiated on June 28 1884 at the 

Vérité du Grand Orient de France

 lodge at Bordeaux… On November 3 1905, he joined the 

Le Progrès

 lodge in Paris. He resigned from Freemasonry on December 20 1917 after 33 years of involvement”. [35]




So there we have it.




Sébastien Faure, the police-controlled freemasonic paedophile who diverted anarchist energy into a struggle against “anti-semitism”, is still revered by the movement today.




Emile Gravelle, the anti-imperialist, anti-industrialist and nature-defending artist and campaigner who dared to poke fun at the industrial-imperialist Rothschilds, is today an obscure and half-forgotten figure.




It really is about time that 

real anarchists

 [36] got to their feet and made their presence known!

author: Unknown
title: Gram altın 6 bin liranın altına geriledi
content:
Küresel piyasalardaki gelişmeler ve ABD merkezli makroekonomik beklentiler, altın fiyatlarında sert düşüşe yol açtı. Ons altın son günlerde yaşadığı kayıplarla 14 ayın en düşük seviyesine inerken, gram altın da kritik eşik olan 6 bin liranın altına geriledi.

20 Kasım işlemlerinde 3.550 dolara kadar inen ons altın, bugün TSİ 07.26 itibarıyla 3 bin 532 dolar seviyesinde işlem gördü. Gram altın ise 5 bin 716 liraya kadar geriledikten sonra sabah seansında TSİ 07.26 itibarıyla 5 bin 735 lira bandında hareket etti.

Altın fiyatları üzerindeki baskıda doların güçlenmesi belirleyici unsurlar arasında yer aldı. Dolar endeksinin 104 seviyesine dayanması, dolar cinsinden fiyatlanan altını diğer para birimlerini kullanan yatırımcılar açısından daha pahalı hale getirerek uluslararası talebi zayıflattı.

Düşüşte, ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) aralık ayında faiz artıracağı yönündeki beklentiler ve Fed cephesinden gelen "daha sıkı adımların gerekebileceğine" dair mesajlar etkili oldu. Öte yandan ABD tahvil piyasasında yükselen getiriler de altının cazibesini azalttı; ABD'nin 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'in üzerinde seyrederken, 10 yıllık enflasyondan arındırılmış reel getiri yüzde 2,85-2,90 bandına dayandı. Getirisi bulunmayan altın karşısında tahvillerin öne çıkması, değerli metal üzerindeki satış baskısını artırdı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Igor de Paula
title: Oxê de Xangô: o que representa o machado iorubá de duas lâminas que chegou ao STF
content:
Um machado com lâminas dos dois lados que simboliza a consideração de todos os lados de uma controvérsia. Esse é o Oxê de Xangô, um dos principais símbolos da Justiça e da busca pela verdade na tradição dos povos Iorubá da África Ocidental. 




O mesmo pode se dizer de Xangô, o Orixá do trovão e do fogo, que são elementos que representam justiça, razão, imparcialidade e equilíbrio. O Oxê é seu principal símbolo e ferramenta. 




Não por acaso essa foi a escultura escolhida para ser exposta no hall do Salão Nobre do edifício-sede do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), em Brasília. A cerimônia de descerramento da obra foi realizada na última terça-feira, 17 de novembro, em homenagem ao Dia da Consciência Negra, comemorado nesta sexta-feira, 20.




A chegada da escultura ao STF atende a uma solicitação do Instituto de Defesa dos Direitos das Religiões Afro-Brasileiras (Idafro). O pedido foi feito após o Plenário do Supremo, em novembro de 2024, decidir que a presença de símbolos religiosos em locais e órgãos públicos não é capaz de ferir a laicidade do Estado. 




Para o advogado Hédio Silva Júnior, fundador e coordenador executivo do Idafro, a inclusão do Oxê de Xangô entre os símbolos de Justiça do Supremo reafirma os preceitos constitucionais da promoção da igualdade racial e religiosa, do sancionamento cível e criminal da violência racial e religiosa, além da valorização da diversidade. 




“Lamentavelmente há um número significativo de aplicadores do Direito que tratam a censura constitucional ao racismo como ‘tutela de suscetibilidade, de melindres’, o tristemente famoso ‘mimimi’. Mas o racismo traumatiza, flagela, adoece e mata milhões de brasileiros e deve ser tratado exatamente como prevê a Constituição Federal”, ressalta Hédio Silva em entrevista à 

Agência Pública

.



















Hédio Silva Júnior afirma que Supremo reafirma o princípio constitucional da igualdade racial e religiosa ao receber o Oxê de Xangô







Símbolos de Justiça




Hédio Silva destaca que desde que deliberou a constitucionalidade das cotas raciais em 2012, o Supremo já havia rompido com a mística da justiça cega, comumente representada pelas deusas Iustitia, de origem romana, Diké e Astreia (gregas), cujas principais características são os olhos vendados e a presença de uma balança com os pratos equilibrados nas mãos. 




“O Oxê de Xangô atualiza e ressignifica não apenas a representação da Justiça, mas reafirma a imperiosa necessidade de que a administração da Justiça, a jurisdição, seja exercida com imparcialidade, equidistância e com base em fatos e provas. Não inspirada em pré-compreensões ou preferências raciais dos julgadores”, observa o advogado. 




Estado Laico e plural 




A chegada do Oxê de Xangô ao Salão Nobre do STF foi resultado de um percurso longo. Foram anos de um imbróglio jurídico em torno de símbolos religiosos, como crucifixos, expostos em instituições públicas, e o caráter laico do Estado.




Em 2009, o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) ajuizou uma ação civil pública solicitando a retirada de símbolos religiosos em prédios destinados ao atendimento público em São Paulo. O pedido foi rejeitado pela Justiça Federal que entendia à época que a laicidade do Estado não impedia a exposição de símbolos religiosos nos órgãos públicos porque eles refletiam a história regional e nacional. 




O pedido também foi negado em segunda instância no Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região, sob o mesmo argumento da Justiça Federal. O MPF recorreu das primeiras decisões e o debate chegou ao Supremo Tribunal em 2020.




Em novembro de 2024, por unanimidade, o Plenário da Corte acabou com a polêmica ao decidir pela manutenção dos símbolos religiosos em prédios públicos, considerando que a presença deles não contraria a laicidade do Estado, desde que o objetivo seja manifestar a tradição cultural da sociedade. 




O ministro Cristiano Zanin, relator do caso, liberou a presença de símbolos religiosos em prédios públicos pertencentes a qualquer um dos três poderes, da União, dos estados, do Distrito Federal e dos municípios.




Com o fim da controvérsia e a pacificação do entendimento pelo STF, o Idafro enxergou uma oportunidade e entrou com uma solicitação, em fevereiro de 2025, de instalação da escultura do Oxê de Xangô no edifício-sede da Corte. Em seus argumentos, o Instituto defendeu que a medida seria uma forma de ampliar a representatividade religiosa no local, já que no próprio salão onde o plenário do STF se reúne, atrás da cadeira do presidente, encontra-se um crucifixo com imagem de Jesus Cristo.

title: 25 novembre : Marche de nuit pour des vies libres et contre l'État sécuritaire !
content:
Le soir du 25 novembre, prenons la rue pour revendiquer des vies libres, et contre l'État sécuritaire

 

! Rendez-vous à 18h30 à Place des Fêtes (Paris 19

e

), à l'appel du 

CLAF




 

 

 

 




En tant que collectif révolutionnaire, nous pensons que le système police-justice-prison ne se réforme pas, mais qu'il faut l'abolir. Le féminisme punitiviste, institutionnel et putophobe promu par la loi intégrale soutenu par la Fondation des femmes ne nous sauvera pas.




La police ne nous protège pas. Nous ne croyons pas aux possibilités d'amélioration de la prise en charge pénale des 

VSS

 par des flics qui mutilent, violent et assassinent. Ce système garantit un ordre bourgeois, colonial, islamophobe et patriarcal. À travers sa police, l'État réprime, mutile et assassine celles et ceux qui se soulèvent et sont érigés en ennemis intérieurs.




Nous nous tenons aux côtés du mouvement social et lycéen actuel, et de toutes les victimes de violences policières. On se tient aussi aux côtés des mouvements réprimés parce qu'anti-coloniaux, comme ceux pour la libération de la Palestine. Révoltons-nous contre cet État qui réprime celleux qui se soulèvent. Soyons solidaires de nos camarades travailleureuses du sexe, en nous opposant aux lois qui précarisent et exposent à la violence.




Cette violence d'État permet celle des groupes d'extrême droite, qui commettent en toute impunité agressions et meurtres négrophobes, islamophobes et racistes. Elle permet aussi les revendications fémonationalistes pour des politiques anti-immigration et xénophobes.




Nous appelons à une auto-organisation et auto-défense féministe, antiraciste, antifasciste. Toutes dans la rue :




Tant qu'il le faudra, féministes, anti-carcérales et contre la police

 

!

author: Unknown
title: Assemblée générale de préparation à la manifestation du 28 novembre
content:
Rendez-vous le 26 novembre à 19h à la Parole Errante (9 rue François Debergue, Montreuil) pour une 

AG

 de préparation à la manifestation du 28 novembre. Contre les violences de genre, sociales, racistes, coloniales et d'État, poursuivons la mobilisation et faisons front contre les fémonationalistes, les fémosionistes, les racistes et les fascistes.




 

 

 

 

Pour une démonstration de force féministe, antiraciste, antisioniste et anticoloniale




Contre les violences de genre, sociales, racistes, coloniales et d'État, faisons du 28 novembre une grande mobilisation féministe

 

!




Depuis plusieurs années, le mouvement féministe connaît l'

intrusion répétée dans ses manifestations de collectifs fémonationalistes et fémosionistes

 comme 

Némésis et Nous Vivrons

, qui instrumentalisent la lutte contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles à des fins racistes, suprémacistes et coloniales.




Depuis le 8 mars 2025, un 

front féministe antiraciste, antisioniste et anitcolonial

 s'est constitué contre la présence de ces collectifs et n'a cessé de s'élargir. 

Le 8 mars 2026, nous avons réussi à les empêcher de défiler dans notre manifestation, par l'organisation collective, et dans la rue.




Cette année, la manifestation contre les violences de genre, sociales et d'État qui aura lieu le 28 novembre s'inscrit dans un contexte social particulier. 

Depuis septembre, la jeunesse des outre-mer et des quartiers populaires

, puis la majorité des lycées et des universités, 

se sont soulevés contre les injustices et pour de meilleures conditions d'éducation et de vie

. Les jeunes mobilisé-es font face à une répression brutale : des milliers de lycéen-nes et étudiant-es ont été interpellé-es, des centaines ont été poursuivi-es devant les tribunaux, mutilé-es et agressé-es sexuellement par une police sexiste, validiste, raciste et coloniale.




Féminicides, transféminicides, meurtres racistes, islamophobes et négrophobes, violences patriarcales, fascistes et policières :




Nous en avons assez de compter nos mort-es.




Le 23 octobre, Pengo Bossio Wangi a été tué dans un attentat raciste par un suprémaciste blanc, islamophobe et négrophobe qui a tiré sur des hommes, des femmes et des enfants, gravement blessé-es. La même semaine, Mauricio K. a été tué par la police au commissariat de Saint-Ouen.




Nous rappelons que 

la négrophobie, l'islamophobie et le racisme envers les personnes arabes et les Voyageur-ses sont le résultat d'un choix assumé de la classe politique de désigner les populations racisées, les personnes exilées, et celles issues des quartiers populaires comme «

 

ennemies de l'intérieur

 

»

.




Nous n'oublions pas que 

la normalisation des discours qui justifient le génocide en Palestine a servi l'agenda raciste et islamophobe du gouvernement

, la criminalisation de nos organisations politiques et de nos luttes.




Alors que certaines organisations féministes célèbrent l'adoption de la loi dite «

 

intégrale

 

», nous répétons que

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Baclaran vendors bear the cost of ASEAN Summit
content:
By Reachelyn Esona and Roselle Ochobillo

From bustling streets to empty sidewalks.

This may be an image of order for some, but for Baclaran street vendors, it can mean another day of uncertainty over whether they will have earnings to take home.

In the first week of November, the local government of Parañaque City ordered a clearing operation in barangay Baclaran in time for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nation (ASEAN) summit from November 15 to 17.

The Parañaque local government said that the barangay would temporarily prohibit street vendors along Roxas Boulevard, service roads, Redemptorist Road, Quirino Avenue, and beneath LRT-1 from November 2 to November 20, to clear the way for the arriving delegates.

Among those forced to leave their usual vending spots is Eduardo Bargas, 59, who’s been selling toys along Baclaran for almost 20 years to support his wife and only child. After being dislocated, he resorted to selling bottled water to earn a living despite the imposed clearing operation.

According to Bargas, they were informed about the operation as early as November 1. While larger vendors operating inside stall establishments were allowed to continue selling, ambulant vendors like him were temporarily ordered to stop their operations.

Bargas was nearly apprehended once by the authorities. Had he been caught, he said, his goods would have been confiscated. He begged the authorities not to take his items as it was all he had to live on.

Like other vendors, Bargas’s income was severely impacted by the clearing operation. He said he used to earn up to P1,000 (approximately US$ 15.63) a day before the policy was implemented. Now, he takes home only around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69).

The same concern was shared by a 50-year-old towel and sack bag vendor, Marlyn Merioles. She sells along Baclaran to sustain her elderly mother who is on maintenance medication, and her sibling who is a person with disability.

Before the clearing, Merioles was earning around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69) to P500 (approximately US$ 7.82) a day. Since the operation began, there were days she went home with empty pockets.

Merioles said she felt disheartened by the policy. Vendors, she said, are now anxious and find it difficult to sell their goods. They are constantly on their feet, keeping an eye out for patrols roaming the area. Merioles fears that she might not see them coming as her eyesight is already failing.

They were also warned that their goods would be confiscated if they were caught. Merioles said it would be a loss they could not afford because even a whole day of selling was not enough to recover the capital they had borrowed.

Merioles said it would help if the government would sustain their daily expenses. However, she said, only a few of the vendors benefitted from the financial assistance provided for the vendors.

While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) promised P10,000 (approximately $156.35) in cash assistance to vendors affected by the clearing operations in Baclaran, some vendors said they struggled to access the financial aid because it was reportedly limited to registered voters of Baclaran.

Rochelle Maale, who has been renting a stall in Baclaran for 10 years to sell ready-to-wear clothes, was among those who did not receive the assistance because she is not a registered voter in the area.

“The distribution of funds should be balanced… What about those who have been here for a long time but didn’t get anything?”Maale retorted.

Vendors argued that the assistance should be extended to everyone affected by the clearing operations, regardless of their place of residence, since they all experienced the impact of the clearing operations.

However, for many vendors, the issue goes beyond the limited eligibility for financial assistance.

They also questioned whether the P10,000 (approximately US$ 156.35) would be enough to sustain them after nearly 20 days of restricted operations.

Maale shared that the amount was insufficient to cover their daily expenses, especially amid rising costs of goods. “Will that P10,000 even last for a few days? No, it’s still not enough. That’s why vendors are struggling to make ends meet.”

She said some vendors have resorted to taking out loans to meet their everyday needs and restore their capital.

For vendors like Maale, the struggle extends beyond the clearing operations and financial assistance. What they need is a permanent and secure space where they can sell their merchandise, earn a living, and work without the constant fear of being arrested or displaced. (AMU, RVO)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Groups decry abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist in Davao City
content:
Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas answers questions from members of the media during a candle-lighting activity at Freedom Park in Davao City on the 2nd death anniversary of New Bataan 5 on February 24, 2024. Photo from Panalipdan Youth Davao’s Facebook page

Progressive groups condemned the alleged abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas in Davao City.

The Hands Off Mindanao Youth Activists (HOMYA) Network reported that around 10 to 12 individuals wearing all-black clothing and caps allegedly pursued the 24-year-old youth activist along Upper Madapo Hills, Barangay 8-A, on November 17 while he was on his way home.

“[They] tried to corner him and said, ‘This is him. Do not run’,” the network stated in its alert released on November 19.

Pangadas who belongs to the Indigenous Manobo reportedly was able to escape. He lost his phone and slippers and sustained injuries after he tripped and fell down during the pursuit which reportedly lasted for three hours.

The HOMYA network said that this incident reflects the continuing attacks and harassment faced by activists. “These acts of intimidation inflict serious mental, emotional, and psychological distress not only on Mawing, the direct target of these fascist attacks, but also on his family and loved ones who are forced to live under constant fear and anxiety.”

Read: Groups slam PNP official’s apology after tagging Mindanao activists as ‘wanted persons’

Lara Felescoso, spokesperson for Resist! Campaign, a human rights advocacy initiative, also considered the abduction attempt as an attack against Lumad youth and Indigenous community members who fight for their ancestral lands and fundamental rights.

Pangadas, who hails in Talaingod, Davao del Norte, was a former student of the Salugpongan Ta Tanu Igkanogon Community Learning Center, a now-defunct alternative school teaching Indigenous children in the Davao region. He was a relative of the late Manobo leader Bai Bibyaon Ligkayan Bigkay.

Fifty-five Salugpongan schools across the region were shut down in 2019 for allegedly violating Department of Education (DepEd) regulations and for training children to become members of the New People’s Army (NPA), an accusation that has been debunked by the school administration and human rights organizations.

Read: Groups urge gov’t to prioritize reopening of Lumad schools in Mindanao

During a protest in Davao City for the State of the Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in 2022, Pangadas and his older brother Ismael were arrested by the police and faced criminal charges for alleged human trafficking. They were acquitted from these cases.

Read: Court acquits Lumad brothers, 3 teachers from human trafficking charges

Pangadas serves as the education and research officer of the environmental advocacy group Panalipdan Youth Davao and convenor of HOMYA, a network that has been established due to continuing attacks and harassment against activists in Mindanao.

With such circumstances, the HOMYA network did not rule out the possibility that the alleged abduction attempt might be state-perpetrated, raising suspicion that it is linked to the government’s counterinsurgency operations.

Various progressive groups and youth-led organizations demanded an immediate and impartial investigation to identify the perpetrators and hold them accountable. (DAA)

author: Brian Hioe
title: Trilateral Meeting Between Xi, Trump, and Putin Results In Little Substance, But Taiwan Should Remain Cautious
content:
THE TRILATERAL SUMMIT between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping that was held earlier this week resulted in little of substance. Nevertheless, the summit should raise risks for Taiwan, seeing as Taiwan could stand to have its freedoms traded off through Trump’s unpredictable dealmaking.

Indeed, if the summit was intended to harken back to Yalta in the dealmaking that ended World War II, it did not have such significance. The three leaders came to an agreement about peace and nuclear disarmament, as well as boosting fuel production.

Ukraine came up indirectly, and even as Russian strikes on Ukraine continued during the meeting and its talk of peace, no agreement was made between the US and Russia on it. As reflected in the eventual readout, during the meeting, Trump lashed out at the International Criminal Court in what might be read as a conciliatory gesture to Putin, seeing as he is wanted by the court.

It may be fortunate for Taiwan, then–as with Ukraine–that it did not come up in the meeting. It is thought that the possibility of Trump taking some stance on Taiwan that would have signed away its freedoms to China was lessened by allegations against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that he was involved in an affair with a Chinese spy. It is probable that foreign policy hawks in the US leveraged on the scandal and framed the affair between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang as one involving Chinese spying in order to constrain Trump’s actions in the meeting.

It proves dangerous, however, for both Taiwan and Ukraine that Trump, Xi, and Putin would have a meeting without any Ukrainian or Taiwanese leaders present. And the presence of Xi is concerning for Taiwan, in that he apparently is seen by Trump as a stakeholder in what might otherwise be a bilateral meeting between Trump and Putin. Perhaps this goes to show how the Russian and Chinese governments have become increasingly intertwined in terms of joint interests, however.

Indeed, Xi and Putin are probably well aware of the Democratic wave that swept the US in recent midterm elections. Trump is now a lame duck, but he may still be intent on exercising power. Xi and Putin, then, could perhaps take advantage of an eagerness by Trump for quick wins in order to win concessions on Taiwan and Ukraine, much as Trump struck an oil deal with Putin to try and win a quick win in lowering oil prices in the US ahead of the vote. Consequently, it proves important for Taiwan, Ukraine, and other political actors to keep a close eye on moves by the three leaders to hold meetings–and to try and sink the possibility of deals that Trump may be willing to sign with Xi and Putin ahead of the actual meetings taking place, or in order to constrain his actions.

Domestically, however, one expects some of the usual suspects to actually take the rhetoric of peace by Trump, Xi, and Putin at face value. Insofar as the KMT has tried to sink closer ties between the US and Taiwan by claiming that this would lead Taiwan to suffer a fate like Ukraine, with a view of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine as caused by Ukraine getting too close to NATO, it is possible that the KMT would embrace the view that Taiwan, too, should seek a bargain with China, and that Trump could perhaps be convinced to back such a bargain. And it is also not impossible that Taiwan factors into the calculus of such leaders. Intrusions by Russian fighter jets into Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone, in an apparent first, earlier this week were likely timed ahead of the meeting as a means of projecting power. As it has been twice this week that Russian intrusions have occurred, it is to be seen if this is a new feature of regional security.

title: Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan: 589 milyon zarok li herêmên şer dijîn
content:
Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan (Save the Children) têkildarî zarokên li herêmên şer dijî raporek belav kiriye. Li gorî raporê zarok herî zêde di sala 2025an de li herêmên şer jiyaye ango rûbirûyê şer bûne.




Di heman demê de binpêkirinên wekî rêgirîkirina li gihîştina alîkariyên mirovî, revandin û tundkariya zayendî bi awayekî berbiçav zêde bûne.



















Li Afganistanê 3,7 milyon zarok bi xetereya birçîbûnê re rûbirû ne




5 Tebax 2026










Di rapora herî nû ya rêzeraporên bi navê "Şerê li Dijî Zarokan Rawestînin" de hat eşkerekirin ku sala 2025an li cîhanê 589 milyon zarok li herêmên şer jiyane.




Ev hejmar ji sala 1990î û vir ve ku tomarkirina amaran dest pê kiriye amara herî bilind e û ji du qat zêdetirî hejmara giştî ya nîvê salên 90î yên sedsala borî ye.



















Artêşa Îsraîlê di 20 rojên dawî de 490 zarok qetil kirin




7 Nîsan 2025










Birêvebirê Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan a Almanyayê Florian Westphal got:







"Ji bo bi milyonan zarokan tirs, tundî û koçberî bûne beşek ji jiyana wan a rojane." 







Westphal her wiha amaje pê kir ku divê ev amar ji bo civaka navneteweyî bibin"zengilekî hişyarkirinê."




Herêmên şer ên ku zarok lê dijîn




Li gorî raporê  sala 2025an li parzemîna Afrîkayê û li Rojhilata Navîn ji her 5 zarokan nêzîkî 2 zarok li herêmên şer jiyane.




Li cîhanê ji zarokên ku li herêmên şer dijîn jê ji sedî 44ê wan tenê li parzemîna Afrîkayê ye.




Rêjeya zarokên ku li wê parzemînê rûbirûyê şer dibin di 15 salên borî de ji 3 qatan zêdetir zêde bûye; sala 2010an ji sedî 12 bû lê sala 2025an derketiye ji sedî 39an.



















UNICEF: Ji Helebê 228 zarok gihîştin Rojava




16 Çile 2026










Li Rojhilata Navîn jî sala 2025an ji sedî 40,2yê zarokan li herêmên şer jiyane. Hejmara zarokên ku li herêmê di bin bandora şer de mane bi rêjeya nêzîkî ji sedî 29an zêde bûye; sala 2024an 52 milyon zarok bûn, sala 2025an derketiye 67 milyon zarokî.




Binpêkirinên metirsîdar




Li gorî raporê di sala 2025an 8 hezar û 322 bûyerên piştrastkirî yên rêgiriya li alîkariyên mirovî hatine tomarkirin ku li gorî dehsaleke berê 16 qat zêde bûye (sala 2015an tenê 509 bûyer û sala 2005an tenê 8 bûyer hatibûn tomarkirin).




Piraniya van bûyeran li Filistînê bi 5 hezar û 946 bûyeran hatine tomarkirin ku ev hejmar zêdetirî ji sedî 70yê hemû bûyerên tomarkirî yên cîhanê pêk tîne. Bi vî awayî, rêgirîkirina li alîkariyên mirovî piştî kuştin û kêmendamkirina zarokan bûyeduyem binpêkirina herî berbelav.



















2025: Zarokan di bianet kurdiyê de çawa cih girtiye?




31 Kanûn 2025










Komkirina binpêkirinan




Li gorî lêkolînê, Neteweyên Yekbûyî bi giştî 38 hezar û 967 binpêkirinên giran ên li dijî zarokan ên sala 2025an piştrast kirine ku piştî amara rekor a sala 2024an (41 hezar û 763 binpêkirin) duyem amara herî bilind a salane ye.




Zêdetirî nîvê van binpêkirinan tenê li 3 deveran qewimîne ku ew jî Filistîn, Komara Demokratîk a Kongoyê û Nîjerya ne.




Tenê li Filistînê 12 hezar û 449 binpêkirinên piştrastkirî hatine tomarkirin ku nêzîkîsêyeka hemû bûyerên li cîhanê ye.



















UNICEF: Li Xezeyê rojane 28 zarok dimirin




5 Tebax 2025










Amarên herî berbiçav ên binpêkirinên sala 2025an ev in:




Li gorî raporê, di şer de 14 hezar û 224 zarok hatine kuştin an kêmendam bûne. Di revandina zarokan de hejmareke rekor hatiye tomarkirin ku gihîştiye 5 hezar û 128bûyeran.




Hezar û 787 bûyerên tundiya zayendî hatine tomarkirin (di dehsaleke borî de bi rêjeya ji sedî 71 zêde bûye û ji sedî 86ê bûyeran li herêmên şer ên Afrîkayê, bi taybetî li Kongoû Sûdanê qewimîne).

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Lakbayan Southern Tagalog children finally released
content:
Released Lakbayani children. (Photo from Salinlahi Facebook page)

The children were denied their rights to counsel.

The 15 minors arrested in barangay Sucat, Muntinlupa City on November 15 have been released four days later (November 19).

This follows the order issued by the Muntinlupa City Office of the Prosecutor on November 18 for the release of all those arrested.

The minors aged 14 to 17 were part of the Lakbayan Southern Tagalog that started their march from the University of the Philippines Los Baños on November 12 to join the protest on the arrival of US President Donald Trump.

The 15 minors were the last to be released from being held in Bahay Pag-asa in Muntinlupa City. There were a total of 20 minors among the participants of Lakbayan Southern Tagalog, who were arrested on November 15 during the police’s violent dispersal in barangay Sucat.

The five minors aged 15 below were already released on November 17 as they were found to have no criminal liability.

The more than 200 adults who were part of the Lakbayan were earlier released on the night of November 18.

This contradicted the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) claim on November 18, that all 236 delegates of Southern Tagalog were released. The 15 minors were only released in the afternoon of November 19.

“Despite days of delaying tactics and bureaucratic processes that kept the minors detained for four days after illegal arrest and parents waiting in distress – returning everyday and waiting outside overnight – with the pressure of child rights advocates, lawyers, and church organizations, the children are now free,” Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns said.

“As we celebrate this collective victory, we also continue to demand for the immediate release of the nine illegally arrested and detained protesters at the Liwasang Bonifacio last November 15. One of them is a minor and currently remains at the Manila Youth Reception Center (MYRC),” the group said in their social media page.

According to Salinlahi, the children were denied their rights to counsel as the Bahay Pag-asa Head blocked the lawyers and paralegals from talking to them.

Salinlahi stressed that these children suffered police brutality and their longer detention only makes their violations of their rights extend much further.

“Bahay Pag-asa is mandated to protect and rehabilitate children—not become an instrument for prolonging their detention and suppressing their rights,” Salinlahi said in a statement.

For the National Union of People’s Lawyer (NUPL) the Philippine National Police (PNP) must be held accountable for their brutality against activists who are only exercising their right to protest. “These findings expose the fundamental weakness of the PNP’s case. Having arrested and charged hundreds of individuals in one sweeping operation, the police could not even sufficiently distinguish the alleged acts of one respondent from another.”

Meanwhile, three students of the University of Makati (UMak) were also released on November 19.

The Taguig City Prosecutor’s Office dismissed the cases that were filed against the students. These are alarm and scandal under Article 155 of the Revised Penal Code and resistance and disobedience to an agent of a person in authority under Article 151 of the same code.

The Taguig City Prosecutor’s Office said in its resolution, “The evidence on record shows that the actions of (three students), were made specifically to voice out certain political and social grievances and not the purpose of causing general disturbance or public disorder.”

Lawyer Jose Topacio of the Alliance of Nationalist and Genuine Labor Organizations-Kilusang Mayo Uno (ANGLO-KMU) meanwhile pointed out that the three students were released only after six days of continuous confinement at the Taguig City Police Station, way past the time periods prescribed by Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code.

“We are also alarmed at the brazen displays of intimidation by the police, where the detainees were repeatedly told that the police intended to hold them for six days, that detailed files about them were being compiled since the Grand Hyatt protest on 10 September, and that their arrest should serve as a ‘lesson’ to them,” Topacio told Bulatlat in a message.

Topacio also noted how Taguig City police shouted at the visiting relatives of the students and repeatedly asked to move away from the station to other parts of the Taguig City Hall complex while conferring with counsel.

“Nevertheless, we are grateful for their release and would like to thank their counsels during the inquest, Attys. Krizza Hedriana and Ana Perez from the University of Makati for rendering timely aid in the morning,” said Topacio who was part of the quick reaction team on November 13.

Progressive groups continue to call for the release of the remaining nine individuals under the custody of the Manila Police District (including one minor remaining in MYRC).

According to the Alliance of Concerned Teachers-Philippines, their inquest proceedings concluded on November 16.

“Three days have passed, yet there is still no resolution. The prosecutor is currently delaying the signing of their resolution. This harassment has no legal basis, and they must be released immediately. The abusive police officers must be held accountable for their violence against ordinary citizens,” the group said. One of their volunteers was among those who were arrested.

Progressive groups said that what happened on November 15 was the biggest mass arrest in a single day under the Marcos Jr. administration. (with reports from Anne Marxze D. Umil) (DAA)

author: Jim McIlroy
title: Activist Stephen Langford released after week in Silverwater
content:
Stephen Langford, long-time solidarity activist and member of Socialist Alliance, was released from Silverwater Correctional Complex on November 19 following a week-long stint after being arrested at a regular protest outside the former office of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Marrickville.

Rachel Evans, Socialist Alliance candidate for Heffron, told a rally outside Newtown Court on the day of his release that Langford was targeted because he is a committed activist.

“The police came straight up to him at the protest action he takes every week… They said ‘You are under arrest’ but did not clarify what he was charged with,” she said.

“Stephen did not resist arrest, and was taken to Surry Hills police station, and then to Silverwater. He was only offered one phone call … and we were told Stephen would be held for between one to three weeks, and that we could not visit or video link him. They said he could only call us and refused to allow us to leave messages.

“We condemn all levels of police and corrective services for treating him this way. Stephen is a non-violent, peace and anti-war activist, who worked tirelessly to free East Timor, and was later granted an Order of Timor.”

Langford has previously been arrested for breaching bail conditions after pasting an 1816 quote by former NSW Governor Lachlan Macquarie on his statue in Hyde Park. Macquarie said: “All Aborigines from Sydney onwards are to be made prisoners of war and if they resist they are to be shot and their bodies hung from trees in the most conspicuous places near where they fall so as to strike fear into the hearts of surviving natives.”

Macquarie said this before the infamous Appin Massacre on April 17, 1816, in which at least 14 Aboriginal men, women, and children were killed — shot or driven over cliffs — and several others captured, imprisoned and tortured by colonial troops.

Langford's peaceful protest is intended to be an act of truth-telling, revealing the brutality of the colonial government towards First Nations people.

NSW Police imposed strict bail conditions on Langford, including including restricting his movement in a section of Marrickville, where his recent protests have taken place.

“Stephen is kind and generous. He is a retired nurse and feels injustice to others deeply. He would not hurt a fly, and has spent 30 years fighting to win freedom for oppressed peoples all over the world,” Evans said.

“Political graffiti should not be a jailable offence. Stephen should be given an apology and compensation for the way he's been treated.”

Langford is due to appear in court on January 21.

author: Esperanza
title: Danzar con la cámara: “A 26 pixeles de distancia” llega al 7º FestivalPICNIC de Valdivia
content:
Hacer de la boca una escena expandida por la medialidad es uno de los imaginarios posibles de Tecnocorporeidades, proyecto de creación artística liderado por Nirvana Sepúlveda y Loreto García, quienes trabajan la relación cuerpo-tecnología combinando danza contemporánea, performance y proyección en tiempo real. “No es nuestro propósito instalar un mensaje de cómo nos relacionamos con la tecnología, sino más bien provocar en torno a esta relación”.




Por Morín Ortiz.




Un proyector, una pantalla, un notebook, tres cámaras web, un micrófono, un foco led, dos aros de luz y tres cuerpos que producen movimientos y voces expandidas, componen el universo de “A 26 pixeles de distancia”. Obra de danza contemporánea de Tecnocorporeidades que, en 40 minutos, “produce ciberespacios eróticos, lúgubres y lúdicos, donde el cuerpo físico se disuelve en un cuerpo digitalizado que desborda los límites de lo real”, dice la sinopsis de esta obra para mayores de 18 años. 




Dirigida por Nirvana Sepúlveda y Loreto García, quienes se conocieron en el Centro de Danza Espiral para luego seguir su formación en danza en la Academia de Humanismo Cristiano, en Santiago. Desde entonces, se sintieron atraídas. Por el afán de investigar de Loreto García, quien además es socióloga, y por la desinhibida creatividad de Nirvana Sepúlveda, quien danza desde pequeña y practica burlesque. Entonces comenzaron a crear en contextos sociales marcados por las tomas feministas, la revuelta social chilena y la pandemia. Hoy la tecnología media la mayor parte del tiempo esta relación creativa y afectiva, porque Loreto vive en Temuco y Nirvana en Barcelona.



















Pero el nacimiento de esta experimentación escénica tuvo lugar en Casa Varas de Temuco el año 2021, y luego en el centro cultural Ceina de Santiago, donde las investigaciones en torno a la proyección de danza en tiempo real devinieron en una performance, que hoy se convirtió en la primera de tres escenas que componen la obra. Recuerdan que por estos años las habitaban reflexiones pandémicas del cómo hacer contacto e insistir en el encuentro pese a las pantallas. “La danza, que piensa el cuerpo, tiene que pensar en este cuerpo que ya no es solo físico, sino que está expandido en múltiples redes imaginarias y virtuales”, señala Nirvana.




El nombre de “A 26 pixeles de distancia” es una cita del texto “Realidad virtual” del libro “Enciclopedia del amor en los tiempos de porno” (Editorial Cuarto Propio, 2014) de Lucía Egaña Rojas y Josefa Ruiz-Tagle. Esta y las oraciones finales “No soy real. Ya no me queda nada de humanidad, solo el deseo”, hicieron eco en Tecnocorporeidades por propiciar una visión expandida del cuerpo. 







“Desarrollamos interacciones del cuerpo con la imagen desde una propuesta 

cyborg

, que entiende el cuerpo como una figura híbrida que desdibuja los límites entre lo humano y lo más que humano y crea alianzas políticas basadas en el deseo por lo otro», comparte Loreto.







Más que una búsqueda discursiva, este trabajo escénico explora las operaciones técnicas mediante las cuales “producimos afectos y efectos con la tecnología. Un lugar experimental a partir de la relación cotidiana que tenemos con ella”. Proceso que les llevó a pensar “en el binarismo como mecanismos de producción de subjetividades y desde ese lugar, el proyecto Tecnocorporeidades nos permite construir otros imaginarios en torno a la sexualidad, al género, a las posibilidades que tiene un cuerpo”.




El equipo de “A 26 pixeles de distancia” lo componen Nirvana Sepúlveda y Loreto García en la dirección e interpretación, Yoko Pérez y Tiwa Labastida también como intérpretes, Nicolette Michael en diseño integral e iluminación, Samuel Martínez en asistencia técnica e iluminación, Carlos Contreras como realizador audiovisual y fotógrafo, Álvaro Núñez en composición musical, Matías Vergara en operación técnica, Lukas Julio en producción y Morín Ortiz en comunicaciones.




Con casi una decena de presentaciones autogestionadas en Santiago, Temuco y Collipulli




Tecnocorporeidades está en pleno desarrollo de un proyecto de Circulación Nacional financiado por el Fondo Nacional de Fomento y Desarrollo de las Artes Escénicas, convocatoria 2026. Con el que se presentaron en el Festival LOFT de Concepción y les tendrá en el Festival PICNIC de Valdivia y en la Carpa Trashumantes en Temuco.




Con un espacio de formación y una exhibición, llegarán hasta el 7º Festival PICNIC del Centro Cultural Bailarines de los Ríos, el jueves 19 de noviembre, de 12:00 a 15:00 horas para realizar el Laboratorio Tecnocorporeidades. Una exploración entre la danza y las tecnologías de la imagen, a través de la improvisación y la composición en tiempo real, a cargo de Loreto García y Lukas Julio. La inscripción es gratuita mediante un 

formulario en línea

 que se encuentra en los Instagram de bailarinesdelosrios y  tecnocorporeidades.




La obra “A 26 pixeles de distancia” se presentará el viernes 20 de noviembre a las 19:30 horas. Entrada a mil pesos. Ambas instancias tendrán lugar en el espacio de este centro cultural ubicado en Barrios Bajos, pasaje San Luis #1157, Valdivia, Chile.







Esta información se publicó en 

Radio Kurruf

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Freed Southern Tagalog activists to file counter charges vs police
content:
Photo by Kyle Justin Macabalitao/Bulatlat

This is the spirit of the released delegates of the Lakabayan Southern Tagalog who were violently arrested and detained by the police last November 15 in barangay Sucat, Muntinlupa City. In a press conference on November 19, they announced that they will file counter charges against the officers of the Southern Police District (SPD).

National Union of People’s Lawyers (NUPL) President Ephraim Cortez said the arrest of more than 200 activists and 18 journalists can be considered illegal. Cortez maintained that the police violated the provisions of the Batasang Pambansa Blg. 880 for obstructing or disrupting a peaceful assembly, Article 124 of the Revised Penal Code for arbitrary detention, and Republic Act No. 7438 for the right to counsel.

“The police have already violated their own guidelines and the rights of their arrestees on how they should have been treated during the arrest, not to mention the injuries that they sustained,” said Cortez.

Niezelle Visaya, spokesperson of the Lakbayan Timog Katagalugan, recalled how hundreds of police personnel from the SPD intimidated and harassed the delegates of Lakbayan, from morning until 2 p.m. of November 15 while they were holding a program at Sucat People’s Park.

Visaya said that at around 2:00 a.m. of November 15, hundreds of police from the SPD went to the Sucat People’s Park, intimidating the delegates who were there to rest. The police also started to block the entry and exit points of the delegates.

“They began violently arresting the organizers. Some of us were brought up to the Barangay Police Headquarters, where we were placed in small rooms that don’t have proper ventilation. They continued to bring mothers, Indigenous People, and even children into these rooms,” Viasaya said.

Community journalist Marky Casquite from the Southern Tagalog Exposure also recalled how he was arrested by the police despite his assertion that he is a member of the media.

“I was suddenly picked up and arrested by the police despite showing my media ID,” Casquite said.

“They handcuffed me. They were not even content with that, they also dragged me to the barangay hall leaving me with injuries to my arm from the tightly fastened handcuffs and to my knee from being dragged,” Casquite said, adding that he did not receive first aid even though he was already bleeding.

Lucky Oraller of the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan – Timog Katagalugan (BAYAN-TK) demanded that charges against them and others who were arrested should be junked.

“While Marcos welcomed Trump through the red carpet, his forces dragged, caught, and arrested the ordinary Filipino just to welcome Trump for the ASEAN Summit,” said Oraller.

Oraller also decried how their cellphones and other protest paraphernalia were confiscated, including the vehicle and effigy.

While it was confirmed that the phones were returned to the delegates, the placards, streamer, effigy, and the vehicle along with the bags inside have not been returned, Oraller said.

“We’re not sure what the police could do to our vehicles and bags that are still in Camp Bagong Diwa. [W]e call to the people to monitor the case, as there are threats that they would plant evidence to frame us up,” said Oraller.

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Filipino migrant healthcare workers denounce ICE detention, deportation threats
content:
Image of packaged sent to Balllesteros (photo from CLSU USSC)

Filipino migrant healthcare workers condemned the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown while raising concerns over medical neglect inside US detention facilities.

Speaking at a press conference organized by Tanggol Migrante Movement USA on November 13, two Filipino healthcare workers called for humane treatment and due process for migrants, regardless of their immigration status or profession.

Mariae “LC” Nacu was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Phoenix, Arizona, on August 22.

The 22-year-old registered nurse had been working at St. Joseph’s Hospital in Phoenix and has a valid employment authorization.

She was held at the Eloy Detention Center for three weeks before her release on bond, according to Tanggol Migrante Movement USA.

The organization said that her bond was set at $17,000 (P1.08 million) on November 13.

Nacu also estimated that she spent around $300 weekly (P19,068) on commissary items and phone calls while detained.

More than two months after her detention, ICE continued to hold her identification documents, including her driver’s license, according to the organization.

“The difficult part was that I wasn’t there [in the detention center] as a nurse. I was another person in detention, locked in a cell, trying to get someone to listen,” Nacu said.

She recalled witnessing a medical emergency involving another detainee and struggling to get someone to listen to her concerns.

Nacu described the separation from loved ones, handcuffing, and transfers between detention facilities without knowing where she was going as “traumatizing and dehumanizing.”

Dr. Veronica Velasquez, a Filipino physical therapist and recipient of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), faces the threat of being deported.

Co-chair of the Los Angeles Kalusugan Collective, Velasquez regularly visits detainees at the Adelanto Detention Center where she witnessed brutality and medical neglect.

Velasquez said that she has organized with Tanggol Migrante Movement USA for two years and continues to support detained migrants despite facing immigration-related uncertainty herself. “I am a healthcare worker who has seen firsthand the brutality inside detention centers. I, myself, am threatened with deportation and have experienced over 23 years of this immigrant injustice system. Even so, I’m here still fighting for my community while the community fights for me.”

She said that nearly 100 community members attended her first court hearing.

Both healthcare workers raised concerns about the treatment of migrants inside US detention facilities, particularly their access to medical attention.

Velasquez said that her experience in visiting detainees exposed her to cases of alleged brutality and medical neglect. “As healthcare workers, we are in a special position to shed light on these issues of migrants in detention […] You cannot deny us from saying that there is medical violence happening in these detention centers.”

Nacu’s account of witnessing another detainee’s medical emergency also underscored the difficulties people in detention face when seeking help.

Her testimony, however, does not independently establish the circumstances or outcome of the medical emergency.

Bulatlat previously reported the case of a Filipino detainee, Kuya G, who underwent a toe amputation after months of alleged medical neglect at the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, Washington.

Migrant rights advocates said that detention facility personnel failed to properly diagnose and address his condition.

The case adds to concerns raised by migrant organizations about the treatment and medical care available to people held in immigration detention.

Read: Filipino migrants face inhumane treatment at ICE detention centers

Velasquez raised concerns over the slow response and lack of accountability of Philippine consulates who are supposed to be assisting detained migrants. She cited one case where a consulate called the police on mothers of detainees who were seeking assistance.

Her remarks echo concerns raised by Filipino migrant organizations about the Philippine government’s response to the detention of Filipino nationals in the United States.

Nacu said that access to humane treatment, medical care, and due process should not depend on a person’s profession or immigration status. “We shouldn’t have to be nurses, doctors, or healthcare workers to deserve dignity. Every person deserves humane treatment, necessary medical care, and due process, regardless of their profession or immigration status.”

The two healthcare workers called for solidarity with migrants facing detention and deportation threats. “In nursing, when someone needs help, we don’t expect one person to handle everything alone. We communicate, support each other, and work as a team. I hope we can bring that same commitment to the people and communities affected by immigration detention,” Nacu said. (RTS, DAA)
