Aakaluk Adrienne BlatchfordInupiaq and Yup’ik activist from Unalakleet, Alaska, who is a geoengineering outreach organizer with the Indigenous Environmental Network.

Indigenous Environmental Network

Democrat Mary Peltola was declared the winner this week of Alaska’s closely watched race for U.S. Senate, making her the first Alaska Native lawmaker elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, we speak with Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford, an Inupiaq and Yup’ik organizer from Unalakleet, Alaska. She says Peltola’s win is a significant milestone for Indigenous peoples in Alaska.

“Having somebody represent us in such a large capacity with such a big weight on her shoulders, but still carrying that struggle with her as she continues to advocate for our people and our way of life, is monumental,” says Blatchford.

Aakaluk Adrienne BlatchfordInupiaq and Yup’ik activist from Unalakleet, Alaska, who is a geoengineering outreach organizer with the Indigenous Environmental Network.

Indigenous Environmental Network

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. We’re broadcasting from the U.N. climate summit, known as COP31. I’m Amy Goodman, with Nermeen Shaikh.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: In Alaska, voters have just elected Congresswoman Mary Peltola as the next senator from Alaska, bringing the incoming Democratic majority to 56 seats. Peltola is Yup’ik Alaskan and will be the first Indigenous woman from Alaska elected to the U.S. Senate. This is Mary Peltola thanking supporters on Tuesday.

SEN.-ELECT MARY PELTOLA: Alaskans have voted for change, and I’m so honored to be your next U.S. senator. Together, we’re going to put an end to the era of self-serving politicians lining their own pockets at your expense. And together, we’re going to put Alaska first. I’ll work relentlessly to serve the interests of Alaska, and I’ll be guided by your voices every step of the way.

AMY GOODMAN: Mary Peltola campaigned in many difficult situations and places to reach communities across Alaska that are often overlooked in elections. One in five Alaska voters are Indigenous.

Well, we’re here at the U.N. climate conference in Antalya, Turkey. The Arctic is warming faster than anywhere else on the planet, and shifts in sea ice and temperatures in the Arctic influence weather patterns globally. This has led some researchers in the Arctic to begin experimenting with marine geoengineering.

We’re joined right now by an Inupiaq and Yup’ik organizer from Unalakleet, Alaska. Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford is a geoengineering outreach organizer with the Indigenous Environmental Network, joining us here.

We welcome you to Democracy Now! You have tears in your eyes, Aakaluk. And I wanted to ask you, before we talk about what’s happening here at the summit — the second draft has just been released of the final document. But I wanted to ask you about this huge news this week in the United States: The first Native Alaskan is elected to the U.S. Senate, Mary Peltola. People have heard about her, but not in that way. You are weeping.

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: Yeah. To hear that out loud, it was heartfelt, knowing that somebody that has been born into our communities, that’s been raised alongside us, that faced these struggles, you know, in our motherlands, the place that remembers our bones — the reality of that, having somebody represent us in such a large capacity with such a big weight on her shoulders, but still carrying that struggle with her as she, you know, continues to advocate for our people and our way of life, is monumental.

AMY GOODMAN: How large is the Indigenous community in Alaska? You know, I think of the only — I think of another famous Alaskan, the woman who ran for vice president — right? — under John McCain, Sarah Palin. We’re about to talk about Russia and an imprisoned Indigenous activist there. But Sarah Palin famously said, “You can see Russia from here.” But now Mary Peltola is making history in a very different way. What does she represent? And when it comes to the U.N. climate summit, are you confident that she stands where you do on the elimination, for example, of fossil fuels, something Alaska is very dependent on?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: You know, there’s a lot of different layers to politics in Alaska, but we’re going to hold her feet to the fire when it comes to divestment from this fossil fuel industry, and the introduction of false solutions in Alaska that follow alongside that, that destruction of Mother Earth. And when it comes to having a Yup’ik representative, a woman, in that office, you know, it really resonates with us as Indigenous people, because they’re our matriarchs. They’re the people that hold that responsibility to defend the sacred when it comes to our lands and our waters and our resources. So, I have confidence in Mary and in what she’s going to bring.

AMY GOODMAN: Do you know her personally?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: I’ve met her. I don’t know her personally, though, no.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: And could you talk about the climate impacts in Alaska already, the devastating decline — there are reports of this — of the catch of Chinook salmon, and how central that is to Alaska’s both economy, but also it is the food of the Indigenous peoples that have been there for centuries?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: Like water, salmon brings us life. It’s something that is a — you know, a deep part of our culture, our cultural survival, our food security, our sovereignty. When we talk about the salmon and the waters that carry them, we also talk about ourselves, because we have a deep relationship with the land and what it provides. And without that salmon, you know, our people are threatened to no longer be in those lands.

AMY GOODMAN: And the Arctic melting faster than anywhere on Earth, and you are wearing, with your necklaces, a little sign that says “Decolonize Climate Policy.” What does that mean?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: We have the answers as Indigenous people. We know that with our way of life and our traditions carried on into these spaces, that decolonizing this space and implementing what we know, our traditional ecological knowledge, our value systems, into these policy spaces is what’s going to move forward to help bring regenerative economies and a just transition that’s equitable and that’s going to give opportunities for Indigenous peoples to not only live in our lands, but thrive in our lands.

AMY GOODMAN: And geoengineering, what you’re most concerned about when it comes to the issue of geoengineering and experiments in Alaska?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: You know, when we look at geoengineering, it’s a false solution, and it only perpetuates what we’re seeing when it comes to the dependence on this fossil fuel industry. And we need real climate solutions, not technology for climate mitigation. There’s a lot to be said when these projects are funded and operated by these industries that are bringing forward destruction to Mother Earth.

AMY GOODMAN: We want to thank you so much, Aakaluk, for joining us. We have seen you out there protesting, being part of news conferences, holding up signs. We’re here at the U.N. climate summit. This is Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford with the Indigenous Environmental Network. She is Inupiaq and Yup’ik from Unalakleet. And why don’t you say it yourself, so I say it right?

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: You got it. You got it down. Unalakleet, Alaska. Unalakleet.

AMY GOODMAN: Unalakleet, Alaska.

AAKALUK ADRIENNE BLATCHFORD: Yeah.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. In a moment, we’ll be joined by an Indigenous activist from Russia. But first, let’s go to Joan Carling, an Indigenous leader from the Philippines. She spoke earlier today here at the U.N. climate summit.

JOAN CARLING: I’m Joan Carling from — a Filipino activist. And as my colleague has mentioned, Trump was in the Philippines to take control of our minerals and our land for data centers. And there’s a big demonstration that happened, and more than a hundred were arrested. And they are now calling for solidarity. They are calling for global solidarity, because we cannot allow this to continue. When we speak of respecting Indigenous peoples’ rights, that means we don’t want land-grabbing for just transition. We don’t want the polluting of our rivers. We don’t want the destruction of our livelihoods. That’s what we are talking about here. We also want companies to be accountable for the harms that they are doing to our communities. For mining companies, enough is enough. We have already suffered, and we cannot continue to be sacrificed again and again in the name of just transition, in the name of climate action.

AMY GOODMAN: Joan Carling, Indigenous leader from the Philippines, speaking earlier today at the U.N. climate summit.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Nunavut Arctic College to offer its own teaching degree
content:
Nunavut Arctic College is expected to offer its own credited bachelor of education program next fall.




“We have the skills, we have the knowledge, we have the administrative mechanisms to support the program,” said president Jackie Price in an interview. “So it’s time.”




The college’s current equivalent is offered in partnership with Memorial University in Newfoundland and Labrador, through a program that allows students to complete their studies remotely from Nunavut. Prior versions of the program included the University of Regina and McGill University in Montreal.




Due to funding restraints, the college will offer the new program in Iqaluit and up to four other communities to start, though its administration is still assessing which ones, Price said.




In 2021, the college received more than $34 million for its education program, through a five-year agreement between Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. and the territorial and federal governments.




That money allowed the program to expand to 21 communities through remote learning, Price said. But the funding has run out.




The news comes at a time when the Government of Nunavut is hiring more unqualified teachers, who don’t have formal training as teachers.
















The number of teachers approved to work in the territory without a bachelor of education or equivalent degree nearly doubled since 2021, from 54 to 93 this school year, figures shared by the Education Department indicate.




“That’s over 10 per cent of our membership right now that’s unqualified. We would not accept 10 per cent of our nurses to be unqualified,” Nunavut Teachers’ Association president Justin Matchett said in an interview.




He said he hopes the new program will change that.




“We need to strive for quality education for everybody here,” Matchett said.




Education Minister David Akeeagok said in a written statement the number of unqualified teachers in Nunavut concerns him.




While only those with bachelor of education degrees would, ideally, staff classrooms, he said that unqualified teachers receive training and have other meaningful qualifications, such as Inuktitut proficiency.
















“Nunavut faces longstanding and well-known challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified teachers, exacerbated by the shortage of teachers across Canada,” he said.

title: "This Is Not Going Well": COP31 Draft Text Avoids Fossil Fuel Phaseout, Bets on "Magic Technologies"
content:
As we continue our week of broadcasts from the global United Nations climate conference known as COP31, we get an update on the formal negotiations from German activist Luisa Neubauer. The 

latest draft text

 of the key climate commitments that countries are debating has dropped language about phasing out fossil fuels, but it does include an emphasis on carbon capture and storage — a largely unproven technology that critics say cannot be deployed at scale to curb emissions.




“We have much better solutions at hand, like renewables,” says Neubauer. “This is not going well. We are not doing fine. And if anything, after this conference ends, we need people to take the streets and fight for more justice out there.”

title: Auch in der Schweiz: Jugendstreik gegen Austerität und Aufrüstung
content:
„

Am 20. November streiken Jugendliche in ganz Europa unter dem Slogan «Fight for our future, not their wars!» gegen Austerität und Aufrüstung. In der Schweiz bildet sich dafür ein breites Bündnis, das zum Anschluss an die internationale Mobilisierung aufruft. (…) „Wir gehen auf die Strasse, weil unsere Zukunft auf dem Spiel steht. Wir fragen uns, ob wir uns unsere Ausbildung noch leisten können, ob wir nach dem Abschluss einen Job finden und von unserem Lohn leben können. Statt zukunftsfähige Perspektiven zu schaffen, spart die Politik ausgerechnet bei Bildung und sozialer Sicherheit, das ist einfach unverständlich!“, meint Jael Seiler, Kauffrau in Ausbildung aus Bern. „An unseren Universitäten lernen und forschen wir für die Zukunft. Es ist absurd, wenn unser Wissen dazu dient, ein marodes System aufrechtzuerhalten und tödliches Kriegsmaterial weiterzuentwickeln, statt nachhaltige Gesellschaftsvisionen zu entwerfen

…“ 

Aus dem Aufruf des Schweizer Jugendstreikbündnisses

 

 zum Jugendstreik am 20. November – siehe weitere Informationen:







Nationaler Jugendstreik: Die Jugend steht auf – Gewerkschaften stehen hinter ihr




„

Für Bildung, Kaufkraft und Klimaschutz, gegen Sparpolitik, Aufrüstung und Lohndruck. Dafür gehen am Freitag in der ganzen Schweiz Jugendliche auf die Strasse. Der Schweizerische Gewerkschaftsbund (SGB) unterstützt den Jungendstreik und ruft seine Verbände auf, mitzumobilisieren.




Mehr als 176’000 Menschen unterschrieben im Sommer 2025 den Aufruf für acht Wochen Ferien in der Lehre. Anfang November lehnte die Bildungskommission des Ständerats selbst eine Erhöhung auf sechs Wochen ab. Für die Jugendkommission des SGB zeigt der Entscheid einmal mehr, wie viel Druck es braucht, damit die Anliegen der Jungen in der Politik überhaupt Gehör finden. Auf ihren Antrag hat der SGB-Kongress am 13. und 14. November eine Solidaritätsresolution zum Jugendstreik beschlossen.




Mehr Geld für Bildung




«Fight for our future, not their wars!» lautet das Motto des nationalen Jugend- und Studierendenstreiks. Die Streikenden kritisieren, dass Milliarden in die Armee fliessen, während bei Angeboten gespart wird, auf die sie angewiesen sind. Sie verlangen mehr Geld für Schulen und Berufsbildung, für das Gesundheitswesen und den Service public, für Klimaschutz und soziale Sicherheit

…“ 

Artikel von Clemens Studer vom 18. November 2026 in work

 

 – Zeitung der unia







Siehe die 

Solidaritätsresolution des SGB

 

 










[Schweiz] Vor dem grossen Streiktag : Generation Kipppunkt 


„

Kommende Woche schliessen sich Schüler:innen aus der ganzen Schweiz einem internationalen Jugendstreik an. Was bewegt sie? (…) 

Zum Vernetzungstreffen eingeladen hat das lokale Streikbündnis, zu dem eine ganze Reihe linker Gruppen und Jungparteien gehört – vom feministischen Hochschulkollektiv über die Jungen Grünen bis zur Kommunistischen Jugend. Dennoch ist es vor allem die Juso, die medial in Erscheinung tritt; sie war es auch, die im Sommer auf nationaler Ebene entschied, sich dem internationalen Aufruf zu einem «Youth Strike» in ganz Europa anzuschliessen. Seither wurden Aktionen von Genf bis St. Gallen und von Basel bis ins Tessin angekündigt.




Etwa Anfang September hätten sie mit der konkreten Planung begonnen, sagen David Rietzler und Jael Seiler von der Berner Juso, die das Treffen leiten. Mitte September hat der bevorstehende Streiktag aber neue Vorzeichen bekommen. Damals nämlich ging es los mit den grossen Protesten in Frankreich, angestossen von Schüler:innen, die gegen den Verfall ihrer Bildungseinrichtungen mobilisierten, und bald kam es auch in weiteren Ländern zu riesigen Demos. Mittlerweile sind für den 20. November Jugendstreiks praktisch überall in Europa angekündigt, ständig tauchen auf Social Media neue Accounts mit neuen Aufrufen auf, mancherorts gefilmt inmitten des Protestgetümmels der letzten Wochen.




Das wirkt sich auch auf die Dynamik in der Schweiz aus. «Ich spüre in meiner Generation dieselbe Wut aufs System», sagt Rietzler, «auch wenn es hierzulande vielleicht nicht um marode Schulen geht, sondern etwa ums Entlastungspaket 27.» Ganz offensichtlich, findet er, kümmere sich die hiesige Politik viel lieber um hypothetische militärische Bedrohungsszenarien als um ganz reale Sicherheitsbedürfnisse junger Menschen. «Gelder für Klimaschutz, für soziale Sicherheit sowie zum Beispiel für die Prävention gegen Gewalt an Frauen werden einfach gestrichen», sagt Seiler. Dass die Gen Z in der Schweiz zu privilegiert sei, um für ihre Anliegen zu kämpfen, glauben die beiden nicht. Auch hierzulande gebe es sehr viel Armut. «Und ich sehe es ja bei mir selbst», sagt Seiler. «Ich weiss noch nicht, ob ich mein Leben nach der KV-Lehre selbstständig finanzieren und vielleicht noch eine Berufsmatur machen kann.»




Fragt man die übrigen streikwilligen Schüler:innen nach ihren Beweggründen, so nennen sie als Erstes stets die beängstigenden Klimaaussichten, mit denen ihre Generation aufwächst

…“ 

Artikel von Raphael Albisser in der WoZ vom 12. November 2026

 




Jung, politisch, unzufrieden – Europas Jugend rebelliert




„

Seit Wochen gehen junge Menschen in Europa auf die Strasse – erfasst die Protestbewegung jetzt auch die Schweiz? (…) 

«In unserer Generation gibt es eine riesige Unzufriedenheit mit den aktuellen Lebensumständen», sagt Rietzler. Er kritisiert: «Die Politik geht die Probleme nicht an, sondern investiert immer mehr in Militär und Aufrüstung.» Und spare dafür beim Klimaschutz oder bei der Bildung.




Kritik am Entlastungspaket 2027




Konkret kritisiert er das Entlastungspaket 2027 des Bundes, mit dem in verschiedenen Bereichen gespart wird. «Es geht um unsere Zukunft. Darum gehen wir am 20. November auf die Strasse.»




In verschiedenen Schweizer Städten gibt es Komitees für den Jugendstreik. Es gibt Vernetzungstreffen an Schulen und Universitäten, sie malen Transparente und organisieren Podiumsdiskussionen. Der Jugendstreik wird international durchgeführt und ist bereits seit Sommer geplant. (…)


Die Organisatoren in der Schweiz solidarisieren sich mit den Protesten im Ausland. Die Themen seien die gleichen, es gehe um die Zukunft: Klimaschutz, Bildung, Gesundheitskosten, hohe Mieten, Angst vor Arbeitslosigkeit. (…)




Es droht Gewalt von Linksextremen




Ende Oktober kam es auch in Zürich und Basel zu 

Gewalt bei unbewilligten Demonstrationen

 

. Linksextreme Gruppen hatten zu diesen aufgerufen. Kommt es nun auch beim Jugendstreik zu Gewalt? Online rufen linksextreme Gruppen bereits mit expliziten Videos auf.




Die Organisatoren des Jugendstreiks betonen, dass sie zu einer friedlichen Demo aufrufen. «Wir möchten, dass nicht nur eine mögliche Eskalation thematisiert wird, sondern die realen Forderungen und Sorgen, die hinter dem Jugendstreik stecken.»




«Das ist nicht Jammern auf hohem Niveau»




Auch in Zürich wird mobilisiert. Studentin Alba Fischer vom «Bündnis gegen Austerität» geht auf die Strasse. Ist die Situation der jungen Menschen in Frankreich vergleichbar? «Wenn das Jammern auf hohem Niveau ist, dass man sich das Leben nicht mehr leisten kann, Wohnungen nicht bezahlbar sind, die Krankenkassenprämien jedes Jahr steigen, jedes fünfte Kind in Armut aufwächst», sagt Alba Fischer. «Dann weiss ich nicht, was Jammern auf dem richtigen Niveau ist.»

…“ 

Beitrag von Michael Spillmann und Pirmin Roos vom 19.11.2026

 

 

 mit einigen Videos. Siehe zu den angesprochenen Halloweenprotesten vom 31. Oktober 2026:







Zivilpolizisten und Pyrotechnik




„

Augenzeug*innen berichten, wie sich mutmassliche Zivilpolizisten während den Halloween-Krawallen vermummten und Pyrotechnik mit sich trugen. Handelte es sich dabei um sogenannte Agents Provocateurs?


In der Halloween-Nacht am 31. Oktober 2026 riefen linksautonome Aktivist*innen zu Protesten im Zürcher Langstrassenquartier auf. Nach wochenlangen, teils gewaltsamen Jugendunruhen in ganz Europa erreichte die Protestwelle nun auch die Schweiz. Die Protestbewegung ist heterogen und vielfältig; im Fokus steht der Kampf gegen die Militarisierung und Austeritätspolitik. Etwa eine Stunde lang standen die schwarz gekleideten, teilweise maskierten Demonstrant*innen auf der Strasse und warteten darauf, dass endlich etwas passierte. Einige verteilten Bier und Schutzbrillen, palästinensische Fahnen wurden geschwenkt, laute Musik dröhnte aus den Boxen

…“ 

Artikel von Noctua Rosa Moser vom 08.11.2026 in Das Lamm/Dilemma

 




Krawall in Zürich: Der «Joker» ist los! Ausschreitungen auf der Strasse, in den Medien und der Politik: Das waren die Zürcher Halloweenproteste.




„… 

Es ist Samstagabend um exakt 23.23 Uhr, die Proteste überall in Europa haben auch die Schweiz erreicht. Mit einem durchaus originellen Ansatz: An diesem 31. Oktober hüllt sich der Protest ins Halloweenkostüm, womit das behördliche Vermummungsverbot elegant umgangen wird. Grinsende Clowns, schrille Gespenster und Guy-Fawkes-Masken haben sich an der Zürcher Langstrasse versammelt. Billiges Dosenbier wird als Lockmittel an Zaungäste verteilt, Technomusik erschallt aus mobilen Lautsprechern.




Sprachloser Umzug




Dann zünden Petarden, es geht auch schon los. Keine Transparente mit Parolen, keine Forderungen, die geäussert werden – ein sprachloser Umzug, einzig auf Krawall gebürstet. Mülltonnen werden herangerollt, Flaschen als Wurfgeschosse in Einkaufswagen aussortiert. Dann brennen auch schon die ersten Container und was der heutige Stadtraum sonst noch zur Verfügung stellt (Elektrovelos, E-Trottis). Man muss an diesem Abend gar nicht unterscheiden wollen zwischen sogenannt guten Protestierenden und bösen Krawallanten, zwischen Militanten und Mitlaufenden: Auf den Putz hauen wollen offenkundig alle, kaum jemand ist ohne Schutzbrille gekommen. Und die Polizei liefert mit ihren Wasserwerfern ja auch schon die erwarteten Zutaten: zuerst das kalte Nass und dann auch das Tränengas

…“ 

Artikel von Kaspar Surber in der WoZ vom 5. November 2026

 













Grundinfos:







Schweizer Jugendstreikbündniss

 

: „

Wir sind ein wachsendes Bündnis aus verschiedenen Organisationen, die zum Streik am 20. November aufrufen. Wer den Streik in deiner Region unterstützt, findest du auf der Streikkarte. Schweizweit mobilisieren folgende Organisationen für den Jugendstreik: JUSO, GSoA, Junge Grüne, VPOD, VSS, PdA, Kommunistische Jugend, FAJ Schweiz, Schweizerische Friedensbewegung, Schweizer Netzwerk gegen Krieg, Act now!, XR Familles. Dazu kommen viele regionale Organisationen, Kollektive, Parteien und Gewerkschaften. Das Bündnis ist ausserdem Teil einer 

internationalen Koalition

 

.“




https://www.instagram.com/jugendstreik/




Siehe den internationalen Überblick im Dossier: 

Das öffentliche Bildungswesen wurde international marode gespart – die Jugendproteste für ihre Zukunft breiten sich international aus







Der Beitrag 

Auch in der Schweiz: Jugendstreik gegen Austerität und Aufrüstung

 erschien zuerst auf 

LabourNet Germany

author: anred
title: Santa Fe: ante la inundación del Paraná y la falta de respuestas gubernamentales, las y los vecinos se organizan
content:
Foto: corresponsal.




Ante la crecida del Rio Paraná y frente al abandono total por parte de las autoridades estatales en todos sus niveles, la Asamblea Autoconvocada de Vecinos de Arroyo Leyes y de la costa santafesina convocaron este lunes 16 a una conferencia de prensa frente al Centro de Salud N°13 de Arroyo Leyes exigiendo que se atiendan de forma urgente las demandas de las y los vecinos de la zona. Entre las principales demandas al gobierno provincial, a cargo de Maximiliano Pullaro, y la gestión comunal de Eduardo Luis Lorinz, están que informen un 

protocolo oficial en caso de una posible catástrofe; la realización de la postergada obra de defensa en el margen Oeste de la Ruta Provincial N°1; la

 

provisión urgente de agua segura, alimentos, medios para cocinar, productos de higiene, repelente, generadores y nafta para zonas afectadas; garantizar un subsidio económico mensual a las familias afectadas durante el período de emergencia

; 

garantizar la estabilidad laboral y el cobro efectivo y total del salario del personal público y privado afectado por la emergencia hídrica; garantizar la salud Pública; accesibilidad a viviendas dignas para las familias afectadas; y la provisión de embarcaciones a vecinos afectados. 

Por corresponsal, para ANRed.







Desde la asamblea convocaron a una conferencia de prensa el pasado lunes 16 de noviembre frente al 

Centro de Salud N°13 de Arroyo Leyes

, donde 

advirtieron sobre el estado de las defensas y cuestionaron que no haya partidas previstas para obras en el presupuesto provincial 2027

.




Así están las defensas construidas por los propios vecinos de Arroyo Leyes para proteger sus viviendas ante el avance del agua. Foto: Gentileza.




Durante la conferencia de prensa, también adelantaron que 

continuarán reuniéndose para coordinar acciones con otras asambleas de la Costa

, para mantener un espacio de organización y participación que permita visibilizar las dificultades que atraviesan las distintas localidades y avanzar en una agenda común de reclamos frente a la emergencia hídrica.




Foto: corresponsal.




 




Por la crecida del río en Arroyo Leyes ya 

hay al menos 150 familias, entre personas evacuadas, autoevacuadas y vecinos/as que todavía permanecen en sus viviendas, sin electricidad desde hace más de tres días y con el agua en el acceso a sus casas. 

Vecinos/as trasladan sus pertenencias a zonas altas y reclaman por la falta de luz, dado que el comité de emergencia decidió que los lugares que estén anegados van a tener cortes de energía preventivos.




En las inmediaciones funcionan unas seis guarderías náuticas, con aproximadamente 800 embarcaciones, según informó el medio local 

Aire de Santa Fe

, y algunos propietarios comenzaron a retirarlas ante el avance del agua. En este marco, las y los residentes afirman que no recibieron respuestas de las autoridades comunales ni provinciales. Ante la falta de respuestas, realizaron un

 corte de la rutaprovincial 1 durante la tarde del pasado domingo 15.




Este es el pliego de revindicaciones:







La exigencia de un 

protocolo oficial en caso de una posible catástrofe

 (asistencia, acciones específicas y destinos específicos), dados ya los 

pronósticos de Instituto Nacional del Agua (INA)

 y de la 

Empresa Binacional Yacyretá (EBY)




La exigencia al gobierno provincial de la 

realización de la postergada obra de defensa en el margen Oeste de la Ruta Porvincial N°1, desde el kilómetro 8 al 22

, de manera consensuada con la comunidad. Sin desmedro de la urgencia de la obra, que debe comenzar cuanto antes, se exige su inclusión en el presupuesto 2027, además del refuerzo, alteo y mantenimiento de todos los anillos de defensa de la provincia.




La 

provisión urgente de alimentos, medios para cocinar, productos de higiene, repelente y agua segura para zonas afectadas

.




La provisión de agua segura a toda la población de la costa que depende del suministro de las napas, hoy en riesgo de contaminación producto de la crecida.




Garantizar 

un subsidio económico mensual durante el período de emergencia

 que sea suficiente para garantizar la canasta básica de las familias afectadas, la mayoría de las cuales viven del trabajo en negro o por cuenta propia.




Garantizar la estabilidad laboral y el cobro efectivo y total del salario del personal público y privado afectado

 por la emergencia hídrica.




Garantizar la Salud Pública

, ampliando la atención en los Centros de Salud locales las 24hs del día, los siete días de la semana, reforzando el escaso personal y garantizando la disponibilidad de ambulancias y postas de salud próximas a las zonas más afectadas.




Accesibilidad a viviendas dignas

 para las familias afectadas.




Ante los posibles robos a las casas inundadas, 

refuerzo de la seguridad

, aumentando la cantidad de personal, patrullaje y disponibilidad de embarcaciones para monitoreo de las zonas afectadas.




Provisión de embarcaciones a vecinos/as afectados

.




Suministro de generadores y nafta para las familias afectadas

.




Atención particular para los domicilios con personas electrodependientes

.




Asegurar, poniendo a disposición los medios de transporte necesarios, el 

acceso de infancias, adolescencias y personas mayores de la población afectada, a la educación y propuestas recreativas

.




Exigir a la gestión Comunal la difusión del Plan de Contingencia ante la Emergencia

.

title: A New International Order? Xi, Trump & Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in China
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted his U.S. and Russian counterparts for a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, with the leaders of the three biggest nuclear superpowers meeting for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen. Afterward, the countries published a “peace declaration” that affirmed “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.” The declaration also announced a commitment to increase petroleum production, called for reforms at the United Nations and urged the International Criminal Court and similar bodies to “not abuse their jurisdiction.”




While in China, President Donald Trump also had a separate meeting with President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war in Ukraine, though it’s unclear if they made any progress.




“It’s a significant post-1945 moment, which was the last time that we had great summits,” says Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin. “What is the most important takeaway … is an ascendant China. It was China that really set the terms of what was said.”

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Hasan Piker Aims to Raise $1m for Anti-ICE Groups With GTA 6 Livestream
content:
US Twitch streamer and leftwing political commentator Hasan Piker has launched a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed fundraiser for two pro-migrant rights groups – aiming to raise $1m (£759,000).




​Piker, who

 

began playing

 the hugely anticipated game as it launched at midnight on Thursday,

 has already 

raised over $82,000

 from the multi-day “GTA 6: Melt the ICE” campaign.  




If the fundraiser reaches $1m, Piker has pledged to give himself a “Zohran Moustache”, after the New York City mayor unveiled new facial hair earlier this month for Movember.  




The money will be split between the Los Angeles-based

 

Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights

 (Chirla) and the

 

National Immigration Law Center

 (NILC). Both organisations have played key roles in securing legal protections for migrants and opposing abductions and other abuses by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).




“NILC and Chirla… are helping the most vulnerable that have been targeted by ICE get legal representation, rapid responses for ICE raids, lobbying congress for change and much much more,” the stream’s fundraiser page on Tiltify says.




​Piker, who was

 

banned from entering the UK in June

 over his opposition to Israel’s genocide in Gaza,

 

raised over $1m

 in October 2023 for Palestinian medical aid. Earlier the same year, he raised $1.2m for relief efforts following earthquakes in Turkey, where he spent his childhood, and Syria.




Ahead of the GTA 6 launch on Wednesday, Piker wrote on X: “I never experienced Xmas, since we don’t have it in Turkey but I assume this is the closest one can feel to being a child on Xmas eve. I cannot wait for GTA6”.




At one point during the livestream, Piker encountered a satirical radio show parodying far-right commentators Alex Jones and Nick Fuentes.




“I will admit I’m a little bit sad,” he said, reacting to the gameplay. “I really wish I was getting dunked on by Rockstar.”  




The new release has been described as the most widely anticipated video game ever, and may even be

 

the biggest entertainment launch

 in history, having made 

$1.65bn in pre-order sales

 alone.

title: New photo of Abdullah Öcalan released
content:
A new photo of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who is imprisoned on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, has been released. The photo was taken on October 9, 2026, during a family visit.




The photo was published on Wednesday by Ömer Öcalan, Abdullah Öcalan’s nephew and a member of parliament for the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party). The photo shows Abdullah Öcalan alongside his nephew Ömer Öcalan, his niece Havva Elçin, and his cousin Hacı Aydın Öcalan.

title: Women hold dialogue workshop in Qamishlo
content:
The workshop was attended by 300 participants, including members of women’s movements and organisations, as well as female intellectuals and politicians. Discussions focused on political and legal violence and the role of women in integration.




The declaration issued following the workshop highlighted the following points:




1. Guaranteeing women’s rights in the Syrian constitution and ensuring equality between women and men. No discrimination should be made on the basis of gender, nationality or religion, and women’s rights should be constitutionally guaranteed.




2. Guaranteeing women’s participation in legislative, executive, administrative and judicial institutions, ensuring that they are represented and have decision-making power at every level.




3. Guaranteeing education in the mother tongue in the constitution.




4. Fighting political and institutional violence against women, as well as taking a stand against policies of ignoring women. Women must be guaranteed the right to organise, express their opinions and participate in politics.




5. Protecting women from violence through laws and mechanisms. Ending domestic, social, economic and sexual violence, and punishing those who perpetrate violence against women. Ensuring women’s access to justice and protecting all women without discrimination.




6. Strengthening the role of women’s movements and organisations and ensuring their participation in the peace process and transitional justice.




7. Establishing autonomous mechanisms to legally pursue violations against women. Punishing those who undermine women’s achievements and rights.

title: Dr. Korkmaz: Turkey may pay a heavy price for military alliances
content:
Tensions between Iran and Israel, the new political landscape in Syria, escalating conflicts in Yemen and the Mecca Defence Pact are reshaping the balance of power in the Middle East. Relations between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states, the position of the Kurds in regional developments and the future of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey are also among the major issues on the regional agenda.




Dr. Toros Korkmaz spoke to ANF about developments in the Middle East, regional power relations and the future of the peace process in Turkey.




'Power struggles in the Middle East bring both risks and opportunities'




Korkmaz said that the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey began at a time of continuing wars and power struggles in the Middle East, and that it could not be considered independently of the uncertainties created by these developments.




Korkmaz said: "Opportunities and risks do not emerge in isolation. This is actually a dialectical process. If we look at the peace process, a very serious perception of a security threat emerged in Israel following Hamas's attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. This prompted Israel to put its plan to reshape the Middle East into action. Following this plan, we witnessed the fragmentation of Syria, then the Israel-Iran war backed by the United States, and the direct involvement of the US in that war. The peace process came onto the agenda after all these developments. Frankly, I do not think such a peace process could have begun under the present circumstances if this environment of war had not emerged and if the Turkish government and state had not been aware of Israel's plan to reshape the Middle East. That is why I believe the 7 October attack was very important."




'A possible war with Iran will affect the process in Turkey'




Korkmaz said that the direction of the Kurdish question could change amid the ongoing armed conflicts in the Middle East, particularly the threat of war involving Iran. He warned of the risks arising from Turkey's reluctance to move the process forward.




Korkmaz also said: "Consider what would happen if Iran were severely weakened by the Iran-Israel war and entered a process of fragmentation. In that case, the possibility of Kurds in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) gaining increasing autonomy would emerge. This would put pressure on Turkey. Under such circumstances, Turkey might decide to continue the peace process. However, a different picture could emerge if the current stalemate continues and the Turkish state concludes that Israel has reached the limits of its power and no longer has the capacity to advance further or reshape the Middle East. If such a perception develops within the Turkish state, there may be a tendency to freeze or slow down the peace process, or to limit reforms as much as possible.




Therefore, how the war ends, who emerges victorious and what kind of regional situation develops afterwards are extremely important. Will Iran fragment or remain intact? What are the limits of Israel's power? All these questions will be decisive."




'National consciousness and aspirations are growing among Kurds'




Korkmaz said that the war concerned not only Turkey and the Turkish state but also the development of Kurdish national consciousness throughout the conflict.




Korkmaz said: "National consciousness is growing among Kurds across all four parts of Kurdistan, in Syria, Iraq, Iran and Turkey. Kurds recognise that the Middle East has become a region engulfed in conflict and that they can survive this period only by strengthening unity and solidarity among themselves. I believe this is an important development.




The Kurdish dynamic must be taken into account. It cannot be ignored. Kurds are becoming increasingly aware of their national identity and are organising across all four parts of Kurdistan. What have we witnessed during this process? For example, for the first time, all Kurdish parties in Iran came together. Organisations that previously seemed incapable of coming together found common ground. In Turkey, particularly in Northern Kurdistan, there has also been a significant increase in national consciousness. At times when Kurdish rights were violated in Rojava and the region was under threat, Kurds mobilised not only in Turkey but also across Europe.




War creates existential conditions, and such circumstances can contribute positively to the development of national consciousness among peoples. I believe Kurdish national consciousness has developed more strongly during this war than in previous periods."




'The Mecca Pact could draw Turkey into conflicts'




Korkmaz warned that Turkey might feel compelled to enter alliances that could prove extremely costly, describing the Mecca Agreement as one such arrangement.




Korkmaz said: "Under this agreement, three countries, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, form a military defence pact. However, this pact also carries numerous risks. From an external and superficial perspective, one might reach the following conclusion: Money will come from Saudi Arabia and the Gulf countries it leads, while Turkey possesses military technology. This would create a new market for Turkey, allowing it to sell military technology to the Gulf states. Pakistan, meanwhile, could provide support in the nuclear and military fields. That is the picture presented by a superficial assessment.




However, a closer examination reveals a different situation. Saudi Arabia is engaged on numerous fronts. It has a direct front in Yemen, another in Sudan and a front against Iran in the Gulf. It also has a front to the north, in Syria. In other words, we are talking about a power involved in conflicts and tensions in many places. Pakistan also faces problems on at least five different fronts. Moreover, Pakistan is one of the world's most authoritarian countries. Human rights activists there can be detained and imprisoned directly on terrorism charges.




Both Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are countries governed by authoritarian regimes where democracy is absent. At the same time, they are involved in conflicts and tensions with other countries."




'Turkey could pay a heavy military price'




Korkmaz warned that Turkey's participation in the Mecca Pact could oblige it to deploy troops to conflict zones. He said: "This could result in substantial loss of life. These are enormous risks. Indeed, as soon as the Mecca Agreement was signed, India strongly objected to Pakistan and declared that the agreement was directed against it. This aspect is also extremely important. Turkey could face heavy costs and be forced to deploy troops directly. While seeking to gain access to a market, it could suffer very serious casualties.




Secondly, the Mecca alliance also has a sectarian character. In its current form, it appears to be a Sunni alliance. It also involves positioning against Iran. We know that Iran supports various forces in the Middle East. The conflict in Yemen, Hezbollah in Lebanon and the confrontations with Israel must be considered in this context. If the war in Yemen intensifies in the future and the Houthis strengthen their position, Turkey could find itself confronting a bloc of forces linked to Iran. A conflict with Hezbollah or Iran could come onto the agenda. This would have extremely serious consequences."




'The Mecca Pact could become an agreement targeting Kurds'




Korkmaz said that Turkey's attempts to assume a role in the Middle East's power struggles, while disregarding the Kurds, carried major risks.




Korkmaz continued: "There is a fire burning somewhere, and you approach it with petrol as part of a military strategy. Instead of doing this, if Turkey reached an agreement with the Kurds, recognised their rights and became a genuinely democratic country in the region, it could achieve far greater gains than those it hopes to obtain through military alliances.




That is because Turkey could then be presented as an example of democracy in the Middle East. Consider another example. Would Turkey gain more economically, culturally and in every other field by joining the European Union and becoming part of it, or through military alliances with authoritarian regimes?Making peace with the Kurds and ensuring their democratic integration would also positively affect Turkey's relations with the West and the European Union.




We should also examine the provisions of the Mecca Pact. In particular, Article 5 provides for intelligence sharing against terrorist organisations. At first glance, this provision might appear reasonable. However, the Turkish state still regards the Rojava region, the Kurds of Rojava and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) as terrorist entities. Likewise, the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), or what is now called the Kurdish Movement, is viewed in the same way. The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) in Iran is also designated a terrorist organisation.




Consequently, even if it is not explicitly stated, this agreement could involve an approach targeting the Kurds. This is an agreement between nation-states that prioritises the nation-state mentality. It is based on nation-state structures that disregard the peoples of the region, different beliefs and the pluralistic character of the Middle East.




Yet the Kurds are one of the strongest local forces in the region. Nevertheless, the nation-states in which they live can easily classify them as terrorist elements. The Mecca Agreement inherently carries this risk. It may have other benefits, but I believe the possibility of it becoming an agreement directed against the Kurds is more important. This dimension must be examined and discussed."




'

A ground operation against Iran would be risky'




Korkmaz also examined why Iran had not collapsed despite the interventions against it. He said: "The Iranian regime has managed to remain in power so far. One of the main reasons is that Iran is a very large country. It has approximately twice Turkey's population and territory. Geographically, the Zagros Mountains lie to the south, while the Alborz Mountains lie to the north. Iran is a protected region surrounded by these mountain ranges.




It has become clear that the regime cannot be overthrown through air strikes alone. That would require a major ground operation. Military experts say that occupying Iran by land would require at least 1.5 to 2 million troops. Even deploying a force of that size would not guarantee the operation's success. Such an undertaking would carry enormous risks. At present, there are no serious indications that Iran is about to collapse or fragment in the near future. This must be stated clearly.




This is where a major risk also emerges for Turkey. The United States could use the Mecca alliance as a justification for involving Turkey in a major ground operation against Iran. This is a possibility, and it represents a serious risk. What the Kurds need to do in this situation is pursue cautious and realistic politics. It would be wrong to adopt an approach such as, 'The Iranian regime will collapse soon, so let us launch an uprising for independence and freedom,' or 'We will act when the US and Israel give us the go-ahead.' Acting in this way could cause extremely serious harm.




As in Turkey, Kurds should push for democratic integration in Iran. They should be able to say to the Iranian state, 'You are under a major attack. Recognise our rights and establish a democratic system based on those rights.' That is because when democracy develops, the justification for external attacks also disappears. Where does the claimed legitimacy of attacks against Iran come from today? From the Iranian regime's theocratic and authoritarian character, its oppression of peoples and its refusal to recognise democratic rights. If Iran had a pluralistic, democratic and secular system, and had developed a model of governance similar to that of Rojava, these attacks would lose their legitimacy.




Therefore, what Kurds should do there is push for democratic integration rather than launch an uprising for independence at the instigation of the US and Israel. A wait-and-see approach may be an appropriate strategy for the Kurds. However, this must not mean remaining passive. They need to strengthen their organisations, struggle for democratic integration and increase pressure on the Iranian regime in this direction. That is what the Kurds should do."




'The Turkish state insists on a security-based approach to the process'




Toros Korkmaz said that achieving democratic integration through the ongoing process in Turkey would benefit the entire region. He stressed the importance of developing a pluralistic and democratic mentality and highlighted the value of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan's warnings on this issue.




Korkmaz said: "Turning to the process in Turkey, unfortunately, we cannot see any progress at present. Realistically speaking, the process is not moving forward. The state has not managed to change its traditional statist and nationalist approach. It continues to view the Kurdish question entirely from a security-based perspective, treating it as a terrorism issue.




When we examine the statements of senior state representatives, the President and high-ranking bureaucrats, we see that the issue is still being described as a terrorism problem. The statements by presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum that the first four articles of the Constitution will not be changed also reflect this approach. The Kurdish question is still not being acknowledged as an issue of identity, culture and language. It has been reduced entirely to a terrorism issue.




The process is currently stuck. We cannot see any progress. What needs to be done at this point is to maintain pressure on the state to take steps. The Turkish state tradition is characterised by an unwillingness to act unless it faces pressure. Therefore, Kurds must express their demands for identity and language rights as strongly as possible and struggle alongside other democratic forces in Turkey by building the broadest possible organisations. This is the stage the process has reached.




However, it is the Turkish state that will suffer the consequences of this situation, and it is already doing so. This must also be said. The reason Turkey feels compelled to enter the Mecca Agreement is its failure to democratise internally. If Turkey had been able to democratise itself, it would not have had to assume military obligations that could come at such a heavy cost. However, because those governing the state do not have a sufficiently democratic mentality, have failed to develop a democratic approach and still do not understand this reality, they are exposing Turkey to enormous risks."

title: Women's Peace Monitoring Commission established in Istanbul
content:
The Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission announced its establishment following preparatory meetings involving approximately 100 women.




The commission announced its establishment at a press conference held at the Kadın Zamanı Association. It aims to be represented on the Independent Monitoring Board to be established under the framework law adopted by Parliament. Representatives of women's organisations and many other women attended the meeting, where participants chanted the slogan "Jin, jiyan, azadî" (Woman, Life, Freedom).




The statement emphasised that lasting peace requires more than an end to conflict. It also involves confronting the past, uncovering the truth, ensuring justice and rebuilding society.




The statement drew attention to the impact of war, forced displacement and losses experienced across generations on women, stressing that women's equal participation and authority in decision-making mechanisms are fundamental to lasting peace.




The statement noted that women experience war and conflict in different ways, including imprisonment, poverty, male violence, labour exploitation and displacement, but that these experiences are often made invisible in peace processes. The commission stressed the need for independent monitoring of the process from a gender equality perspective.




The commission said that its first priority would be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595, adopted by Parliament, and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the parliamentary commission's report.




The statement continued: "Following a meeting involving approximately 100 women, we decided to move forward as the Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission. We hereby announce the establishment of our commission. We are still at the beginning of this journey. Our first priority will be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595 adopted by Parliament, the rationale behind the law and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the commission's report, as well as the legal and political steps necessary to resolve the Kurdish question and democratise Turkey. We aim to monitor these steps, the laws enacted and the mechanisms established, their impact on everyday life, the obstacles they face, their shortcomings, what remains undone and what is made invisible, through women's eyes and drawing on the experience of the women's freedom struggle. We also aim to make our voices heard on these issues. We believe it is essential to exert pressure in favour of peace wherever the necessary steps are not taken. In this process, we need to speak out more, not remain silent. We will do this through reports, visits, monitoring delegations, various subcommissions and other methods we develop together, and we will regularly share our findings with the public. Above all, we call on all women to monitor this process with us and join the commission at every stage. Let us take responsibility together for building an equal and lasting peace. We remind those in positions of decision-making authority: We are watching you. We women will hold you accountable for peace!"

author: Unknown
title: Evin Zapsu's lawyer: Evin is in severe pain and needs treatment
content:
The health condition of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, who is held at Kayseri Bünyan Women's Closed Prison and was diagnosed with cancer on 16 November, remains critical. Biopsy results and other medical examinations revealed stage four uterine cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. Despite repeated calls for her release, Evin Zapsu remains imprisoned.




Relatives of ill prisoners have called for their release outside the Ministry of Justice, while Evin Zapsu's lawyer, Berivan Çelik, spoke to ANF about her client's health and the latest developments.




'Evin is suffering from severe pain'




Berivan Çelik said that Evin Zapsu remained in good spirits despite trying to conceal the pain, swelling and physical changes. Çelik said that doctors had informed Evin Zapsu, who was diagnosed with stage four uterine cancer with metastases, that she urgently needed surgery. She warned that further delays in treatment could leave her client dependent on others for care.




The lawyer said that she met Evin Zapsu face to face at the prison last Tuesday and witnessed her deteriorating health firsthand.




Despite taking two strong painkillers, Evin Zapsu was visibly suffering from severe pain and had significant abdominal swelling and other physical changes. Çelik said that her client remained in good spirits but was trying to conceal her suffering.




Berivan Çelik said: "Although she had taken two strong painkillers before coming to our meeting, it was very clear that she was in pain, even though she tried not to show it. Nevertheless, her spirits were high and she was smiling. She believed that even if her test results were bad, she would be able to overcome the illness without too much difficulty."




Report concludes that she can remain in prison




Berivan Çelik said that an earlier medical assessment had concluded that her client could remain in prison. Three days after they submitted a request for the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin Zapsu was taken to Kayseri City Hospital, where a medical board prepared a report.




Çelik said that the report concluded that Evin Zapsu was fit to remain in prison, while subsequent biopsy results revealed the severity of her illness.




Çelik also said: "Three days after we first requested the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin was taken to Kayseri City Hospital. A medical board report was prepared at the hospital, and the report issued last Monday concluded that she could remain in prison. However, the biopsy results revealed stage four uterine cancer with metastases.




We therefore submitted another application today. We have not yet received a written response to our previous request. No decision approving or rejecting our application has been communicated to us."




'The masses have spread to her chest and armpits'




Berivan Çelik also referred to radiological imaging and CT scan results, saying that her client's health had deteriorated since the first scans were carried out in August.




Çelik said that masses initially detected in the abdominal area had spread over time and that new masses had developed.




Çelik also said: "The initial radiological scans showed masses only in her abdomen. She told us that these masses had gradually spread upwards towards her chest and that new masses had begun to appear in her armpits. We have the radiological images, CT scans, their reports and the biopsy results.




When we compare the reports from August with her current condition, we can see that the masses have increased considerably and are causing much more pain."




Berivan Çelik said that the doctor who examined her client had told her that she urgently needed surgery to remove the masses. She explained that following the initial pathology results, she and Evin Zapsu's family had consulted an oncology specialist on the basis of the scans taken in August.




Although the specialist provided a verbal opinion, they were unable to obtain a written assessment. Following the biopsy results, they submitted a new application.




Çelik said that they attached the biopsy results to their second petition and stressed that treatment must begin immediately.




'Treatment is not possible under prison conditions'




Berivan Çelik also described the health problems her client faces in prison, saying that the cold conditions force her to sleep with hot-water bottles and that she spends most of her time in bed because of the pain.




The lawyer said that Zapsu's hospital visits generally resulted in little more than the administration of painkillers and added: "Evin told me that the prison was very cold and that she constantly had to lie down with hot-water bottles. She is also distressed by having to remain in bed and needing others to look after her. She tries to meet her own needs and makes an effort not to become dependent on anyone. 




Evin is taken to hospital when she requests it, but she is only admitted for outpatient consultations at the district state hospital or the city hospital. These visits generally involve only short-term treatment, such as painkillers."




'Treatment must begin immediately'




Berivan Çelik expressed concern about Evin Zapsu's health, stressing that despite her positive spirits during their meeting, the severity of her pain was unmistakable.




Çelik stressed that treatment must begin without further delay and concluded: "Evin was in very good spirits, but I witnessed her condition firsthand. It was obvious that she was suffering from severe pain. No matter how high her spirits were, it was extremely difficult for her to cope with that pain. She was doing everything she could to avoid showing it.




Her abdomen was severely swollen. There was visible redness, bruising and swelling associated with the pain. I witnessed all of this myself during our meeting. If her treatment does not begin as soon as possible, her condition will become much worse."

author: Unknown
title: Janet Biehl: Democratic integration should guide the peace process
content:
American writer and social ecology thinker Janet Biehl, in an assessment she wrote on Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 February 2025 Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, emphasised the importance of democratic and legal steps for advancing the peace process in Turkey.




Statements and letters prepared as part of an international solidarity campaign launched with the participation of 97 intellectuals will be published as an English-language e-book by Daraja Press.




Janet Biehl’s foreword to the book, entitled “The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, was also conveyed to the Imrali Delegation.




In her article, Janet Biehl said that the Framework Law adopted by Parliament was of vital importance for advancing the process. She said that, following confirmation by the National Security Council of the PKK’s disarmament steps, the way could be paved for the reintegration into social life of political prisoners and some PKK members living abroad.




However, Janet Biehl emphasised that, alongside the implementation of the legal framework, additional confidence-building measures were also necessary. In this regard, she outlined a number of demands, including clarifying Abdullah Öcalan’s status, ending the appointment of trustees, releasing political prisoners, guaranteeing the healthcare rights of sick prisoners, and lifting restrictions on Kurdish political activities and the media.




She also identified the release of Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as guarantees allowing PKK members who lay down their arms to participate in politics, as necessary steps.




A pluralistic and democratic society




Biehl said that the assessments made by other intellectuals featured in the book also set out the objectives of the peace process. Key themes emerging from these contributions include a multi-ethnic political system, the coexistence of peoples on equal terms, the democratisation of the nation-state and the construction of a pluralistic society.




Referring also to Abdullah Öcalan’s principle of “democratic integration”, Biehl highlighted the importance of establishing a system in which different peoples can coexist within a shared political sphere, free from relations of domination.




Biehl concluded her foreword with the following words: “I hope that these voices and ideas will serve as guiding lights for the peace process over the coming months and years.”




Janet Biehl




Janet Biehl is an American writer, translator and social ecology thinker. Having worked alongside Murray Bookchin for many years, she is known for her work on social ecology, libertarian municipalism and democratic confederalism.

author: Daniel Avalos
title: Residentes en movilización por el descuido de quienes nos cuidan
content:
Residentes de hospitales de Nación, Provincia de Buenos Aires y CABA realizaron este miércoles un paro y una movilización conjunta. Reclaman una recomposición salarial y mejores condiciones laborales, pero también advierten sobre el deterioro de la calidad de atención y la falta de recursos en el sistema público de salud.




Fotos y texto Daniel Ávalos para ANRed.







No era solamente una discusión por el sueldo. En las caras y en las palabras de quienes marcharon este miércoles había una preocupación que iba más allá de los números: sentir que todo el esfuerzo puesto en formarse, estudiar y sostener guardias interminables no tiene reconocimiento. Son profesionales que eligieron la salud, se esforzaron durante años de formación, y hoy trabajan en hospitales públicos. Atienden pacientes, forman parte de los equipos de atención y sostienen buena parte de la actividad cotidiana de los servicios. Sin embargo, sienten que ese trabajo pierde valor frente a salarios insuficientes, falta de recursos y decisiones de los distintos gobiernos que afectan directamente sus tareas.




 




Con un paro y una movilización conjunta, residentes de Nación, Provincia de Buenos Aires y Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires llevaron sus reclamos a las calles. La jornada comenzó en la Casa de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. Desde allí marcharon hacia el Ministerio de Salud de la Nación y luego al Ministerio de Salud porteño. Tres jurisdicciones, distintos gobiernos y una preocupación compartida.




En la provincia de Buenos Aires, un residente de primer año cobra alrededor de $1.300.000. El reclamo es llevar ese ingreso a un piso de $2.600.000. La diferencia entre ambas cifras no es un detalle . Es la distancia entre el trabajo que realizan y las condiciones materiales en las que pueden sostener su vida. Porque la vocación no paga el alquiler ni llena la heladera. Tampoco debería ser una excusa para naturalizar jornadas extensas, salarios bajos o pérdida de derechos laborales.




Pero hay otra preocupación que apareció con fuerza durante la jornada: la calidad de la atención.




Los residentes advierten que cada vez cuentan con menos herramientas para hacer su trabajo. Faltan medicamentos, insumos y personal. Los equipos se reducen y la demanda de atención sigue estando ahí, del otro lado de la puerta del consultorio o de la guardia. Cuando un profesional no dispone de los recursos necesarios y debe multiplicar esfuerzos para cubrir las necesidades de un servicio, el problema no queda dentro del hospital. También lo padecen quienes llegan buscando atención.




El ajuste también tiene responsables, el deterioro que denuncian los residentes no puede separarse de la política presupuestaria del Gobierno nacional. El ajuste sobre el sistema sanitario tiene números concretos. En mayo, el Ejecutivo recortó más de $63.000 millones de distintas partidas del Ministerio de Salud. Entre ellas, $25.000 millones fueron destinados al fortalecimiento de los sistemas provinciales, y otros $20.000 millones para medicamentos, insumos y tecnología médica. No es una discusión contable. Son recursos que deberían traducirse en hospitales funcionando, medicamentos disponibles y mejores condiciones para atender a la población.







El ministro Mario Lugones está al frente de ese Ministerio y tiene responsabilidad política sobre las decisiones que se toman desde allí. No alcanza con administrar el ajuste ni la precariedad que promueve su gestión, y hablar de eficiencia cuando son los trabajadores y los pacientes quienes terminan enfrentando sus consecuencias. En ese contexto, la situación de las residencias nacionales suma otro problema. El nuevo régimen de becas, establecido por una resolución firmada por el propio Lugones, elimina derechos como el aguinaldo y los aportes jubilatorios.




Los trabajadores también denuncian recortes de cupos y cierres de espacios de formación. La preocupación alcanza al futuro de las residencias y a la posibilidad de seguir formando profesionales dentro del sistema público.




En el documento conjunto, los residentes también alertan sobre el desfinanciamiento de las áreas de salud mental y discapacidad, la falta de recursos para garantizar tratamientos y medicamentos, y el incumplimiento de políticas previstas en la Ley Nacional de Salud Mental.




En CABA, además, denunciaron amenazas y medidas de amedrentamiento contra quienes participan de las protestas.







Esta movilización excede el reclamo salarial. Hay profesionales que identifican que el esfuerzo para llegar hasta donde están y el que hacen todos los días dentro de los hospitales no encuentra respuesta en ninguno de los tres niveles de gobierno. La preocupación no es solamente cuánto cobran, sino qué condiciones tienen para ejercer su profesión, y qué atención pueden ofrecer cuando faltan recursos para hacerlo.




Quienes se preparan durante años para cuidar a otros están teniendo que salir a la calle para defender las condiciones en las que pueden hacerlo. Y eso también habla de la salud pública que estamos construyendo.




La salud pública no se sostiene sólo con edificios, presupuestos o anuncios oficiales. Se sostiene con trabajadores que estudian, se forman, hacen guardias y ponen el cuerpo todos los días. Cuando ese trabajo pierde reconocimiento y las condiciones se deterioran, lo que está en juego no es solamente el futuro de los residentes. Es también el derecho de toda la población a recibir una atención digna.

author: anred
title: Los tres megayates que pretendían anclar en el Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego arribaron a Ushuaia
content:
Los cruceros Lonian, Hodor y Sherakhan este miercoles 18 por la mañana, captados por la cámara del fotógrafo Juan Odela.




La flota de megayates de super lujo que desató una fuerte controversia ambiental, legal y geopolítica en Tierra del Fuego ya se encuentra en aguas fueguinas, pero lejos de los ecosistemas protegidos de Bahía Lapataia. El lunes 16 de noviembre, los buques Lonian, Hodor y Sherakhan – los dos primeros con bandera británica – arribaron a la capital provincial y permanecen fondeados en la Bahía de Ushuaia, cerrando en los hechos la pulseada administrativa que obligó a dar marcha atrás con la autorización firmada por la Intendencia del Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego. 

Por Agenda Malvinas.







Los registros del sistema de seguimiento marítimo satelital 

VesselFinder

 

confirman que las tres embarcaciones navegan de manera coordinada, operando como una verdadera escuadrilla logística de turismo VIP:







M/Y Lonian:

 Fue el primero en tocar aguas de la bahía local, arribando a las 

14:10

. Con 87 metros de eslora y bandera de Islas Caimán, es la nave insignia vinculada al magnate estadounidense Lorenzo Fertitta.













M/Y Hodor:

 Ingresó en segundo lugar, a las 

17:08

. Este buque de apoyo de 67 metros —también registrado en el enclave colonial británico de Islas Caimán— funciona como plataforma logística y transporte auxiliar para la expedición.













M/Y Sherakhan:

 Cerró el despliegue de la flota ingresando a las 

17:34

, completando el posicionamiento conjunto frente a la costa de Ushuaia.










El desenlace que confirmó la advertencia técnica




La permanencia de los tres buques en la bahía de Ushuaia ratifica, en la práctica, la solución que el propio cuerpo técnico del Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego había planteado antes de que estallara el escándalo.




En el informe conjunto del 20 de octubre 

(IF-2026-102110148-APN-PNTF#APNAC)

, siete profesionales y jefes operativos del área protegida habían dictaminado que resultaba improcedente habilitar el fondeo en Bahía Lapataia y el sobrevuelo de sus dos helicópteros, señalando de forma explícita que estas operaciones podían desarrollarse perfectamente en otros sectores costeros, 

«como la bahía de Ushuaia – ubicados afuera del área protegida»

.




Pese a ese dictamen categórico, el 

intendente Marcelo Almirón

 había firmado el permiso el 27 de octubre 

(NO-2026-104217762-APN-PNTF#APNAC)

 a instancias de la agencia marítima local 

USHIP S.R.L..

 Solo tras la difusión pública de los expedientes oficiales y la repercusión periodística a nivel provincial y nacional, la empresa operadora desistió del pedido y la Intendencia debió emitir un comunicado de repliegue para dar por cerrada la autorización.




El saldo institucional y la alerta sobre la intermediación




El fondeo actual de la escuadrilla en la Bahía de Ushuaia evita el arrastre de cadenas y anclas de gran porte sobre los bosques sumergidos de cachiyuyo (

Macrocystis pyrifera

), así como la perturbación acústica de helicópteros sobre los hábitats del huillín y las aves costeras dentro del Parque Nacional.




Sin embargo, el episodio deja abierta una discusión de fondo sobre el funcionamiento de los controles estatales en el extremo sur. La secuencia documental expuso cómo una agencia marítima local puede tramitar permisos a medida por encima de las leyes nacionales y los informes técnicos, instalando un precedente de excepcionalidad que, como demuestran antecedentes similares en reservas provinciales como 

Península Mitre

 e 

Isla de los Estados

, exige un escrutinio público permanente sobre el manejo.
