author: CNT Madrid
title: Rechazar su presente, imaginar nuestro futuro: la I Estratégica de CNT Madrid
content:
Entramos en un nuevo ciclo de luchas inaugurado con la acampada de Sol en nuestra ciudad y con la huelga general que convocamos el pasado 11 de noviembre. Para abordarlo, la CNT de Madrid necesita fijar su rumbo. Por ello, el sindicato celebra 

estos días 20 y 21 de noviembre

 su primera asamblea Estratégica.




Estratégica es el nombre con el que la militancia del sindicato de oficios varios de Madrid capital adherido a la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo ha dado a conocer lo que es una 

asamblea extraordinaria

 que pone punto y aparte a varios meses de discusiones y debates en nuestra interna. Durante cerca de medio año, compañeras de toda nuestra organización vienen trabajando con ahínco en dotarnos de un espacio para decidir cuestiones fundamentales que atañen al futuro de CNT Madrid.




El papel del sindicato en la lucha de la vivienda, afianzar la presencia de nuestra anarcosindical en los barrios de Madrid, tener clara una postura frente a la inteligencia artificial. No son pocos los desafíos que como clase trabajadora organizada debemos afrontar. También tenemos la certeza de que son muchas las manos militantes que han ido llegando en los últimos meses al sindicato, en respuesta a una llamada tan simple como necesaria: solas no podemos, juntas sí.




Por eso CNT Madrid ha convenido que este encuentro de la Estratégica 2026 debe servir también como un lugar de encuentro para un período de reflexión ante todo lo que se nos viene. Por eso, de hecho, el leitmotiv que nos lleva a esta primera Estratégica es un eslogan muy sencillo: 

rechazar su presente, imaginar nuestro futuro.




Rechazamos el presente que nos pretenden imponer, uno en el que el rentismo y el capitalismo continúan asfixiando a una clase trabajadora que además sufre la violencia política, económica y policial de una ultraderecha tan embrutecida como siempre.




Frente a ese presente que nos pretenden imponer, la CNT de Madrid empieza a imaginar nuestro futuro. Pero no desde posiciones vagas o de ensoñaciones improductivas: poniendo en orden nuestras prioridades, tácticas y finalidades, siempre en consonancia con la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo a la que orgullosamente nos adherimos, y que lleva más de un siglo estando donde tiene que estar: en la lucha.




Si quieres participar y construir también sindicalismo de base, no esperes más y afíliate. Si no vives en Madrid hay un cada vez mayor número de sindicatos de la CNT repartidos por todo el territorio. 

Rechaza con nosotras su presente: imaginemos nuestro futuro.

author: EDRi
title: New report documents authoritarian use of technology across the globe
content:
Privacy International's latest report documents how states are deploying authoritarian technology to stifle dissent, assert control and diminish human rights. The report conveys how surveillance technologies are being expanded and entrenched with the purpose of exerting control over entire populations and/or specific groups of people such as journalists and human rights defenders.

By Privacy International (guest author) · November 19, 2026

EDRi-member Privacy International (PI) have been observing and monitoring an increase in states’ adoption of authoritarian practices and policies. These practices are facilitated by new and emerging technologies or embodied in their very deployment to stifle dissent, assert control and diminish human rights. These digital technologies, such as facial recognition, social media monitoring, spyware, and more, are being deployed — both online and offline — by authoritarian and democratic regimes alike. PI have coined the term ‘authoritarian use of technology’ to describe this global phenomenon.

PI believes that the authoritarian use of technology goes beyond the unlawful use or abuse of technologies by states that the organisation has been monitoring and exposing for years. Authoritarian use of tech results in a systematic undermining of democratic principles, erosion of the rule of law, exertion of significant social and political control, or normalisation of the surveillance of individuals and their communities – particularly those already at risk.

These technologies are being expanded and entrenched with the purpose of exerting control over entire populations and groups of people at risk, such as human rights defenders (HRDs), journalists, lawyers, activists, dissidents and those from minority ethnic, national and religious backgrounds. This is being done to target, persecute or ostracise them. This ultimately creates a ‘chilling effect’, spreading a fear of reprisal, which serves not only to infringe upon the rights of certain individuals, but of whole communities and populations. In turn, this has a corrosive effect on democratic institutions, mechanisms of accountability, oversight and redress, and the fabric of open societies.

In their new report, PI examine the use of five technologies: facial recognition technology, mobile phone extraction, spyware, social media and intelligence monitoring, and mass communications surveillance. The report also provides several cross-cutting themes emerging from the authoritarian use of these technologies on human rights. These include: a systemic interference with the right to privacy, the erosion of and chilling effect on enjoyment of broader fundamental rights and freedoms, the disproportionate or discriminatory targeting of certain groups in society, the absence of clear legal basis, effective safeguards, and independent oversight, and lastly, the lack of accountability of private sector actors.

Facial recognition technology (FRT) is a technology that uses a camera to capture images of people’s faces and then extracts and processes their biometric data to verify an individual or identify a match against an existing image. The report collates examples of how governments and law enforcement are deploying FRT at protests to identify, monitor and track protesters either openly or surreptitiously, and even banning wearing face coverings at protests to facilitate it. The report also features case studies of FRT projects in the UK, Israel and the Occupied Palestinian Territories, and Brazil.

PI’s report includes a chapter on mobile phone extraction, which documents the technology being deployed to gather information and intelligence about activists, journalists, political dissidents, and migrants, which they believe to constitute an authoritarian use of the technology. Our electronic devices, such as our mobile phones and tablets, contain huge amounts of information and sensitive data about our lives. Mobile phone extraction involves extracting data from an individual’s device, or from the cloud services they use, including device information, photos, videos, audio recordings, notes, documents and apps used, as well as the messages, call logs and emails they draft, send and receive.

The report also gathers examples of spyware repeatedly being deployed by both authoritarian and democratic governments to conduct secret, intrusive surveillance of journalists, human rights defenders, opposition politicians, their family members and other individuals already at risk of state repression. Spyware is a huge intrusive surveillance technology that can secretly get everything from a person’s phone: messages, photos, contacts, location, microphone, camera, and browsing history, without them ever knowing. The report refers to the NSO Group and The Pegasus Scandal, and examples from across the Gulf countries of Bahrain, United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.

The report also includes social media intelligence monitoring as a tool increasingly being used by governments and non-state actors for exercising authoritarian control. It draws on the US Department of State’s screening and vetting process of student visa applicants to include applicants’ social media, as well as its use to monitor and track government dissent and protestors in Colombia, the UK and Mexico.

Lastly, PI’s report covers the use of mass communications interception as posing one of the most significant intrusions for privacy, as it can be directed not just at specific individuals but at entire populations. Communications interception is the monitoring, interception, collection, preservation and retention of information that has been communicated, relayed or generated over communications networks by a third party such as law enforcement agency, intelligence agency, a private company, or a malicious actor. The report explains how International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) catchers, which function by mimicking nearby mobile cell towers and intercept communications and location data transmitted by personal communication devices, are being used to intercept protester’s communications and devices in the USA and allegedly the UK. The use of Bulk Communications Interception in Libya provides another example of what may be referred to as an authoritarian use of tech.

Across their analysis of states’ deployment of such technologies, PI found that legislative, technical and regulatory safeguards to oversee the deployment of such technologies were weak, incomplete, unenforced, lacking entirely, or even explicitly serving to bolster and uphold their weaponisation as tools of oppression. Therefore, they conclude each chapter with a specific set of safeguards and restrictions pertaining to each technology that are required to restrict their use to ways that comply with human rights law. However, PI also concludes that certain technologies are so inherently intrusive by design that they are incapable of being reconciled with human rights standards. In particular, they believe that live FRT and mass communications interception exemplify this category of disproportionately intrusive technologies.

The collated case studies and examples of how these technologies are being used illustrates that these are not isolated incidents but part of a wider emerging global trend – the rise of the authoritarian use of technology as a phenomenon that is cutting across borders, cultures and jurisdictions.

PI will continue to monitor developments and raise awareness about the intrusive and devastating impact that the authoritarian use of technology can have on the enjoyment of human rights. They will continue to advocate for the necessary safeguards and restrictions that should be implemented to ensure states do not misuse and abuse these technologies.

Contribution by: Sarah Simms, Senior Policy Officer, Privacy International

Privacy International, Global Report on the Authoritarian use of Technology, October 2026

author: Freedom Editor
title: Why anarchists like James Bond
content:
With all our criticism of the franchise’s nationalism and misogyny, we can still enjoy the films and their flawed hero

Yesterday’s article in Freedom caused a stir on publication. When I read it I was determined to write a counter, but in doing so I have to ask myself: why on earth do I enjoy James Bond films?

Some of A. J. Boyer’s criticisms of Bond are sound, so I’m going to try to start with areas where we might find agreement. I should also say that the content of this article includes incidents in the books and films that are offensive. I mention them here to explain in more detail why liking Bond can be more than just problematic.

Around 20 years ago I decided to read Ian Fleming’s original Bond novels. I was shocked by the levels of sexism and racism in the books. On a recent re-read of Live and Let Die the use of the N word and the casual racism through his descriptions of people left me feeling sick. As consumers of culture, we don’t leave our ability to think critically on the shelf when we take the book down to read. We can read something and decide its merits and / or its lack of such. This applies to watching films too. That particular book is disgraceful. You can’t really say it’s just a product of its time. It’s the product of a man who is showing off his racism. A few years ago, elements of Fleming’s work were altered to remove some of the worst offending material. Bizarrely, the alterations didn’t include changing Bond’s reference to having sex with a particular woman as always containing the ‘sweet tang of rape’ and referring to homosexuality as a ‘stubborn disability’. There’s still much to hate about his writing despite the updating and there’s no defence for it.

I won’t include a list of all the disgusting moments in his writing but the levels of it go far beyond what occurs in the films. In the film version of Goldfinger, Bond forces himself on the ludicrously named Pussy Galore. Fleming’s book goes further and describes her as a lesbian. By the end of both the book and the film, Bond and Galore are an item. In the book, Bond has convinced her that her sexuality was an error on her part, so masculine and amazing is he.

Fleming does everyone a disservice in The Spy Who Loved Me by presenting the entire story from a female gaze; something he really isn’t equipped to do. Presented in first person, through the eyes of the character, Vivienne Michel, the novel includes her being confronted by two mobsters who break into her motel with the intention of robbing her and sexually assaulting her. Bond comes to the rescue and she enters a sexual relationship with him. Fleming includes Vivienne explaining how she rejected the brutality of the mobsters but likes the brutality of Bond. It’s another difficult read among many.

So, there’s an awful lot of reasons to dislike James Bond. Not just the character but the original novels in general. The character may be flawed but that shouldn’t mean the novels have to be. But they are. Fleming made them like that and if you tried to remove all the terrible content, some of the novels simply wouldn’t exist.

However, Andrew makes a point that I fundamentally disagree with. He states that “the James Bond franchise presents a character that is so antithetical to anarchist values, that it becomes impossible to take seriously”. Here’s the thing, though: I don’t take the films seriously. I take them as a bit of entertainment. The films are fun, silly and adventurous. The character is utterly ridiculous and horrible. He stands against everything I agree with. But Bond exists in a strange world. It is a fantastical world in many ways. It’s a world closer to science fiction than reality. The laser beam heading to Sean Connery’s crotch in Goldfinger, the invisible car in Die Another Day, Pierce Brosnan using a parachute to surf a tsunami in the Arctic without a jacket of any sort; the list of nonsense in these films is massive.

We should also note that, as the franchise has been going for over 60 years, it also provides an interesting lens to societal views throughout time. The insistence that Timothy Dalton’s Bond only stick to one sexual relationship in 1987’s The Living Daylights is the franchise’s direct response to concerns around HIV and AIDS. In more recent films, Bond is constantly criticised for his behaviour by his superiors. He doesn’t change much, but attitudes around him do. He is a much better flawed hero in the films than in the books, because the books themselves are so flawed.

Fleming could actually write well, which is all the more damning. In action scenes, his use of very short sentences encourages the reader to dart through the action. His descriptive powers are often dense as he shows off his own extensive knowledge of the world. It would be wrong to say that he couldn’t write. It’s just that he wrote some utterly appalling stuff. I don’t want to make a cheap point about Proudhon here but we’ve got some writers like this in our own canon. Interestingly, Fleming didn’t like the violence of the films, in particular the way Bond seems to relish killing people. Prior to the films he wrote From a View to a Kill, which sees the character agonise over being a sniper. It focuses on the process of going from getting that view of the intended victim through a telescopic lens, to then actually pulling the trigger. As the theme song to the film version of Casino Royal puts it, “when you take a life, do you know what you give?” When From a View to a Kill was chosen as inspiration for a film version in 1985, the word ‘from’ was omitted from the title and the subject matter changed. It is a rare moment where Fleming’s Bond is relatable, in a way.

I’m not here to defend Bond as a character and I’m certainly not here to defend Ian Fleming. I’m here to answer the argument that we can’t simply dismiss Bond as entertainment. I agree, we can’t. But we also can’t assume that every anarchist dislikes (or ought to dislike) Bond. We can’t assume that anarchists who do enjoy Bond films are simply consuming this stuff without thinking. As someone who started watching the films from a very young age—prior to the invention of ITV 2—they were a rare treat. We would go to school the next day and whatever had been shown would be the talk of the playground. I grew up with it. I grew up recognising the character was unpleasant.

There isn’t even a quantum of solace for the patriots who believe in Bond’s view of the world, as Briain’s influence fades around them. But I grew up enjoying the adventure, the wonderful music, the sci-fi gadgets, the locations I’ll probably never get to see in person. Those are the reasons I’m excited to see the next James Bond film. I’ll be keeping my critical thinking with me when I watch it.

author: ROAPE
title: Statement of the Finishers Revolutionary Movement
content:
At the beginning of this year, young Ugandans (activists, researchers, academics and lawyers) came together under one roof to confront a question that could no longer be postponed: what becomes of Uganda after the sham elections of January 2026?




With the possibility of Muhoozi Kainerugaba succeeding his father, we gathered around a simple conviction: Uganda must not be handed from one generation of the same ruling family to another. Succession is not liberation. Changing the face at the top while preserving the same machinery of patronage, militarism and corruption is not the future Uganda deserves.




Under the name Finishers Revolutionary Movement, we committed ourselves to organizing Ugandans to reject this succession project and to take up the unfinished work of national democratic liberation.




What we stand for




The Finishers is more than a name. It is an idea: that Uganda’s liberation cannot remain an unfinished historical promise, and that our generation has a responsibility to finish the task. That means we will:







End dictatorship.




Dismantle systems of patronage and impunity.




Reclaim democratic power for the people.




Build a country capable of true economic independence.







What have we done




Since the beginning of the year, we have been organizing, teaching and rallying people to confront injustice and corruption and to recover the spirit of resistance that every generation of Ugandans has inherited. We have reminded our people that oppression survives not only through the violence of the state, but also through fear, silence and the belief that nothing can change.




Because political freedoms in Uganda have been brutally restricted, we have had to organize with caution. Much of our work has been quiet and covert, because even the ordinary act of bringing Ugandans together has become dangerous.




Why we write in mourning




In the last month, the state has descended on the Finishers with an iron hand. Three of our comrades have been arrested or disappeared.







Praise Aloikin 

was arrested, later released on court bail, and continues to face the state through an ongoing court case.




Byakika Abubaker 

and 

David Musiri 

have been taken, and their whereabouts remain unknown.







We mourn them. We fear for them. We are angry.




Yet we refuse to let their disappearance become the disappearance of an idea. The state may arrest a Finisher. It may abduct a Finisher. It may intimidate a Finisher. But it cannot arrest the hunger for freedom that brought us together.




We are Finishers. We are not terrorists. We are young Ugandans who looked at the country we are inheriting and decided we cannot remain spectators to its destruction. We chose to organize. We chose to resist. And we choose to continue.




Our demands







That the state immediately disclose the whereabouts of Byakika Abubaker and David Musiri, and return them safely to their families.




That the state end enforced disappearances and abductions of Ugandans for their political beliefs and organizing.




That the state stop criminalizing the right to organize, assemble and hold political ideas.




That Praise Aloikin be afforded a fair process, and that the case against her be dropped.







Our appeal to the people of Uganda




Do not leave the Finishers alone. Protect your own. Protect the people who are standing up for the country we all claim to love.




When a Finisher is taken, ask where they are. When a family is left searching for a disappeared son or daughter, stand with that family. When the state attempts to criminalize an idea, refuse to repeat its lies. When fear tells you to look away, remember that the person taken today could be your neighbour, your child, your brother, your sister, or you tomorrow.




The Finishers belong to the people, and so does the idea. You do not have to carry our name to carry it. You do not have to stand where we stand to believe that dictatorship must end. You do not have to be an activist to understand that Uganda cannot be inherited like a family estate




Our resolve




We do not know what the state will do next. We know only that repression is meant to make us disappear one by one, to isolate us from each other and to convince Uganda that resistance is futile. We refuse that outcome.




The disappearance of our comrades has deepened our grief, but it has also clarified our resolve. We will remember those who have been taken. We will stand with their families. We will demand their return. And we will continue the work they were part of.




Because the Finishers are more than their members. The Finishers are an idea, and an idea whose time has come cannot be disappeared.




Protect the people. Protect the idea. Protect the future.

title: A palavra semente nunca morre
content:
Durante o intercâmbio no Assentamento Terra Vista, a conversa com Mestre Isaac revelou um profundo conhecimento sobre os ciclos da natureza e o manejo da terra. Ele explicou que a lua orienta todo o plantio: na lua crescente, tudo o que se planta cresce; na minguante, o que se planta é guardado, dá pouco, mas o pouco serve para guardar semente. A lua nova, por sua vez, significa força — é o momento de plantar raízes como mandioca, cacau, laranja e café, pois são bens de raiz.




Isaac ensinou que a mandioca, na lua nova, deve ser picada e deixada na sombra para secar o leite antes de ir à terra, senão a terra puxa o leite e ela não carrega; na lua crescente, três guias após a nova, planta-se e ela cresce comprida, sem curvas. Ele destacou a importância de se aliar à natureza: na horta, não bate veneno, e para controlar lagartas usa casca de ovo em gravetos, pois a lagarta se identifica como ovo e não bota mais no local.




Também falou da diversidade: plantar quatro ou cinco qualidades de feijão juntas faz uma carregar mais que a outra, quebra a praga e enriquece o alimento. É preciso ter variedades, capim santo, cidreira, erva-doce, tudo que existe. Por fim, Isaac refletiu que semear é semear semente e conhecimentos: “vocês vieram de lá para cá com esse objetivo, e nós passamos os nossos daqui para lá. A palavra semente nunca morre.”

author: Unknown
title: Kalkan: The women's freedom movement provides leadership to the entire struggle
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave a lengthy interview to Medya Haber TV.




In the third and last part of this lengthy interview, he spoke about the importance of the women's movement, the PKK and the international situation.




Part one of the interview can be read 

here

, and the second 

here

.




I

t seems that there are people around the world raising their voices against this situation. Developments are taking place in this direction. The left has returned to power in Brazil. In Serbia, the side supported by the student movement came to power. Trump also lost. There are protests on the streets of Europe every day. How should we interpret these developments in the context of your latest assessment?




Recently, I have been thinking about certain things. Why have they destroyed Iran and Ukraine to such an extent? They also destroyed Syria. I remember the period when efforts were being made to develop Syria. A great deal of capital had been invested, and construction was taking place. This is the nature of the system. It destroys everything and then creates new business opportunities for itself through reconstruction. Naturally, while reconstruction takes place, the owners of capital add billions to their existing billions. They exploit people to such an extent and make enormous profits. Soon, for example, the reconstruction of Iran and Ukraine will begin. The monopolies will profit. They will make unprecedented profits from rebuilding Ukraine. New weapons will also be manufactured to replace those used in its destruction, and the monopolies of the arms industry will profit as well. This situation demonstrates more clearly than anything else the nature of the existing system, the system of power and the state, and the point it has reached under capitalist modernity. It is a system capable of launching even more severe attacks. Its internal contradictions and conflicts have become so deep.




Their greed for profit is so powerful that they are prepared to carry out every kind of attack to make more money and seize what others possess. Do you know what frightens them? Two things. The first is the fear of the revolutionary struggle of the peoples. They fear that if they fight among themselves, society might take advantage of the situation, develop consciousness, organise itself and enter into a revolutionary democratic struggle. They fear that an alternative capable of overthrowing them might emerge. That is their first fear. The October Revolution of 1917 instilled this fear in them. Earlier revolutionary attempts also did so. Many revolutionary developments throughout the twentieth century reinforced it. Today, they calculate this possibility every day. They live in fear. The second thing they fear is the weapons they have created. For example, we have been saying that the Third World War has been continuing for 30 or 35 years. It is not as intense or decisive in military terms as the First World War. Nor is it like the Second World War. Why? Because it cannot be. They cannot conduct the Third World War in that way. If they did, those launching the attacks would not only destroy their opponents but also destroy themselves.




The weapons they would use have reached a level where they threaten to destroy nature, the Earth, humanity, all living beings and the planet itself. That is the point we have reached. It is this fear that prevents them from escalating the war further. Some people say, "The military dimension is weak. These are preparations for the Third World War. The Third World War will come." The Third World War is already taking place. As we say in Kurdish to such people, "Rojbaş", meaning "Good morning!" It has been going on for 30 or 35 years. There will not be a war like the First or Second World War. That will not happen. Anyone who attempts such a thing would have to be considered completely insane. It would lead humanity towards extinction. Recently, people who do not seem entirely rational have risen towards positions of power. Naturally, humanity has experienced great fear in many areas. That is what was actually described as the rise of the right. There is no such thing as simply the rise of the right. What is rising is this danger. The system of capitalist modernity has reached that point. For the time being, they are still exercising some restraint. We should recognise that. But nobody really knows how long this can continue.




'We must resist this system'




The issues we have mentioned are connected to war. That is why I am raising them. They are connected to the war that has continued for 35 years. Its centre is the Middle East. The war between Iran and the United States and Israel continues. It continues at a low intensity. It has not stopped. There are claims that it will expand and that attacks will increase. We do not know what will happen. Ukraine was also a very important area between Asia and Europe. It was a northern energy corridor, an alternative to the route south of the Mediterranean. They acted to cut off that route. In the south, meanwhile, the war continues in the Middle East. Developments around the world are connected to this. The politics of war that threaten humanity have genuinely suffered a setback in recent elections. This is one dimension through which these developments should be assessed. The elections in Israel and the United States can be interpreted in this way. Developments stretching from Brazil to Serbia also show that democratic left-wing forces have become more effective. These forces exist, and similar developments can be seen in many other areas.




In Germany, the Left Party also won in Berlin. They are trying to prevent it from taking power. The existing state treats democratic, left-wing and socialist forces in a manner similar to its treatment of the fascist right-wing movement. But the main response came from young people. It began in France and spread to Italy, the Netherlands, Germany and everywhere else. It appealed to all sections of society. These were university students and secondary school students. What is particularly interesting is that they turned resistance into a social movement. They extended their leadership to other sections of society. They demonstrated something important: there will always be people who resist this system. No matter how extensively special warfare policies are employed, no matter what measures are taken to prevent different sections of society from opposing the system, some people will still break through that barrier, overcome special warfare and resist the system, raising the banner of resistance. The current situation has demonstrated this. I would like to make one final point on this subject. There are many issues that deserve further assessment and discussion.




'Left-wing and democratic forces are not doing enough'




These events, the developments we have discussed, have taught us something. In reality, it is not that there is some unstoppable rise of the right or that society is incapable of recognising what the forces of capital and the capitalist system are doing. We should not simply say, "They work very hard, their words and actions gain support in society, and that is why they win elections and threaten to come to power in Europe." What should we say instead? The truth is that left-wing and democratic forces are not working hard enough. They are insufficiently organised. We must recognise our own shortcomings. Those who call themselves democrats and socialists must engage in self-criticism. They are not doing enough to raise society's awareness. They are not sufficiently connected to society; they have become detached from it. They do not go among the people. They are too rigid and dogmatic. They cannot convince people or inspire confidence. They have almost reached a point where they operate within the existing system.




This is a very bad situation. The elections demonstrated it, and the resistance of young people demonstrated it as well. If there were genuinely a correct understanding, effective organisation and a determined struggle, the system of capitalist modernity could be exposed everywhere. An alternative democratic society system and the struggle for a democratic society could develop everywhere, gain supporters and become a mass movement. What is needed, therefore, is correct consciousness, a correct programme, appropriate strategies and tactics, and, of course, courageous and self-sacrificing efforts. If those who call themselves intellectuals, politicians and artists, those who claim to be the pioneers, the spirit and the consciousness of these societies, of the people and the oppressed, fulfil their duties and responsibilities, everything can develop successfully.




The anti-capitalist struggle can develop effectively everywhere, overcome capitalism and bring it to an end. In fact, capitalism has survived longer than it should have. It should never have reached this point. A hundred years ago, at the beginning of the twentieth century, revolutionaries said that prolonging its existence would be a catastrophe. It should already have been overcome. It survived for another century, and those responsible for creating an alternative, including socialist forces, bear significant responsibility for this. If they recognise and understand this and successfully fulfil their responsibilities as pioneers, it will be possible to overcome a system that threatens nature, society and humanity through such devastating warfare. Our call is therefore to develop this consciousness and struggle more strongly in every sphere.




You drew attention to the Dersim massacre. Of course, in response to these attacks, a major struggle was launched under the leadership of the PKK in 1978, and the values you have highlighted were created through the sacrifice of martyrs. As we approach its 48th anniversary, how should we understand this historical reality, and how should we assess its significance?




Yes, this is something we have always emphasised. The PKK is a movement of leadership and martyrs. What does this mean? It is not simply propaganda. It has a meaning and value rooted in real historical experience.




What it means is this: from its smallest steps to its greatest achievements, from its very first words to the entirety of its thought and action, everything was brought into being under the leadership of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan]. Leader Apo's creative thinking, labour, efforts and will made all these developments possible. Leader Apo became a leader through struggle, hard work and the creation of progress. It did not happen because someone simply bestowed such a title upon him. Nor was it a matter of assigning him a particular position. It did not happen behind a desk either. Starting from nothing, he carried out the work and struggle that gave rise to some of the most meaningful and significant developments in history. Through resistance everywhere — in the country, abroad and in İmralı prison — he developed and brought forth the reality of leadership. This must be properly understood. The reality of leadership is the greatest value created by the PKK and through the PKK's struggle. It has addressed the most significant deficiency of the Kurdish people.




Today, this has given rise to a development that extends beyond the borders of Kurdistan and meets a need felt by all oppressed peoples. The reality of leadership has truly become the source of intellectual and problem-solving power that points the way towards the liberation of all oppressed peoples.




The Kurds know this well. They have understood it and embraced it. We believe this will always remain the case. From one generation to the next, Kurdish youth will understand this value more deeply and comprehensively. They will defend it more strongly and follow and implement the truth of leadership with greater success.




Leader Apo said, "The PKK is the Party of Martyrs." He stated that the martyrs exist and live on in the form of the PKK. He described the PKK as the embodiment of the memory of Haki Karer. Indeed, from its very first steps up until the decision to end its organisational existence, every development took place along the line of martyrdom. It was created through struggle along this line. It was built through the sacrifice of martyrs and the shedding of blood. We are not talking about hundreds, nor thousands, but tens of thousands. And these martyrs are not exclusively men. Women took the lead in this struggle. Women demonstrated the greatest determination in fighting. They did so in the mountains, in prison and through social work. In this respect, the PKK became a movement defined by the reality of its martyrs.




Indeed, at the congress held in May 2025, where the PKK's organisational existence was formally dissolved, the congress entrusted the values it had created to the people. Above all, it entrusted the reality of leadership and martyrdom to the people on this basis. It entrusted these values to the martyrs. It said: "Understand the line of leadership and martyrdom correctly. Always uphold it. Never abandon or break away from this line."




This was very important. This process is continuing. Over the past three months, hundreds of comrades who had fallen as martyrs during the previous five or six years but whose deaths had not yet been publicly announced were declared as martyrs in Bakur (North Kurdistan), Başur (South Kurdistan), Rojhilat (East Kurdistan), Rojava (West Kurdistan) and abroad. These announcements are still continuing in Rojhilat. It is becoming clear that these individuals are the living realities of this movement.




The PKK brought the Kurdish people from the brink of extinction to liberation




The people do not say that these are someone else's martyrs or someone else's children. They embrace them as their own martyrs. Our martyrs embody a reality that raises awareness, organises, builds society and creates a sense of nationhood.




The democratic nation line is developing, taking shape and coming to life under the leadership of the martyrs. The reality of the martyrs is what raises consciousness, educates, organises, and instils courage and self-sacrifice.




Therefore, alongside the leadership, the reality of the martyrs represents the most vibrant and enduring expression of the values created by the PKK. It has always been this way, and it will remain so.




The leadership values created by Leader Apo and our heroic martyrs will continue to live on in Kurdish society, in the free existence of the Kurdish people and in the development of a Kurdish democratic nation. They will continue to represent these realities. Without them, it would not be possible for Kurdish identity to exist.




The PKK has promoted many values. It brought the people back to life from their deathbed. We call it a resurrection movement. It brought the dead back to life. It brought the people from a point of complete annihilation, from a state of having been reduced to nothing, towards liberation.




It brought them from the most extreme conditions of enslavement to an awareness and will for freedom, and ultimately to living freely. By overcoming the threat of annihilation under genocide in Kurdistan, it made free existence possible. It became the creator of all developments and values in the name of freedom. As Leader Apo once said, the PKK is an endless novel, a poem, a song. It will always remain so. It continues. Its organisational existence may come to an end. The Kurdish people may continue their struggle for freedom and develop their democracy through different organisational forms, strategies and political approaches. But all of this will take place on the foundations of the values created by the PKK.




At this point, it was the PKK that laid the foundations for free existence and life. It therefore became an eternal light that will never be extinguished. And it will always remain so. Undoubtedly, another hugely significant achievement of the PKK was the women's freedom revolution: the development of the women's freedom movement and struggle.




Women played a leading role in the popular uprisings (

serhildan

). The women's freedom movement provided the ideological and organisational leadership of the entire struggle. Women both took the lead and guided the movement towards what it considered the correct path. They also instilled courage and a spirit of self-sacrifice. They became the guarantee of victory and the creators of success.




They brought about the emergence of a Kurdish society liberated along the lines of women's freedom. They challenged and broke the male backwardness, domination and individualism that had persisted throughout history. The struggle continues on this basis today.




27 November marks the 48th anniversary of the PKK's founding. 25 November, meanwhile, is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. It is an important and deeply meaningful day, one directly connected to the founding of the PKK. The PKK challenged and broke patriarchal mentality, systems, emotions and ways of thinking. On the basis of women's freedom, it brought about the rebirth and development of both women and men.




This was not merely a struggle against violence. It genuinely enabled the strongest development and realisation of a freedom revolution. It transformed the struggle against violence towards women into a women's freedom revolution. It elevated it to the level of a women's freedom revolution that leads all democratic and social revolutions. This, too, is an extremely important value.




Today, women everywhere are making statements and raising their voices on 25 November to protest patriarchal male violence and to proclaim their demands for an independent stance and a free life. I salute all these efforts and struggles. I truly believe that these occasions should prompt a much deeper examination of patriarchal mentality.




I also call on all men to distance themselves from violence — particularly violence against women — which is the starting point of their own enslavement, and to critically examine their own attitudes and behaviour.

title: Women call for closure of Silopi Thermal Power Plant
content:
The Free Women’s Movement (TJA) held a press conference about the Silopi Thermal Power Plant, owned by the Ciner Group and located between the towns of Bêspin and Gite in the Silopi (Silopya) district of Şirnak (Şirnex). The statement, attended by numerous women and representatives of democratic organisations, drew attention to the plant’s effects on the environment and public health.




Reading the statement, Dilan Elçi, co-chair of the Şirnak branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), said that the right to clean air, water and soil was being violated by coal mining activities on Mount Cudi and the thermal power plant. Stating that the exploitation of nature and the oppression of women stem from the same patriarchal and capitalist mindset, Dilan Elçi said environmental destruction directly affects women’s livelihoods, economies and social lives as well.




Dilan Elçi stated that sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, dust and heavy metals emitted from the plant’s chimney pose a danger to human health and other living beings. She called for the plant’s impacts to be investigated through independent scientific research and for the findings to be made public.




Emphasising that peace with nature is also a fundamental issue within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Dilan Elçi called for coal mining activities on Mount Cudi to be halted and for the Silopi Thermal Power Plant to be shut down completely.




The statement concluded with chants of “Bê xezayê jiyan nabê” (“There can be no life without nature”) and “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (“Woman, life, freedom”), followed by a sit-in protest.

title: Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.
content:
Legendary animal liberationist Barry Horne honoured by Northants Sabs.




Just weeks after publishing damning footage of the 

Quorn Hunt killing a fox and training hounds

 to attack, saboteurs descended upon their prestigious opening meet – and completely ruined it.




Quorn Killers and Horne Haunts Quorn. Banners proudly displayed by Northants Sabs at the Quorn killers opening meet, 6 November, 2026. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.




The day saw violence and abuse by the hunt, and resulted in the arrest of a terrierman who attempted to flee from police.




The day was dedicated to Barry Horne, a legendary activist who made the ultimate sacrifice for animal liberation.




Barry was involved in numerous daring rescue operations, helping to free animals destined for experimentation. He died following a series of hunger strikes intended to pressure Tony Blair’s Labour government over its promise to hold an inquiry into vivisection.




Barry Horne, 17 March 1990, rescuing 82 beagle puppies and 26 rabbits from Harlan Interfauna in Huntingdon. The site is now associated with MBR Acres Ltd, and the long-running Camp Beagle protests against the breeding of dogs for laboratory experiments for the petrochemical, chemical and pharmaceutical industries.




The government reneged on its promise, and animal rights activists reacted with fury in Barry’s name, and thousands more animals, including cats, rabbits and guinea pigs were liberated by activists during his hunger strikes.




Barry was also formerly a member of Northants Hunt Sabs. He died on November 5, 2001. His death radicalised and mobilised countless more animal liberations in his name. 

In September 2026 multiple dogs were liberated from the MBR site

.




On Friday 6 November 2026, a day after the 25th anniversary of Barry’s death, the Quorn Hunt held their opening meet at its kennels in Kirby Bellars, Leicestershire.




The day did not quite go as they may have planned.




The Quorn Hunt October 2026, kill a fox and use the body to train the hounds. Notice the huntsman blowing for the kill over the hounds as they tear the body apart. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




On the back of the horrendous footage released only weeks earlier, Northants Hunt Sabs, including personal friends of Barry’s, turned out to stop the Quorn Hunt from killing on their watch.




Part time whipper-in and terrier ‘man’ Mickey Vaughn practising for the regional gurning championship.

Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.




Northants Sabs truly smashed the day, hunt tempers flared as sabs arrived at the meet with banners and flags speaking truth about ‘trail hunting’.




Vaughan bravely attacking a woman. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




True to form, the hunters natural default for violence saw sabs attacked and pushed to the ground. Sabs stood their ground following the violent outburst and the hunt was soon put back in their box.




Vaughan being put back into his box. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




Sabs stayed on the hunt throughout the day, leaving huntsman Joe Tesseyman struggling to find opportunities to hunt foxes with saboteurs on his case.




Huntsman Joe Tessyman on the run from sabs and police alike. Image Northants Hunt Sabs




Then, near Cream Gorse, the hunter became the hunted.




A Quorn terrierman was spotted leaving the covert on a quad bike, with officers from Leicestershire Police’s Rural Crime Team in hot pursuit.




The hot pursuit began with a terrierman fleeing from police after leaving the covert. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




Mickey Vaughan, the terrierman and occasional whipper-in, attempted to slow the pursuing officers down by positioning his horse in the road. Police moved him aside and continued after the terrierman on the quad.




The quad overturned, and the terrierman was spotted running up Pasture Lane with a police officer hot on his tail behind.




You can’t park that there, mate. Image Northants Hunt Saboteurs.




Clearly a runner he was not.




He was promptly caught, cuffed and arrested.




At first I was all like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




We couldn’t possibly comment on what the arrest relates to and will not speculate, but lets hope they throw “obstructing an officer” at him whilst they are at it. Same goes for Vaughan who attempted to prevent the officer from pursuing the masked terrierman.




Then I was like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs




Meanwhile the mounted field dwindled out, no doubt many of whom left thoroughly embarrassed by the thuggish behaviour of this supposed-prestigious hunt. Remind us how much they pay in cap money for a day watching foxes being ripped apart?




By about 2pm, the hounds were back in the kennels. Job nicely done.




For a hunt that prides itself on centuries of prestige, royal connections and aristocratic tradition, this was a spectacularly undignified display which truly showed these thugs for what they truly are.




And there is something beautifully fitting about the contrast. The Quorn’s history, steeped in privilege. Its followers have included royalty, including the present King Charles III when he was Prince of Wales.




The contrast is staggering. The selflessness and sacrifice of a man devoted to protecting animals, versus the brutality of those who only know how to harm them.




Barry Horne dedicated his life to challenging the exploitation of animals, enduring imprisonment and ultimately dying following his hunger strikes.




Twenty five years after his death, former comrades were still out in the fields standing up for the animals who cannot defend themselves from this horrific abuse inflicted by these entitled, and sadistic monsters.




The Quorn had its opening meet, but Barry Horne had the last word.




HORNE HAUNTS QUORN.




A spokesperson for Northants Hunt Saboteurs said:







“The recent crushing of the Quorn Foxhound’s opening meet was by no means made successful by luck. This was a deliberate and direct message from Northants sab volunteers who returned retribution. This was less for the cameras and more action, as after all, how much more evidence do you need?




“And how does it get any more damning than catching a hunt on camera training their hounds to kill foxes, having a terrierman ragging at a foxes body and then a huntsman blowing for the kill directly over the hounds as they do so?




“This is what the Quorn were caught doing on 16th October 2026.




“With this Labour government dragging their heels in taking action to ban these sick bastards, it is time for us as activists to step it up a gear and to take the fight harder to the abusers.




“If we don’t then we risk allowing yet another government to fail us, but more importantly, to fail the animals.




Our time is now”







Northants Hunt Saboteurs dedicated their hit to Barry Horne.

support Northants sabs here

.

Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.

 appeared first on 

Hunt Saboteurs Association

author: Barracuda Media
title: Cartel e trabalho escravo: as acusações contra a Cutrale que o Deutsche Bank ignorou
content:
Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial 

Inside Deutsche Bank

 

aqui.


































Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial 

Inside Deutsche Bank

 

aqui.













Quando o bilionário José Luís Cutrale faleceu em 2022, não faltaram obituários e reportagens elogiosas ao empresário. Dono de uma das maiores empresas do agronegócio brasileiro, a Cutrale, ele foi descrito como “

rei da laranja

” e exaltado como a “

primeira estrela global do agro brasileiro

”. Para seus herdeiros, José Luís deixou uma fortuna pessoal estimada em quase 2 bilhões de dólares e uma companhia responsável pela produção de algo entre um quarto e um terço do suco de laranja consumido no planeta.




Mas, além dos números impressionantes, Cutrale e sua companhia homônima também acumularam acusações trabalhistas ao longo das últimas décadas – inclusive de trabalho análogo à escravidão – e foram o alvo central de processos 

judiciais

 e 

administrativos

 pela suposta formação de cartel, dentro e fora do Brasil.




Relatórios internos sigilosos e trocas de e-mails do Deutsche Bank (DB) acessados pela 

Agência Pública

, no entanto, mostram que as suspeitas contra a empresa de suco de laranja e seu dono foram repetidamente amenizadas por funcionários do banco alemão

 – um padrão de comportamento que se repetiu com outros clientes brasileiros de peso implicados em casos polêmicos ou até mesmo acusados de crimes.




Um calhamaço em alemão de 1.148 páginas é o elemento central da história. O relatório de “Conheça Seu Cliente” (Know Your Costumer, ou KYC, na sigla em inglês) sobre a família Cutrale, suas empresas e suas ligações revela que o banco alemão tinha conhecimento dos problemas e polêmicas ligadas ao magnata do suco de laranja, mas que optou por diminuir sua relevância, preferindo destacar que Cutrale “goza de reputação internacional impecável” e seu suco de laranja é “consumido no mundo todo”.
















Relatório do Deutsche Bank lista empresas ligadas à família Cutrale que eram clientes do banco




O material é parte do 

Inside Deutsche Bank

, investigação transnacional da qual a 

Pública

 faz parte, baseada no vazamento de mais de 15 milhões de documentos do banco, obtido pelo jornalista indiano Josy Joseph e por Khadija Sharife, jornalista investigativa sul-africana. O projeto tem coordenação global da Barracuda Media e do Centro Lationamericano de Periodismo de Investigación (CLIP) na região.




Os documentos vazados para o projeto mostram, 

segundo detalhado em diversas reportagens

, como o banco alemão repetidamente ignorou sinais de alerta de possível lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções e como descumpriu suas próprias regras para clientes poderosos.




Em resposta aos assuntos levantados pelo projeto Inside Deutsche Bank, o banco afirmou que as questões apresentadas pelos jornalistas “remontam a muitos anos atrás, em alguns casos, décadas. Quando pertinente, essas questões foram analisadas na época e discutidas com órgãos reguladores e autoridades competentes, conforme necessário”, afirmou o banco.




“Hoje somos um banco diferente”, acrescentou a instituição.




Além da Cutrale, documentos internos mencionando empresas como BRF e JBS, Vale, 

Banco Safra

, Andrade Gutierrez e Braskem revelam, em diferentes graus, as prioridades do DB e de seus funcionários – mesmo quando as evidências pediam precaução.




A primeira 

reportagem

 da série detalhou uma grande controvérsia em torno do BTG Pactual de André Esteves, com quem o chefe de Commodities do Deutsche Bank se recusou a fazer negócios, chamando-o de “pilantra”. Outros executivos defenderam a relação com o banco, dizendo ser um dos principais clientes do DB no Brasil.




Suco de laranja




A versão do relatório disponível no vazamento é datada de 2018, mas outros documentos internos do Deutsche Bank citam revisões em relatório de KYC sobre a Cutrale pelo menos desde 2015. Esse tipo de relatório costuma ser produzido sempre que um novo cliente vai ser adotado pelo banco – o que ocorreu, no caso da citricultora, em pelo menos 2021. Assim é possível que a instituição já soubesse dos problemas vinculados à empresa desde muito antes.




As mesmas justificativas utilizadas para minimizar os problemas aparecem em outros documentos ao longo dos anos anteriores ao KYC.




O banco sabia, por exemplo, que José Luís Cutrale e sua empresa eram acusados de ganhar espaço no antes disputado mercado produtor de laranja brasileiro por meio de um cartel com outras companhias, que teria segurado os preços do produto e feito com que milhares de citricultores quebrassem e tivessem que deixar o negócio.
















Documento interno do Deutsche demonstra que capivara de Cutrale era conhecida pelo banco




A acusação foi feita por diferentes fontes, como a 

Associação Brasileira de Citricultores

 (Associtrus). Entre a metade dos anos 1990 e 2017, o número de produtores de laranja no país caiu de 26 mil para 5,5 mil, o que causou perdas de ao menos 200 mil empregos. Além disso, em 2010, um fabricante de suco de laranja que teria participado do cartel deu detalhes 

em entrevista

 à Folha de S. Paulo, citando José Luís Cutrale como o articulador do esquema.




A empresa chegou a reconhecer em processo no Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) que fazia parte de um cartel; mas jamais foi condenada judicialmente por isso.




É neste ponto que se apoia o documento do Deutsche Bank. Ele aponta que a Cutrale não foi julgada por formação de cartel e diz que “é improvável que o dono de uma grande corporação brasileira interfira nas operações diárias e se preocupe pessoalmente com uma possível formação de cartel”. O relatório diz que se baseia em um artigo jornalístico, sem revelar qual, para afirmar que “acordos de fixação de preço são prática comum no setor” e que “é estratégia comercial dos agricultores brasileiros acusar o grupo Cutrale de pressionar os preços do suco de laranja”.




O suposto cartel, minimizado pelo DB, foi alvo de uma operação policial em 2006 (Operação Fanta) e de longas batalhas jurídicas e administrativas ao longo dos anos.




Um processo de quase duas décadas no Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) 

foi arquivado

 em 2018, depois da Cutrale outras empresas envolvidas firmarem um acordo em que admitiram participação no cartel

, se comprometeram a cessar as práticas anticompetitivas e concordaram em 

pagar multas

 que somaram mais de R$ 300 milhões.




Ainda tramitaram ações contra a Cutrale no Brasil e na Inglaterra, pleiteando indenizações bilionárias, mas os tribunais consideraram que o caso já 

havia prescrito

.




Há ainda outros dois casos de investigações relacionadas a José Luís Cutrale e sua empresa que são relativizados no relatório.




A primeira tem relação com a Operação Fanta, de 2006, quando jornais noticiaram que uma submetralhadora Uzi, de posse ilegal, 

teria sido

 encontrada na sala da presidência da Cutrale (outras 

matérias

 falam em “sala de um diretor”). Ainda que não tenha havido julgamento contra o empresário quanto a isso – o que o relatório do DB aponta de maneira acertada –, chama a atenção a legitimação da suposta arma ilegal. 

O documento do DB diz que, assim como nos Estados Unidos, no Brasil “as pessoas mais ricas querem se proteger e proteger suas famílias com armas de fogo”.




O outro trecho faz menção a condenações por violações trabalhistas em 1996 e 2004.




Em 2013, a Cutrale foi flagrada em fiscalização que envolveu o 

resgate de 23 trabalhadores

 em situação análoga à escravidão, em caso que fez com que a empresa figurasse na Lista Suja do Trabalho Escravo em 2017.




Mas isso não é citado no relatório datado de 2018.

 Além disso, o documento ressalta que “processos trabalhistas não são incomuns em uma grande empresa com 10.000 funcionários” e que “o Sr. C[utrale] não negocia contratos de trabalho”.




Os questionamentos judiciais quanto à conduta trabalhista da Cutrale, aliás, continuam ocorrendo. Em maio de 2026, a empresa 

foi condenada

 a pagar R$ 1,5 milhão em danos morais coletivos por um juiz do trabalho, depois de acumular mais de 350 autuações trabalhistas entre 2012 e 2024. Alojamentos sem materiais básicos de higiene, práticas irregulares de produtividade e um acidente com óbito na propriedade da gigante do suco de laranja estão entre as constatações que ampararam a decisão.




“A postura da ré configura nítido dumping social, pois, ao sonegar investimentos essenciais em segurança e saúde, obtém vantagem competitiva ilícita frente às empresas que se esforçam para cumprir a legislação”, afirmou o magistrado na sentença.




A Cutrale recorreu da decisão, mas o Tribunal Regional do Trabalho da 15ª Região manteve os principais pontos em 

acórdão

 publicado no final de outubro. Os embargos de declaração apresentados pela empresa ainda não foram julgados.




Os documentos disponíveis no vazamento indicam que, apesar de saber dos problemas relacionados à Cutrale, o Deutsche Bank manteve as empresas ligadas à família como clientes no mínimo até 2019. Um documento datado de julho daquele ano mostra que José Luis foi reclassificado como “cliente de alto risco”.




Contas

 

offshore

 

na Libéria




A relação entre a multinacional agrícola e o Deutsche Bank tem ainda outros capítulos, revela o material vazado. Em 2011, uma troca de emails entre funcionários do banco alemão mostra que a família Cutrale, que já tinha vínculo com a instituição à época, procurou o DB com o objetivo de estabelecer uma operação de negociação de 

commodities

 na Suíça por meio de uma de suas subsidiárias, a Continental Trading.




Devido a conflitos sobre quem deveria atender à potencial conta e à indefinição sobre o país de domicílio do beneficiário final da empresa, o negócio quase subiu no telhado, como demonstra um email enviado por Thomas Bowers, à época chefe do setor de Private Wealth Management (que cuida de grandes fortunas) do DB nas Américas. Ele teve que pressionar seus colegas para fazer a negociação andar.




“A família Cutrale ficou inicialmente bastante impressionada com nossa equipe. Devo dizer que essa impressão está se dissipando rapidamente. (…) Se conduzido adequadamente, este poderia se tornar um importante relacionamento comercial em qualquer padrão global. Se mal conduzido, teremos uma retirada educada e discreta. A família está pronta para seguir em frente e não entende o motivo da demora”, afirma Bowers, que pediu agilidade para seus colegas na resolução do problema.




Bowers, aliás, foi 

peça-central

 nos controversos empréstimos concedidos pelo Deutsche Bank ao presidente norte-americano Donald Trump, que fizeram com que o banco alemão fosse investigado pela justiça dos EUA. Ele cometeu 

suicídio

 em 2019.
















Relatório interno do Deutsche traz uma série de offshores da família com sede na Libéria




Os arquivos disponíveis no vazamento não permitem uma compreensão completa sobre o desfecho da negociação em questão. Revelam, porém, a existência de uma complexa teia de subsidiárias 

offshore

 da família Cutrale sediadas na Libéria com contas dentro do Deutsche Bank. As empresas, mostram outros documentos, eram ligadas ao transporte marítimo do suco de laranja produzido pela empresa brasileira.




A escolha pela bandeira do país africano nas embarcações é prática comum no mercado de 

commodities

 por conta de normas trabalhistas menos protetivas, flexibilidade regulatória, incentivos fiscais e menor necessidade de transparência. A conduta é criticada por sindicatos de trabalhadores por favorecer a precarização das condições de trabalho.




A criação de uma conta 

offshore

 não significa ilegalidade.




Mas ao menos uma dessas subsidiárias acionou alertas sobre a possibilidade de envolvimento com lavagem de dinheiro (não há clareza se algum alerta se mostrou correto).




O documento aponta que “baseado no nosso conhecimento atual, não podemos descartar que as transações em questão constituam lavagem de dinheiro ou sejam conectadas a um crime antecedente nos termos da Seção 261 do Código Penal Alemão (StGB, na sigla em alemão).”
















Alerta sobre lavagem de dinheiro não foi descartado




Outro lado




A 

Pública

 enviou uma série de perguntas relacionadas ao comportamento do banco e de seus funcionários em casos relativos às empresas citadas nesta e nas demais reportagens do especial 

Inside Deutsche Bank

, tanto para a sede global do banco alemão quanto para a filial brasileira, que respondeu em nota.




“Não comentamos sobre relacionamentos potenciais, anteriores ou atuais com clientes. Temos políticas e controles estabelecidos para garantir o cumprimento dos requisitos legais, regulatórios e internos aplicáveis. O modelo de Três Linhas de Defesa do banco foi concebido para garantir que as avaliações de risco sejam submetidas à revisão e contestação independentes pelas áreas de controle, independentemente da relevância comercial das relações com os clientes.”




A reportagem também contatou a Cutrale, que não respondeu até a publicação.

title: Ozgur Ozel: "Em di Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de cih nagirin"
content:
Serokê Parlamentoyê Numan Kurtulmuş di çarçoveya hevdîtinên ji bo avakirina Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de,  li Enqereyê çû serdana Serokê Giştî yê Partiya NÛ Ozgur Ozel.




Ozgur Ozel piştî hevdîtina bi Kurtulmuş re daxuyaniyeke çapemeniyê da û helwesta partiya xwe ya li ser Komîsyona Çavdêriyê eşkere kir.




Ozgur Ozel destnîşan kir ku desthilat di warê demokratîkbûnê de gavên pêwîst navêje û xala 7emîn a rapora Komîteya Parlamentoyê ya ji bo demokratîkbûnê nayê bicihanîn.




Sedemê redkirinê




Ozel ragihand ku sîstema qeyûman berdewam dike, qeyûm li ser 3 kanalên televîzyonê hatine danîn û biryarên Dadgeha Destûra Bingehîn û Dadgeha Mafên Mirovan a Ewropayê nayên bicihanîn.




Ozel ev yek wekî sedemên cihnegirtina partiya xwe ya di nav Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de destnîşan kir.




Ozgur Ozel da zanîn ku Partiya NÛ dê ji ber van sedeman endaman nede Komîsyona Çavdêriyê ya ku biryar e li Parlamentoyê were damezirandin.




Serokê Giştî yê Partiya NÛ rexne li helwesta hikûmetê girt û diyar kir ku desthilat tenê jibo parastina pêgeha xwe gavên siyasî diavêje û got:







"Tekane tiştê ku di berjewendiya vî welatî de ye, rawestandina vê desthilatê ye. Hinekan tenê ji bo ku desthilata xwe bidomînin her tişt kir. Bila kes li ser pişta me hesaban neke"




Ji bo qonaxên piştî vê yên pêvajoyê, bila kes me tevlî hesabên xwe yên şexsî neke û liser pişta me hesaban daneyne. Ji niha û pê ve bila kes bi hizirkirina li ser me hesaban neke. Bila li gorî hebûn an nebûna me hesabên xwe bikin. Kes nikare kesî bixapîne. Dema hûn li wan deriyan dixin, hûn dê wan sozên ku we berê dabûn bînin bîra xwe. Ez dibêjim em di nava vî karî de nînin."







Serokê Parlamentoya Tirkiyeyê Numan Kurtulmuş di çarçoveya hewldanêndamezirandina Desteya Çavdêriyê de bi serok û nûnerên partiyên AK Partî, MHP, DEMPartî û Rêya Nû re jî hevdîtin kiribû.




Ev deste li gorî Yasaya Çarçoveyê ya Tebaxa 2026an li Parlamentoya Tirkiyeyê têavakirin û ji bo şopandina gavên pêvajoya aştiyê û bêçekbûnê hatiye plankirin lê belêredkirina Partiya NÛ dê bandorê li ser hevsengiya nûnertiya partiyan a di nava desteyêde bike.




"Em di nava vî karî de nînin"




Serokê Partiya NÛ Ozgur Ozel di berdewamiya axaftina xwe de got:







"Ji niha û pê ve eger hûn li cihekî deriyê Partiya NÛ bixin, dema hûn tên li wî derî dixin,hûn dê wan sozên ku we berê dabûn bi cih bînin; ne sozên ku we dane Partiya NÛ lê ez behsa wan sozan dikim ku we li ber komîteyê di girtenameyan de xistine bin îmzeyan. Ez ji wan kesên ku gotin 'em dê di demokratîkbûnê de her tim bi hev re bin' û pişt reparçe dikin re dibêjim. Ez ji wan kesên ku teslîmî burokratên Koşkê bûne re dibêjim. Ez ji wan kesên ku bi zext û zordariyê hewl didin tiştekî bikin re dibêjim, em di nava vîkarî de nînin. 




Ew kesên ku dixwazin em di nava van karan de bin, divê pêşî wan sozên ku di dîrokê dedane vî welatî bi cih bînin. Rapor li wir e, komîte li wir e. Ji niha û pê ve ew kesên ku bi serê xwe lîstikademokrasiyê dilîzin, bila kerem bikin bilîzin. Li wir we partiyeke mixalefetê ya 'meqbûl' jî dît; mixalefeta majesteyan!




Heta ji we tê bi kar bînin. Mixalefeteke ku hatiye hilbijartin, di hilbijartinan de bi serketiye, li kolanan bi deh hezaran kes li pey dimeşin û bi milyonan mirovan li meydanankom dike, dê rewabûnê nede wî zemînê ku hûn lê ne. Bi mixalefeta majesteyan re hûn dikarin li ser kîjan rêyê bixwazin bimeşin."







(AEK/AY)

author: EDRi
title: One year later, a broad coalition tells EU lawmakers: do not simplify away people’s rights with the Digital Omnibus
content:
On 19 November 2025, the European Commission presented the Digital Omnibus as an exercise in simplification. One year later, 100 organisations and individuals from across civil society are warning that simplification is turning into deregulation, with consequences far beyond the usual digital-rights debate.

A new open letter calls on EU lawmakers to protect data protection, privacy and other fundamental rights, rather than weakening them in the name of empty promises of competitiveness and the AI hype.

There are plenty of things about EU digital regulation that could genuinely be simpler: people should not have to fight through endless cookie banners, regulators should cooperate better, businesses should not operate in good faith knowing other companies won’t be held accountable when disrespecting the law…

But cutting red tape and cutting rights are not the same thing. The Digital Omnibus proposed, amongst other, significant changes to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and ePrivacy framework. These affect when information about us is protected, how companies may reuse personal data for AI, safeguards around automated decision-making, access and transparency rights, and protection against unwanted access to our devices.

All of this is happening in a much wider political context. Across different EU policy areas, protections for people, workers, consumers and the environment are increasingly being reopened and deregulated under the language of ‘simplification’ and competitiveness.

One of the clearest examples is AI. Companies developing AI systems want enormous amounts of data. The Digital Omnibus on Data would create a specific route under the GDPR for AI development, training and operation to rely on the so-called legitimate interest legal basis. The existing legal tests would not disappear, but the risk is that large-scale reuse of personal data for AI becomes increasingly normalised, while people are left to find out what happened to their data and try to object afterwards.

This is particularly concerning in a market already dominated by big tech companies with huge advantages in data, infrastructure and capital, which can undermine companies that have invested in more privacy-protective and rights-respecting products and want clear rules and a genuine level playing field.

AI is only one piece of the proposal. Other changes touch sensitive and biometric data, automated decisions, transparency and access rights, and the confidentiality of our devices and communications.

These changes matter differently to different communities. They matter to workers subject to automated management and surveillance, worried about losing their jobs or their tasks becoming even more alienating; patients whose sensitive information needs strong protection; people facing discrimination who rely on transparency and access rights to challenge unfair systems; journalists and human rights defenders who depend on confidential communications; children and young people exposed to commercial tracking; and consumers confronted with companies holding vastly more information and power than they do.

That is why this cannot be treated as a niche dispute, even less when we remember the GDPR is the cornerstone of the EU’s digital rulebook.

To mark the first, and hopefully last, anniversary of the proposal, 100 organisations, academics, researchers, individuals and responsible businesses are coming together around a simple message: the EU can simplify its rules without simplifying away people’s rights.

The open letter calls on the European Parliament and Member States to reject provisions that weaken rights and substantive protections, and to ensure that any evidence-backed genuine problems in the GDPR, ePrivacy or other legislation are addressed through proper democratic processes, backed by evidence, consultation and scrutiny.

Fundamental rights are not red tape, and if we are speaking about simplification, the question should rather be ‘simplification for whom?’
