author: Fraser Needham
title: ISC minister says she was not expecting Kinew’s comments about abolishing the Indian Act
content:
Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty says she was as surprised as anyone when Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew raised the idea of abolishing the Indian Act last month and was hoping for more information on what role the province would play.

“I think it’s interesting to see somebody who’s a provincial premier wanting to frame up that space,” she said. “Clearly, in his role he would have to indicate his responsibility in the provincial seat and how you would serve those off-reserve community members.

“I think that’s the initiative I was hoping to see as a minister coming out of that space because you have to increase the responsibility, the partnership, the role of the provincial government in the path beyond the Indian Act.”

The idea of getting rid of the Indian Act was raised by Kinew during a press conference at the First Nations First Ministers meeting in Ottawa on Oct. 26.

“What you saw was a spontaneous moment where premier Kinew wanted to speak about status. Wanted to speak about the Indian Act.”

The Indian Act, passed in 1876, continues to govern matters of Indian status, First Nations governance, and reserve lands. The federal government has tried, and failed, to abolish it a number of times in the past 50 years.

At a later press conference, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was open to the idea as long as it was co-developed with First Nations and has tasked some of his ministers to look into the issue.

He said he was directing Gull-Masty to chart a path with First Nations on amending or abolishing the act.

Conservative MP Billy Morin says the 2026 federal budget is disappointing on a number of levels.

“This might be the most overrated Prime Minister (Mark Carney) I’ve seen in quite some time,” the MP for Edmonton Northwest said. “Even more overrated than his predecessor (Justin Trudeau). This guy’s apparently a banker, a guy who knows how to do finances.

“He’s running deficits bigger than Trudeau. Bigger deficits than Trudeau and he takes great pride in that?”

The budget projects deficits of well over $50 billion over each of the next five years.

The 2023/24 deficit, the last budget under Trudeau, came in at $61.9 billion and the 2026/27 deficit is projected to be $62.3 billion.

Morin is the Indigenous Services critic for the Conservatives.

The president of the Manitoba Métis Federation says leaving Métis people out of the 2026 federal budget is not a mistake the Carney government can afford to make.

“It shouldn’t be something that we need to worry about whether it’s a budget or not,” David Chartrand said. “It should be automatic. It’s part of the fiduciary responsibility and constitutional responsibility of Canada,” he said.

The 2026 budget makes roughly $50 billion over ten years in investments in Indigenous priorities but makes no mention of Métis-specific investments.

Some have expressed fears the government is returning to a non-distinctions-based funding model that largely focuses on First Nations people.

Chartrand said the government collects billions of dollars in taxes from Métis people every year and it needs to invest that money back in their communities.

Fraser spent the last 20 years working in both print and radio in Saskatchewan – mostly in the northern part of the province. Before joining APTN’s Ottawa bureau, he was news director for the Missinipi Broadcasting Corporation working out of their Prince Albert office. He holds a bachelor of arts degree in political science from Carleton University and a diploma of journalism from Algonquin College.

La brújula loca tiene Norte por Sur y la segunda guerra sigue haciéndose tercera. ¡Tendremos la otra cara de la luna! Con la otra como llegada de todas las novedades. Y ruedan las monedas, maldición esta arca de Noé. A la cara de Franklin se le cae el rayo de su cometa y el verde es de papel ¿Y ese hombre soterrado? Camina entre las raíces del oasis…  Piedra buena es insultado como escombro y habla totalmente, absolutamente, habla por sordo. Sordo por el estruendo de los misiles que entraron por su oreja. Y canta porque cantó y ríe porque rió. Inevitable la razón, pierde su vigencia y el olor de la destrucción de los cuerpos queridos se acerca tanto a los sentidos que podemos ser estrellas. (Sustancia es el desayuno). Tienen modos que no tenemos que esperar. Ese hombre buscó profetas y ninguno se mueve de sus estatuas entonces por buscar comida inventa desayunos de media lunas. author: Sharon Zhang
title: Jeffries Refuses to Say If He Opposes US-Israeli Military Integration Measure
content:
Jeffries and Schumer are already under scrutiny for their vehement pro-Israel views as calls grow for new leadership.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Thursday, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) refused to say whether or not he supports efforts to strip the Pentagon budget bill of a highly controversial provision to integrate the U.S. and Israeli militaries, even as other Democrats unite on the issue.

This week, a group of 12 members of the Senate led by Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) urged congressional leaders to remove the measure mandating the creation of a “U.S.-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative” from the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for 2027. Rep. Ro Khanna (D-California) also said this week that it is one of his top priorities for Congress before the new year.

The issue is time sensitive. The measure is slated for inclusion in the Pentagon budget, which is regarded by many in Congress as a bill that must pass before year’s end.

When asked about the measure and the Van Hollen letter at a press conference on Thursday morning, however, Jeffries dodged the question.

“I haven’t had a conversation with Senator Van Hollen,” Jeffries said. “But what I have said is that things have to dramatically change over in the Middle East.”

“That looks like, as far as I’m concerned, making sure you have a safe and secure Israel, living side by side, as a Jewish and democratic state, with an independent Palestinian state,” he went on. The only legislation that he called out specifically was the West Bank Violence Prevention Act, which has been criticized as insufficient by pro-Palestine advocates, and which Jeffries said he supports.

The military integration measure — Section 219 in the House version and Section 1217 in the Senate — would mandate the creation of an initiative to deeply integrate the U.S. and Israeli military and technology sectors, including in areas like weapons production and autonomous warfare. It is backed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and has faced vehement opposition by critics who say that it inextricably links the U.S. and Israeli military at a time when Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, backing horrific violence in the occupied West Bank, and razing huge swaths of Lebanon.

“As an American, I am outraged by Section 219,” said Khanna. Khanna and Rep. Thomas Massie’s (R-Kentucky) amendment to remove Section 219 was blocked in committee twice this summer. “Who do they think they are? This needs to be the top priority in the lame duck session.”

Jeffries also called for “dramatic change” with the memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the U.S. and Israel, which is set to expire in 2028. However, he did not address President Donald Trump’s announcement last week that the U.S. would stop sending the roughly $4 billion in annual funding called for by the MOU next year. This announcement was already met with skepticism by advocates for Palestinian rights, who pointed out that Section 219 and other measures are slated to deepen the U.S.-Israel relationship in more secretive ways.

The remarks are likely to fuel yet more criticism of Jeffries, who has been under scrutiny in the past week along with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer amid calls for new Democratic leadership. Both Democratic leaders are staunch supporters of Israel, and have broken with large swaths of their caucuses this year in votes on blocking assistance to Israel.

Their continued support of the apartheid state comes as support for Israel among the public has fallen to all-time lows amid its genocide in Gaza, as Americans grow increasingly incensed over the U.S.’s aid to Israel, polls have found. The military integration measure is also extremely unpopular: An August poll found that 61 percent of Americans oppose the proposal, including 78 percent of Democrats.

This week, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont) announced that he is not backing Schumer for Senate leadership when the Democratic caucus votes next month, calling for drastic change. In an interview with The Nation, he cited Schumer’s backing of Israel as a reason to oust him from leadership.

“[I]n this moment in American history, Chuck’s views are way out of touch with where the American people are at — and especially with where [the base of] the Democratic Party is. On issue after issue, I think he is just not in tune with where his constituents are at,” Sanders said.

When asked about the issues in which Schumer differs from the base, Sanders said: “You can start off with U.S. military aid to Israel.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $39,000 in the next 5 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

author: Administrador
title: CINCO GENERACIONES BUSCANDO A JOSÉ MIGUEL. (Respuesta a las solicitudes de entrevistas)
content:
CINCO GENERACIONES BUSCANDO A JOSÉ MIGUEL. (respuesta a las solicitudes de entrevistas)

Así se llama: José Miguel. José Miguel Rodríguez Rodríguez, tiene 29 años y desapareció el 18 de junio de 2026 en Salamanca, Guanajuato, junto con Wendy Ángela Ruiz Luna y Brisa Johana Flores Luna. Hace casi 6 meses.

Hace unos días les conté cómo, en una plática que daba el SubMoisés a la delegación zapatista -como parte de su preparación-, se señalaba que lo más importante era el desaparecido, la desaparecida. La ausencia, pues. E insistía él, el SubMoy, en que esa desaparición era como un hueco, como un hoyo, como un mordisco en la vida de sus familiares y cercanos. Un vacío que no podía ser llenado más que con la presencia de quien faltaba, es decir, con el encuentro del ausente.

Que no había promesa, rollo político, diligencia fiscal, intervención policíaca o ministerial, marcha, mitin, denuncia, conteo, manta, cartel, canto, estadística, grito que pudiera “acompletar” ese faltante.

Y entonces hacía como que era el desaparecido el que hablaba, el que se dirigía a sus familiares, amistades, cercanos. ¿Qué les decía? Se ponía así en el lugar del faltante y veía que no estaba cabal. Que, así como a sus familiares él les faltaba, también a él le hacía falta su familia, su trabajo, su estudio, su amor, sus amigos, su vida pues. A él, a ella, le habían también arrancado un pedazo suyo, de su ser, y le habían dejado un hueco igual de grande, igual de doloroso, igual de angustiante.

Y que él o ella les gritaba que ahí estaba, detrás de esa puerta, de ese cerco, de esa tierra, de esa cárcel. Y se desesperaba porque su voz no llegaba lejos, se ahogaba por el ruido, se perdía entre otros gritos.

Pero, así como quien le busca espera encontrarle, ella o él esperaba ser encontrado. Eso era y es lo importante. Acompletarse. Y le decía a sus familiares que agarraran fuerza y coraje. Y que gritaran también. Ellos para que les escuchara, él o ella para que le encontraran.

1530 hombres, mujeres, otroas, niños, niñas, de hasta 5 generaciones lo escuchaban en silencio. Había ahí hombres y mujeres de más de 70 años, bisabuelos y bisabuelas, la mayoría veteranos y veteranas del alzamiento en 1994 y de la clandestinidad en que se gestó la guerra contra el olvido.

Adultos mayores de 50, que también salieron a pelear, a desafiar, a retar a un sistema, a un Estado, a un gobierno, a un ejército, a una policía, a un sistema judicial, a la historia y al destino, con la juventud y la furia que provoca ser olvidados.

Padres y madres de familia, casadas y solteras, de entre 30 y 40 años, que crecieron en la resistencia y la rebeldía y aprendieron que, organizados, podían vivir dignamente. Son autoridades autónomas, promotores de salud y de educación, milicianas y milicianos, insurgentas e insurgentes, mandos organizativos locales, regionales, de zona y de Inter zona. Parte del todo que es la nueva dirección organizativa zapatista.

Otroas que encontraron, luchando, un lugar digno en la comunidad. Y con ese lugar, lograron respeto y admiración.

Jóvenas y jóvenes, de entre 12 y 20 años, que saben leer y escribir, manejan con soltura tecnologías que sus padres y madres ni soñaban, que incursionan en las artes haciendo obras de teatro, películas, pinturas, poesía, canto, bailables, traduciendo a esas lenguas peculiares que tienen las artes, sus vidas, sus historias, sus sueños, sus amores y sus desamores, su herencia, su lengua, su cultura, su ser comunidad, con el corazón roto apenas ayer, y de nuevo sano y completo hoy.

Niñas y niños, el fatídico “Comando Palomitas”, cuyo número varía dependiendo de si hay o no dulces a la hora de pasar revista, la niñez de todas las lenguas igualadas en el juego y la travesura, la risa infantil como vacuna contra todas las fronteras humanas.

Si nos referimos al calendario, hay ahí 5 generaciones. 6 si se cuenta la que ya viene en camino y se adivina en los vientres hinchados de jóvenes madres. Todas, todos, todoas de pueblos originarios. Todas, todos, todoas con la sangre de raíz maya palpitándoles en la mirada apenas visible por entre cubrebocas y pasamontañas.

Y todas, todoas, todos, no ocultando las lágrimas que les ruedan por mejillas de piel oscura, al imaginarse el dolor de quien es buscado. Porque el llorar por el dolor ajeno es de humanos cabales y no avergüenza, sino que enaltece. Porque ocultar el rostro no es ocultar los sentimientos.

Y esas lágrimas son también por José Miguel, y por otros, otras y otroas como él.

Y esas ausencias son las que importan. Y el subMoy nos decía que no debíamos perderlas de vista, ni confundirlas con números, estadísticas, notas perdidas, fichas arrugadas en los escritorios burocráticos de la demagogia.

“José Miguel es un joven noble, trabajador, lleno de sueños y de vida. Es un hijo, un hermano y una persona profundamente amada. Detrás de su nombre y de su fotografía existe una familia que lo espera todos los días, que no ha dejado de buscarlo y que se aferra a la esperanza de volver a abrazarlo”, nos cuentan sus familiares.

Y agregan: “Hoy me dirijo a ustedes no desde un cargo, una institución o una organización, sino desde el lugar más doloroso que me ha tocado vivir: el de un familiar que busca desesperadamente a su familiar desaparecido. Desde aquel día, nuestra vida cambió para siempre.

“Han pasado meses de incertidumbre, de preguntas sin respuesta, de noches interminables y de un dolor que no se puede explicar con palabras. Sin embargo, no hemos dejado de buscarlo ni un solo día, porque José Miguel merece regresar a casa. No buscamos señalar culpables ni hacer acusaciones. Lo único que queremos es encontrar a José Miguel, saber dónde está y traerlo de regreso con nosotros.

“Les pedimos que nos ayuden a difundir la ficha de búsqueda de José Miguel a través de sus espacios y redes de comunicación.

“Hoy les escribo porque no quiero que el nombre de mi familiar se pierda entre tantas historias de dolor. No quiero que su ausencia se vuelva costumbre ni que el paso del tiempo haga que el mundo se olvide de él.

“Él no es solamente una fotografía en una ficha de búsqueda. Es José Miguel. Es nuestro hijo, nuestro hermano, nuestro ser querido. Es alguien a quien seguimos esperando en casa.

“Les adjunto su ficha de búsqueda con la esperanza de que puedan ayudarnos a hacerla llegar a más personas. A veces, una sola publicación, una persona que reconozca un rostro o alguien que decida compartir información puede hacer una diferencia enorme.

“No les pedimos que resuelvan lo que corresponde a las autoridades. Les pedimos que nos ayuden a que nuestra voz llegue más lejos, porque mientras José Miguel no regrese, nosotros no dejaremos de buscarlo. Y terminan su misiva: «Porque el amor por quienes nos faltan es más grande que el miedo, el cansancio y la distancia. Hasta encontrarte, José Miguel».

Y sí, eso no sólo podemos hacerlo, debemos hacerlo. También a eso vamos. No a ofrecer promesas. No a resolver crímenes (porque la desaparición forzada es un crimen). No a ofrecer consuelo ni alivio. No a usar el dolor ajeno.

Sí a hacer grande el grito, a extenderlo, a llevarlo lejos, a lo alto de la montaña, a lo profundo de barrancos y cañadas, al vuelo de ese avión, al rodar de ese automóvil, al andar de esos pasos.

A llevar a geografías lejanas una pregunta: ¿Dónde estás?

No hay mucho que agregar a las palabras de esta familia. Acaso señalar que, quien busca sin grupo, colectivo, red, movimiento, organización, también merece y necesita un abrazo.

A eso vamos, a que la voz de quienes buscan llegue más lejos, tan lejos que la escuche quien falta.

A conseguir, no la toma del Poder, no un cargo o puesto gubernamental, no dinero, no reconocimiento.

Sino a algo más sencillo, terrible y maravilloso: A que cada rincón de esta geografía llamada México se una a la búsqueda de verdad y justicia.

A que el país entero se convierta en un abrazo.

Un abrazo que respete el calendario, la geografía y EL MODO de cada quien, sea individual, de grupo, red, movimiento u organización. Chicas, medianas, grandes, las partes, conservando su identidad, convocadas en un todo: ENCONTRAR.

Por eso invitamos a todas las familias individuales, grupos, colectivos, colectivas, redes, movimientos, organizaciones de familias buscadoras, a que lleven a la Ciudad de México y las Sedes Alternas en Veracruz, Jalisco, Puebla y Querétaro, las fotos y fichas de sus ausencias.

Sabemos que en la Ciudad de México y en esas sedes hay banda que le sabe a eso y se pueden hacer reproducciones, cientos y miles, para que nos traigamos y coloquemos en cada comunidad zapatista. Para que la Sexta México lleve su parte, y el magisterio democrático la suya. Y toda persona noble y generosa las lleve a sus casas, calles, barrios, trabajos, secundarias, preparatorias, universidades, centros de investigación, laboratorios, tiendas pequeñas, medianas y grandes, centros comerciales, bancos, calles, postes, muros (y que toda la banda grafitera les dé espacio y haga como quien dice su marco, así colorido, chido, a las fotos).

Y todo el país se convierta en lo que en realidad es: un archipiélago de dolores y angustias, unido por el mar de la lucha.

Desde las montañas del Sureste Mexicano.

Capitán Insurgente Marcos. México, noviembre del 2026.

P.D.- Ésta es nuestra respuesta a las solicitudes de entrevista: una ficha de búsqueda. Busquen entrevistar a la desaparecida, al desaparecido. Ésa es la entrevista que vale la pena.

author: Aline Melo
title: Organizações lançam carta defendendo projeto que regula mercados digitais
content:
A regulamentação dos mercados digitais no Brasil, os chamados 

Marketplaces

, está em disputa. De um lado, empresas e organizações sociais lançam uma carta que defende a aprovação do Projeto de Lei 4.675/2025.

 A proposta cria regras para ampliar a transparência e fiscalizar a concorrência nesses ambientes, incluindo a atuação do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica, o Cade, criando uma superintendência específica para avaliar os negócios digitais. A carta deve ser divulgada nos próximos dias, após uma reunião convocada pelo Governo Federal, por meio da Secretaria de Comunicação Social da Presidência (Secom), com representantes desses grupos para alinhar estratégias para a aprovação do PL 4675.




Do outro lado da disputa, o projeto tem sido alvo do lobby das Big Techs, que o associa ao aumento do controle estatal sobre a internet.

 A estratégia reproduz argumentos utilizados em outras discussões sobre regulação no Brasil, como ocorreu durante a tramitação do PL das Fake News, e chama o projeto de “PL da censura”.




A proposta teve origem no Governo Federal, a partir de trabalhos do Ministério da Fazenda e do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade), e recebeu um substitutivo apresentado pelo deputado Aliel Machado (PV-PR) em agosto deste ano.




O argumento pela regulamentação dos mercados digitais




Na avaliação de Rafael Zanatta, diretor executivo da Data Privacy Brasil — uma das organizações envolvidas na carta em defesa do 4.675/2025 —, 

a regulação pode beneficiar especialmente startups, desenvolvedores independentes, varejistas e empresas brasileiras que dependem de grandes plataformas para oferecer seus produtos e serviços.




“Esse PL está trazendo um ambiente digital mais competitivo, mais transparente, melhor para startups, melhor para desenvolvedores independentes, melhor para varejistas. E os únicos afetados aqui são empresas muito específicas”, afirma.




Um dos exemplos citados pelo diretor da Data Privacy é o controle da Apple sobre a loja de aplicativos do sistema iOS e as restrições impostas a desenvolvedores quanto aos meios de pagamento. Para Zanatta, a possibilidade de utilizar alternativas, como o Pix, e de reduzir taxas de intermediação pode ampliar a concorrência e diminuir custos para empresas e consumidores.




Zanatta critica a repercussão de que a proposta reproduziria modelos autoritários de controle estatal. “O Partido Novo fala que esse seria um projeto do governo para aumentar poderes, instituir censura e controle na vida do cidadão. Esse projeto não tem nada a ver com moderação de conteúdo, não tem nada a ver com controlar a vida das pessoas. Estão falando que o PL é inspirado nas ‘ditaduras’ da China e Cuba”, afirma.




Na realidade, a proposta brasileira tem como referência experiências regulatórias adotadas em democracias europeias, especialmente o Digital Markets Act (DMA), legislação da União Europeia em vigor desde 2023. A norma estabelece obrigações para grandes plataformas digitais classificadas como controladoras de acesso (gatekeepers), com o objetivo de tornar os mercados digitais mais competitivos e impedir práticas comerciais consideradas desleais. Entre as regras estão a proibição de favorecer serviços próprios em detrimento de concorrentes e a possibilidade de desenvolvedores utilizarem sistemas de pagamento alternativos nas lojas de aplicativos.




O projeto brasileiro também prevê instrumentos de atuação preventiva do Cade sobre grandes grupos econômicos, com obrigações específicas voltadas à proteção da concorrência. Embora existam diferenças entre os dois modelos, ambos tratam da regulação econômica de mercados digitais e da limitação do poder de grandes plataformas, não do controle sobre conteúdos ou opiniões publicados por usuários.




“O PL 4675 protege o Pix, protege infraestruturas públicas digitais e protege que empresas brasileiras possam surgir e crescer sem serem limadas desse processo, ou mesmo compradas”, acrescenta.




Segundo Zanatta, o projeto também daria ao Cade instrumentos para impedir ou reverter operações de fusão e aquisição que possam prejudicar a concorrência, inclusive quando grandes grupos econômicos tentarem comprar empresas brasileiras emergentes. Ele cita como exemplos hipotéticos uma eventual aquisição do Jusbrasil pelo Google ou da Magazine Luiza pela Amazon.




Além da Data Privacy Brasil, participaram da articulação da carta organizações como Artigo 19, Ctrl+Z e Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa do Consumidor (Idec), e empresas privadas e associações como Wellhub, multinacional do ramo de saúde e fitness, Renner, empresa brasileira de moda, Best Rates, aplicativo de comparação de taxas de câmbio, Associação Brasileira de Instituições de Pagamento (ABIPAG) e Associação Brasileira de Bares e Restaurantes (Abrasel). A Coalition for App Fairness (CAF), coalizão internacional de empresas de tecnologia que reúne, entre outras, Spotify, Proton e Epic Games, também participou da reunião.




Críticos ao projeto resgatam narrativas de censura




Em publicação nas redes no dia 11 de novembro, o deputado federal Mario Frias (PL-SP) chamou o (PL) 4.675/2025 de “PL da Censura 2.0” e afirmou que o governo pretendia silenciar vozes divergentes da esquerda por meio da regulação das redes sociais.

 O Partido Novo também publicou um texto intitulado “PL do Apocalipse Digital”, no qual associa a proposta à censura e à ampliação dos poderes do Estado, nome também repercutido por Nikolas Ferreira em suas redes sociais.




Outro exemplo é o do deputado estadual Lucas Bove (PL-SP), que publicou um vídeo no Instagram comemorando o adiamento da votação. Na gravação, o parlamentar afirmou que “eles queriam te calar, não conseguiram” e atribuiu a não inclusão do projeto na pauta à mobilização de pessoas contrárias à proposta, que, segundo ele, se recusaram a ficar em silêncio. Bove também chamou o texto de “PL da censura” e convocou seus seguidores a compartilharem o vídeo como forma de defender a liberdade de expressão.



















O próprio relator, o deputado Aliel Machado, passou a receber pressão nas redes sociais. A publicação em vídeo feita por ele após a reunião com representantes do governo e da sociedade civil recebeu quase 500 comentários que repetiam acusações de censura e de aumento dos custos para os brasileiros.



















O lobby financiado pelas Big Techs contra-ataca




Um 

estudo

 de impacto econômico encomendado pela Associação Latino-Americana de Internet (ALAI) à ECOA Consultoria Econômica estima que os custos diretos de adequação regulatória das plataformas potencialmente atingidas pelo PL 4675 podem variar entre R$ 2,76 bilhões e R$ 11,34 bilhões ao longo de dez anos. A variação depende do número de grupos econômicos designados e dos custos de conformidade considerados nos diferentes cenários do levantamento. 

A Alai é uma associação empresarial criada em 2015, em Montevidéu, que representa grandes empresas de tecnologia, entre elas Amazon, Google, Meta, TikTok, Mercado Livre e Airbnb. O relatório tem sido apresentado a congressistas em Brasília, segundo apurou a 

Agência Pública

.




Na série “A mão invisível das Big Techs”, a 

Pública

 

revelou

 como a entidade faz parte da estrutura de articulação política das big techs na América Latina, com atuação junto a parlamentares, governos e órgãos reguladores para influenciar debates legislativos e defender interesses comerciais de suas associadas. As empresas pagam contribuições anuais de até 50 mil dólares para integrar a associação, que registrou receitas superiores a 1 milhão de dólares em 2023.




O relatório afirma que a conta não vai ser absorvida pelas Big Techs, mas vai cair no colo dos consumidores finais, que absorveriam entre 58% e 80% desse ônus econômico, por meio de aumentos de preços e redução da disponibilidade de produtos e serviços. Usuários profissionais, como vendedores, prestadores de serviços e anunciantes que dependem das plataformas, arcariam com outros 14% a 19%, principalmente por meio de taxas e comissões mais elevadas.




O levantamento também projeta uma redução de 8,3% a 12,5% nos investimentos em inovação, associada ao aumento das exigências burocráticas e da incerteza regulatória. Em outro exercício, os pesquisadores estimam que atrasos de seis meses a um ano no lançamento de novos produtos e serviços digitais poderiam representar perdas de bem-estar dos consumidores entre R$ 4,4 bilhões e R$ 8,7 bilhões em dez anos.




O relatório critica ainda a ausência de mecanismos formais de defesa baseada em eficiências e de um ciclo obrigatório de revisão periódica da regulação. Os pesquisadores também questionam os critérios de designação de agentes regulados, que combinam limites de faturamento com fatores qualitativos considerados abertos e não cumulativos.

author: Francesco Rota
title: FILM AFRICA Press Release
content:
The Royal African Society Announces the Successful Conclusion of the 2026 Film Africa Festival




London, United Kingdom,  9th November 2026




The Royal African Society is delighted to announce the successful conclusion of its 125

th

 Anniversary edition of Film Africa Festival which took place from 23 October to 1 November.

 Now in its 13

th

 year, Film Africa celebrated the richness, diversity, and creativity of African cinema and brought together audiences, filmmakers, industry professionals, and supporters for an inspiring celebration of African storytelling. The festival screened 38 films from 30 African countries, and hosted two symposia, across 11 venues in London, Sheffield, Bristol, and Plymouth.




The festival provided a vibrant platform for African filmmakers to share compelling stories, highlighted diverse perspectives, and engaged audiences through the power of film. This year’s Film Africa Festival provided a special focus on

 The Role of African Women in Cinema, and the Importance of Sustainable Finance, Intellectual Property and Digital Technology 

for the future of African Cinema.




We are deeply grateful to everyone who contributed to making this year’s festival a memorable success. We extend our heartfelt appreciation to all our members, guests, and members of the public who attended screenings, participated in discussions, engaged with filmmakers, and supported the festival throughout its programme. Your enthusiasm, curiosity, and commitment to African cinema were central to the festival’s success.




We are particularly appreciative of our 125

th

 Anniversary sponsors:




Platinum category:

 Afreximbank / CANEX and Nuvion




Gold category:

 Africa Finance Corporation and Oando




Bronze category:

 DLA Piper, Omenaa Foundation, Nigerian Exchange Group, Oakwood Green Africa, and Air Peace.




We also thank the filmmakers, directors, producers, our industry partners, venues, volunteers, and the wider creative community for their invaluable contributions and continued support.




Film Africa remains committed to celebrating African cinema, amplifying African voices, and creating opportunities for cultural exchange and meaningful dialogue through film. The 2026 festival has once again demonstrated the power of cinema to connect communities, inspire conversations, and deepen understanding of the many stories shaping the African continent and its diaspora.




We look forward to welcoming audiences back for future editions, and continuing to celebrate the extraordinary talent and creativity of African filmmakers. To join us and to partake in our future events, please see: 

https://royalafricansociety.org/events/




For further partnership opportunities, kindly send us an email to: 

ras_director@soas.ac.uk

.

African Arguments

author: groundxero
title: The Enemy at Home
content:
The belief that Democrats will dismantle a system designed to serve the rapacious greed of the war machine and the ruling billionaire class is a mirage.




 




CHRIS HEDGES




Nov 12




 




Power does not rest in the Congress. It does not rest in the courts. It does not even rest in the imperial presidency. It rests in the hands of Wall Street financiers, Silicon Valley, private equity firms, the fossil fuel industry, the predatory health care and pharmaceutical giants, agribusinesses and, most of all, the war industry.




 




No mainstream politician, including Bernie Sanders, dares utter a word against our entrenched militarism. If you do, you end up like Ralph Nader, who was turned into a pariah by a compliant media and our corporate-indentured political parties. Nader spoke the truth. He paid for his honesty.




 




We are about to witness the 

largest increase

 in war spending in American history with a proposed $1.5 trillion budget. The average taxpayer already shells out over $4,000 a 

year

 

to the war industry as consumer and environmental agencies are 

dismantled

, health care and education are defunded and programs such as 

Medicaid

 

and 

food stamps

 (the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) are slashed.




 




The new Pentagon budget will 

hand

 $58.5 billion to artificial intelligence and military command-and-control centers and see the effective 

merging

 of the United States and Israeli military industrial complexes. Seventy-four percent of the increase in the proposed $1.5 trillion budget 

will go to

 private contractors, 

including

 those who are building massive data centers on military bases.




 




None of this is good for us or good for the planet. The Pentagon, powered by the fossil fuel industry, is the world’s 

largest institutional polluter

, emitting an estimated 

66 million metric tons

 

of carbon dioxide in 2024.




 




Americans, meanwhile, struggle with rising prices — nearly 30 percent of people go 

into debt

 to buy groceries. An estimated 114,174. Americans 

die

 each year due to lack of health insurance or inadequate health care while a single-payer universal health care system could cover every American, save more than 100,000 lives a year, and reduce annual health expenditures by $1.04 trillion, or nearly 20 percent. Twenty-five percent of Americans are 

functionally unemployed

. The minimum wage remains frozen, despite Democratic Party promises to raise it, at $ 7.25 an hour.




 




The elites use war not only for personal enrichment, but to stifle class conflict.




 




War, as W.E.B. Du Bois said, diverts the poor from their real interests. It funnels national frustrations into the “heroic” battle against a common enemy. The nationalist cant, with its endemic racism, seduces those who are alienated or on the margins of society into feeling they suddenly belong. It entices them to sacrifice themselves for a “noble” cause. They becime the architects of their own enslavement. They march like sheep into war’s purgatory.




 




By the time they wake up, it is too late. They are cast aside, as so many of our 

veterans

 have painfully discovered, like human refuse.




 




But as a tactic to consolidate power and enrich the billionaire class, it is unbeatable.




 




Wars will only be curtailed, if not halted, when we nationalize the weapons industry and dramatically reduce the military budget. Until then, nothing, absolutely nothing, will change.




 




Indeed, things will only get worse.




 




No one in Congress — or any other branch of government — will do this for us.




 




The masters of war sitting in the boardrooms of Boeing, General Dynamics or Northrop Grumman are not praying for peace in the Middle East or coexistence with China and Russia. The generals — who build their careers by orchestrating wars and post military careers enriching themselves working for defense contractors — are not seeking a cessation of global conflicts. They are seeking hundreds of billions in taxpayer dollars and government debt to fuel the self-defeating cycle of endless war.




 




The corporate vultures — especially the war makers — are, as I write, descending on Congress. They are meeting with Democratic Party leaders and holding out promises of millions in cash. They will corrupt, neutralize and compromise most. They will destroy the careers of the very few who refuse to do their bidding.




 




They hold the real power. They have no intention of surrendering it.




 




The manufacturing of weapons systems and the waging of war are the chief activities of the U.S. government. It is no longer one among other means of advancing the national interest. War and violence are how we speak to the rest of the world.




 




The “shadow world,” — as the author Andrew Feinstein calls it in his 

book

 on the global arms trade — is defined by staggering levels of corruption, deception and senseless death. It is lawless and unregulated. Its criminal activities, cannibalization of national budgets and secrecy are sanctified in the name of “national security.”




 




Lockheed Martin, RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies), Boeing, General Dynamics, Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, Leonardo, Airbus, Rheinmetall and ThyssenKrupp, along with Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Palantir, Goldman Sachs, Citibank and Exxon, 

are

 the state.




 




We, including our political class, 

are

 the vassals.




 




The voters can send whoever they want to Congress, but until these corporations and the billionaire class are regulated, taxed and controlled, until their vast monopolies are broken up, until we stop squandering half of all discretionary spending on war, nothing will change.




 




Nothing.




 




Civilizations, as the historian Arnold J. Toynbee argued, “die from suicide, not by murder.” They are disemboweled by an uncontrollable and unaccountable military that drains state budgets and plunges dying empires into one military debacle after the next. These decaying civilizations finally collapse from within.




 




This is where we are headed.




 




The corporations, and the billionaires who run them, buy and trade politicians, academics and journalists like Pokémon cards. Their lobbyists write the legislation. They own the media. They have stifled the academy, shutting down free speech and purging critics. Judges offer them unlimited power. To defy them — and I speak from personal experience — is to be cast into the wilderness.




 




The military-industrial complex, as Karl Liebknecht said of German imperialists on the eve of World War I, is the enemy within.




 




“

Making a Killing: How the West Profits from Slaughter in Gaza and Yemen

,” co-authored by Andrew Feinstein, Ruth Rohde and Jack Cinamon — with contributions from Paul Holden and Professor Anna Stavrianakis — examines the global arms trade in the Middle East.




 




The authors estimate that $130 billion was made from arms exports by Western nations to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates during the war on Yemen and over $50 billion from Israeli foreign military procurements.




 




“RTX Chairman and CEO Christopher T. Calio made $18 million in 2024, after being appointed halfway through the year, while his compensation package surged to almost $25 million in 2025,” the authors note. “His predecessor, Gregory Hayes, was remunerated to the tune of nearly $22 million in 2023. Lockheed Martin CEO and former U.S. Air Force pilot Jim Taiclet, who was deployed in Saudi Arabia while serving during the Gulf War, earns an annual package of more than $23 million. Since his appointment in 2020 he has raked in more than $136 million in total Lockheed Martin compensation.”




 




Phebe Novakovic, the CEO of General Dynamics, has a net worth estimated at $420 million, up $270 million since 2020.




 




But it is not only the CEOs who profit.




 




Members of Congress and their families 

traded

 between $24 million and $113 million worth of Pentagon contractor stocks in 2024.




 




Representative Josh Gottheimer from New Jersey — a Democrat — is a former Clinton speechwriter and a close ally of House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries. Gottheimer, who is 

heavily funded

 by the pro-Israel lobby and an ardent Zionist, 

traded

 $22 million worth of stock in the top 100 Pentagon contractors, including Microsoft — which received $414 million from the Department of Defense in 2023 for software and cloud computing services — Northrop Grumman and IBM.




 




Gottheimer serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Financial Services Committee. He is well placed to know which defense companies are enriched by government contracts and which are not.




 




Former Democratic House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, is not any better. She made an estimated $38.6 million profit in one year from her stock trading, the most of any lawmaker, in 2024.




 




These politicians run the Democratic Party. They carry out the same illegal insider trading and have the same conflicts of interest as the Republicans and the Trump White House. Hunter Biden is no less odious than Donald Trump Jr. and 

Eric Trump

.




 




“Honeywell — which provides sensors and guiding devices to assist the Israeli military in airstrikes in Gaza — is the most commonly held arms company stock among members of Congress, followed by RTX, the company that makes missiles for Israel’s Iron Dome, among other weapons systems,” the authors write.




 




Members of Congress, they report, “made more than 13,300 trades totaling over $635 million in 2025.”




 




The arms trade, the authors illustrate, has created an unelected, shadowy cabal of foreign policy, corporate and military officials, along with academics, who — no matter who is in the White House or the Congress — feed the military beast.




 




This cabal, many parked in think tanks funded by the defense industry and given prominent platforms on cable news channels, preach endless war. They ensure the fabrication of bombs, missiles, warplanes, drones, ships, tanks and guns. They ship these weapons around the globe. They sustain the interconnected network of cutting-edge, high-tech systems of information warfare and surveillance, powered by data processing centers, cloud technologies and artificial intelligence.




 




Once these weapons and tools of surveillance are tested on Palestinians or Yemenis, they are brought back to manage and surveil 

us —

 an imperial boomerang abolishing what is left of our civil liberties and freedom.




 




The tyranny empire imposes on others, as Thucydides reminded us, it finally imposes on itself.




 




The choice, as Rosa Luxemburg pointed out, is socialism or barbarism. If we do not dismantle global capitalism, if we do not free ourselves from the tentacles of the war industry, we will descend into the Hobbesian world of totalitarian capitalism, failed states, mass migrations, endless war, ecocide and permanent immiseration.




 




The 

genocide

 in Gaza is the harbinger of this coming dystopia. It is a stark message by the industrialized nations to the Global South, especially with the breakdown of the climate. The message is this:




 




There are no rules. International Humanitarian Law is dead. The strong will annihilate the weak. We control the world’s resources and most of its wealth. We will not relinquish it. Your suffering and lives are meaningless to us. Defy us and you too will be slaughtered.




 




Fear is the only language these vampires understand. This is a dark fact about human nature. It is why Richard Nixon was our last liberal president. Nixon was not a liberal. He was devoid of empathy. He lacked a conscience. But he was scared of movements. He knew the power of the strike.




 




It is not our job to take power. It is our job to create radical movements to hold power in check. Without these movements, we are doomed.




 




“You get freedom by letting your enemy know that you’ll do anything to get your freedom; then you’ll get it,” Malcolm X 

told

 young civil rights activists from Mississippi 51 days before his assassination on February 21, 1965. “When you get that kind of attitude, they’ll label you as a ‘crazy Negro,’ or they’ll call you a ‘crazy nigger’ — they don’t say Negro. Or they’ll call you an extremist or a subversive, or seditious, or a red, or a radical. But when you stay radical long enough, and get enough people to be like you, you’ll get your freedom…So don’t you run around here trying to make friends with somebody who’s depriving you of your rights. They’re not your friends, no, they’re your enemies. Treat them like that and fight them, and you’ll get your freedom; and after you get your freedom, your enemy will respect you. And I say that with no hate. I don’t have hate in me. I have no hate at all. I don’t have any hate. I’ve got some sense. I’m not going to let anybody who hates me tell me to love him.”




 




The disease of permanent war and militarism is devouring the guts of our nation. These forces snuff out democracy. They turn culture into nationalist cant and sentimental kitsch. They turn education and the media into echo chambers for the rich and the powerful. They wreck the economy. They immiserate the citizenry. They pump toxins into the air, soil and water. They strip us of our liberty. They foster moral nihilism.




 




War is the apotheosis of this corporate rule, designed to exploit people and the natural world until exhaustion or collapse.




 




And time is running out.




 




If we don’t transform this system we, and most other species, will go extinct.




 




Literally.




 




We must mobilize to defeat these forces. This means organized mass disruptions of government and commerce as we have seen in France, Spain and India, and with organizations such as 

Palestine Action

 and 

Just Stop Oil

.




 




If we remain supplicants, if we hope desperately for a feckless political class to save us, the barbarians will triumph.




 




 







Feature Imge:

 Pet Project – 

by

 Mr. Fish




 




Chris Hedges

 is a Pulitzer Prize–winning author and journalist who was a foreign correspondent for 15 years for The New York Times.

Chris Hedges Report

 is a reader-supported publication. Read the original 

article

title: Αλληλεγγύη στους εκπαιδευτικούς που καλούνται στο πειθαρχικό για την απεργία-αποχή από την αξιολόγηση, Παρασκευή 13/11 14:30 στην Περιφερ. Δ/νση Εκπαίδευσης Κ. Μακεδονίας
content:
Γ΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ Κλήσεις απολογίας στο Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο-Κινητοποίηση στην Π.Δ.Ε. 13-11, 2.30μμ!




Παράσταση Διαμαρτυρίας στην Π.Δ.Ε. Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας την Παρασκευή 13/11 στις 2.30μμ




Κλήσεις σε απολογία συναδέλφων στο Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο για τη συμμετοχή τους στην αξιολόγηση.




Πρωτοφανής δίωξη της μίας συναδέλφου, την παραπέμπουν σε πειθαρχικό για δεύτερη φορά!




Συνάδελφοι,


Δύο συνάδελφοί μας καλούνται να απολογηθούν από το Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο Κεντρικής


Μακεδονίας με γραπτή απολογία για το  “πειθαρχικό αδίκημα” της μη συμμετοχής στην


αξιολόγηση, μετά από παραπομπή τους σε αυτό από τη ΔΔΕ Κιλκίς. Η μία συνάδελφος, μετά από


μετάθεση, είναι πλέον μέλος της Ε ΕΛΜΕ-Θ, ενώ η δεύτερη συνάδελφος κλήθηκε ήδη τον Μάιο


του 2026 από το Πειθαρχικό Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας και κατέθεσε τον Ιούνιο γραπτή απολογία για


το ίδιο “αδίκημα”, της μη συμμετοχής στην αξιολόγηση. Τώρα καλείται για δεύτερη φορά!


Το μοναδικό «παράπτωμα» των διωκόμενων συνάδελφων μας είναι ότι υλοποίησαν συλλογικές


αποφάσεις του κλάδου μας με τη συμμετοχή τους στην απεργία αποχή από την ατομική


αξιολόγηση της ΟΛΜΕ και της ΑΔΕΔΥ, οι οποίες εξακολουθούν να είναι σε ισχύ. Διώκονται γιατί


υπερασπίζονται το δημόσιο σχολείο και τα μορφωτικά δικαιώματα των μαθητών/τριών μας


απέναντι στην ιδιωτικοποίηση-εμπορευματοποίηση και την κατηγοριοποίηση της δημόσιας


εκπαίδευσης.


Είναι τέτοιο το μένος της Διεύθυνσης Δευτεροβάθμιας εκπαίδευσης Κιλκίς απέναντί τους που η


μία συνάδελφος απειλήθηκε με δεύτερο πειθαρχικό, για τον ίδιο λόγο, παρότι δεν ανήκει πλέον


στη ΔΔΕ Κιλκίς, μετά τη μετάθεσή της, ενώ η άλλη, μετά το δεύτερο πειθαρχικό, για τον ίδιο λόγο,


απειλήθηκε και με τρίτο και με τέταρτο!!! Πέρα από τη νομική πρωτοτυπία, της παραπομπής στο


πειθαρχικό για το ίδιο “αδίκημα” ξανά και ξανά, ένα είναι φανερό: οι εντεταλμένοι της


κυβέρνησης και της εξουσίας παθαίνουν πραγματική παράκρουση όταν βρίσκονται απέναντι σε


εκπαιδευτικούς που υπερασπίζονται, παρά τον αυταρχισμό και την τρομοκρατία, τις συλλογικές


αποφάσεις του κλάδου και των σωματείων μας. Μόνο τιμή για τους και τις συναδέλφους που


συνεχίζουν τον κοινό μας αγώνα! Ντροπή και αίσχος για τους εγκάθετους διώκτες του κλάδου!


Η μάχη κατά της αξιολόγησης αποτελεί μια ιστορικής σημασίας αναμέτρηση για τη δημόσια


εκπαίδευση και τους εκπαιδευτικούς. Παρά τους εκβιασμούς και το κλίμα τρομοκρατίας και


εκφοβισμού των εκπαιδευτικών, το εκπαιδευτικό κίνημα μετράει ήδη νίκες που αποτελούν


παρακαταθήκη για τη συνέχιση του αγώνα! (απαλλαγές εκπαιδευτικών από τα πειθαρχικά για


συμμετοχή στην απεργία-αποχή ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση, άρση καθαιρέσεων προϊσταμένων που


δε συμμετείχαν στην αξιολόγηση, παύση δυνητικής αργίας Χρ. Χοτζόγλου, απαλλαγή


εκπαιδευτικών που δεν έκαναν τηλεκπαίδευση από το σπίτι, άρση αδειών λειτουργίας 3 ιδιωτικών


Πανεπιστημίων). Οι νίκες αυτές αποδεικνύουν ότι ο αγώνας μας μπορεί να φέρει αποτέλεσμα. Η


απεργία είναι αναφαίρετο, συνταγματικά κατοχυρωμένο δικαίωμα και δεν ποινικοποιείται!


Το  Δ.Σ. της Γ΄ ΕΛΜΕ-Θ καλεί όλα τα εκπαιδευτικά σωματεία της Θεσσαλονίκης, ΕΛΜΕ και ΣΕΠΕ,


την ΕΛΜΕ Κιλκίς, ΕΛΜΕ και ΣΕΠΕ της Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας, σε παράσταση διαμαρτυρίας στην




Περιφερειακή Διεύθυνση Εκπαίδευσης Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας (κτίριο ZEDA) την Τρίτη


10/11/2026 στις 2.30 μ.μ. για να καταθέσουμε, με την παρουσία δικηγόρου των σωματείων μας,


συλλογικά τα “απολογητικά” υπομνήματα των καλούμενων σε απολογία συναδέλφων, όπως


κάνουμε κάθε φορά που διώκονται συνάδελφοί μας.


Καλεί επίσης την ΟΛΜΕ να στηρίξει με ανακοίνωσή της τις δύο συναδέλφους και το κλιμάκιό της να


παρέμβει στην Παράσταση της Παρασκευής στην ΠΔΕ, αν παρευρίσκεται ακόμα στην πόλη μας.


 Απαιτούμε το Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο Κεντρικής Μακεδονίας να προχωρήσει άμεσα στην


πλήρη απαλλαγή όλων των εκπαιδευτικών που έχουν κληθεί σε απολογία και να μπουν


οριστικά στο αρχείο όλες οι υπόλοιπες παραπομπές στο πειθαρχικό λόγω της συμμετοχής


των εκπαιδευτικών στην απεργία αποχή από την αξιολόγηση.


 Να μπουν στο αρχείο όλα τα υπόλοιπα πειθαρχικά για τη συμμετοχή στους


εκπαιδευτικούς αγώνες. Να μπει στο αρχείο η παραπομπή στο πειθαρχικό της προέδρου


και των άλλων δύο μελών της Ε ΕΛΜΕ για τις εξετάσεις PISA.


 Κανένα νέο πειθαρχικό για συμμετοχή στην απεργία-αποχή, καμία πίεση και εκφοβισμός


στους απεργούς εκπαιδευτικούς, να σταματήσουν οι οδηγίες για άμεση έναρξη


αξιολογικών διαδικασιών και ανάρτηση μονομερών πρακτικών.


ΚΑΝΕΝΑΣ ΜΟΝΟΣ-ΚΑΜΙΑ ΜΟΝΗ!


Η ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΟ ΟΠΛΟ ΜΑΣ!


Η ΑΠΕΡΓΙΑ ΔΕΝ ΔΙΩΚΕΤΑΙ. ΝΙΚΑ!




ΟΛΟΙ/ΕΣ ΣΤΗΝ ΠΑΡΑΣΤΑΣΗ ΔΙΑΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΑΣ ΣΤΗΝ ΠΔΕ ΤΗΝ ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ 13/11 ΣΤΙΣ 2.30μμ







Ζ’ ΣΕΠΕ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ: Αλληλεγγύη στους εκπαιδευτικούς που καλούνται από το πειθαρχικό




συμβούλιο Κεντρ. Μακεδονίας σε απολογία λόγω της συμμετοχής τους στην




απεργία-αποχή ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση – Παρασκευή 13 Νοεμβρίου,




2.30μ.μ., στην Περιφερ. Δ/νση Εκπαίδευσης Κ. Μακεδονίας (κτίριο ZEDA)




Συνάδελφοι/ισσες,


Την Παρασκευή 13 Οκτώβρη καταθέτουν τα “απολογητικά” τους υπομνήματα στο πειθαρχικό


συμβούλιο Κεντρ. Μακεδονίας εκπαιδευτικοί της Δ.Ε. που κλήθηκαν σε απολογία λόγω της


συμμετοχής στην απεργία-αποχή ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση-ιδιωτικοποίηση και


εμπορευματοποίηση της δημόσιας εκπαίδευσης.




Όπως και σε όλες τις ανάλογες περιπτώσεις το Δ.Σ. του Ζ΄ Σ.Ε.Π.Ε., δηλώνει την αλληλεγγύη


του στις διωκόμενες απεργούς εκπαιδευτικούς, στηρίζει και καλεί τους εκπαιδευτικούς να


συμμετέχουν στην κινητοποίηση που πραγματοποιείται την ίδια μέρα,


Παρασκευή 13 Νοεμβρίου, στις 2.30μ.μ., στην Περιφερειακή Δ/νση Εκπαίδευσης Κ. Μακεδονίας (κτίριο ZEDA).

author: Qassam Muaddi
title: Palestinian Opinions Are Divided as Elections Are Now Postponed Until 2027
content:
Although some in Gaza welcomed the prospect of elections, many are looking for solutions to more urgent problems.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On October 10, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a presidential decree postponing the legislative and presidential elections from November 2026, the original scheduled date, until September 2027.

Amid obstacles imposed by the Israeli occupation, the postponement was justified by a need to create appropriate political, security, and on-the-ground conditions for free, fair, and inclusive elections.

According to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA, the decree aims to allow for comprehensive national dialogue to strengthen Palestinian unity, preserve Palestinian territory, safeguard the political system, address challenges that the electoral process is facing, and ensure the participation of Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip while protecting their political and constitutional rights.

While some expected the postponement, in light of the cancellation of Palestinian elections in 2021, it nevertheless came as a surprise to observers.

In the Gaza Strip, reactions to the decision have been divided. Some consider it to be in the national interest, arguing that the current conditions in Gaza do not permit elections. Others believe that postponing the vote, after more than 20 years without elections, undermines the national democratic process and marginalizes the role of Gaza’s residents in determining their political future.

Fadi al-Sheikh Youssef, head of a youth-led electoral list that had been preparing to contest the elections, described the postponement as an unjust and direct denial of the Palestinian people’s democratic right.

“The elections should have continued after nearly 20 years of freezing the democratic process in Palestine,” he said. “If the Israeli occupation has imposed obstacles, the elections should have become a political battle fought by all parties against the occupation. This electoral process should have been a new opportunity to expose the occupation to the world and reveal the falsity of its claims about democratic practices and its supposed respect for freedom of expression and Palestinians’ right to political participation.”

He added that the postponement appeared to reflect an agreement among political parties to reproduce the same political landscape.

“Unfortunately, we see this postponement as part of an effort by the parties to recreate the same political scene. Even the justification of national consensus does not reflect the real wishes of the Palestinian people. If there had truly been national consensus, it should have been achieved over the past 20 years, not now, as the political landscape is being reshaped through a democratic process,” he said.

Al-Sheikh Youssef described the decision as deeply unjust and ill-suited to the current political landscape, arguing that it excluded new groups and political actors seeking to enter the arena and defend what remains of people’s dignity.

In a statement, Hamas said it viewed the decision to postpone the elections until next year as a step in the right direction, given the absence of the political, security, and on-the-ground conditions necessary for free and fair elections throughout the occupied Palestinian territories, including Jerusalem.

Hamas said the postponement should lead to comprehensive, serious and productive national dialogue. It also expressed its readiness to participate in discussions aimed at reaching clear and binding agreements for all parties, including mechanisms to reorganize Palestinian political institutions, particularly the Palestinian National Council and the Palestinian Legislative Council.

Furthermore, some Palestinian political analysts and academics offered a broader assessment of the political calculations behind the postponement and its potential consequences for the Palestinian political system.

Political analyst Adel Shadid told Mondoweiss that “despite the Palestinian demands and European pressure on the Palestinian Authority to hold elections, the PA are afraid of elections, because they know its officials know that there are real possibilities of losing, and despite that, I was surprised by the postponement of elections.”

According to Shadid, the elections were postponed in an unexpected manner. “I expected the Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas to unilaterally call off the elections, like in 2021, but I didn’t expect all the Palestinian factions to meet in Cairo and then come out with a joint statement to call off the elections together,” he said.

Shadid pointed out that although the alliance of Hamas, the Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and the dissident Fatah currents led by Mohammad Dahlan and Nasser Al Qudwah had a very high chance of winning, these factions knew that there was still uncertainty regarding Israeli attempts to block Palestinians from voting in east Jerusalem. This would have given the PA the possibility of calling off elections by blaming the decision on Israel, exposing their unwillingness to relinquish control, while the factions wanted to make it clear that it was a Palestinian decision. Shadid also said that “the result of this decision will be that the Palestinian political scene will remain at the current stagnation, which prolongs the overall Palestinian incapacity to face the Israeli offensive.”

Shadid, who twenty years ago ran the elections campaign for Fatah in Hebron, the West Bank’s largest city, today believes that all factions, including the leadership of Fatah in the PA, act on narrow political calculations rather than the overall national interest.

“During the revolutionary years of the PLO, when it was based in exile, political legitimacy came from the role played in the struggle, or as the saying goes, from the barrel of the gun,” Shadid explained. “But since the PA was established as an embryo for a Palestinian state, legitimacy comes from a popular vote, but this transition wasn’t fully and properly made, which has created a rift between the leadership and the people.”

Despite the uncertainty, he remains hopeful for the next generation of Palestinian leaders. “The international solidarity movement today finds more Palestinian partners in civil society, where they can find more Palestinians from the young generations with whom they can cooperate, and eventually, a new Palestinian leadership will emerge and channel all this potential towards Palestinian liberation,” Shadid said.

For Palestinian analyst and academic Akram Atallah, all factions feared the elections, because their performance in the past years, especially during the Gaza genocide, was very poor. This meant that despite the wide opposition alliance, the voting rate would have shown that the popularity of all of them has fallen back.

“I wasn’t surprised by the postponement of elections, because in my opinion, president Abbas believed that Hamas, his main opponent, had lost much of its popularity and capacity of influence, but the formation of the wide opposition alliance changed his calculations, therefore, it was expected from him to postpone elections,” he told Mondoweiss.

Atallah believes that the consequences of calling off elections will be paid by the Palestinian people in general. “Elections for Palestinians meant the possibility to renew their leadership in order to counter the Israeli genocidal and expansionist project, and calling elections off means to remain in the same political weakness experienced by the Palestinian people,” he said.

For Atallah, the entire Palestinian political system is in crisis, from the PA losing influence to Hamas losing capacity to present an opposition, resulting in all factions becoming more concerned with “their share in the political pie” rather than a renewed leadership for Palestine.

Despite this, he insists that “the Palestinian people will produce new leadership, and Palestinians will continue their struggle and resilience despite the political stagnation.”

On the streets of Gaza, opinions remain divided between those who support the postponement and those who oppose it.

Mahmoud al-Dhahir, 41, originally from Rafah and now displaced in Khan Younis, said President Abbas had made the right decision, given the instability of the Gaza Strip’s political and security situation. According to al-Dhahir, people in Gaza are already struggling with severe problems related to food and shelter, leaving them in no position to focus on elections or think clearly about which candidates could meet their needs.

“We are now living in just 30 percent of the Gaza Strip. If elections are to be held, we at least want to be able to return to all parts of Gaza and move freely. Only then can we think about who will serve the interests of the Palestinian people and go to the ballot boxes,” he said.

Al-Dhahir had voted in the 2006 elections, hoping that conditions would improve. However, after Palestinians chose their representatives through the ballot box and Hamas’s list won, he said, Israel imposed a tighter blockade on Gaza and deprived its residents of their rights.

He argued that conditions in the West Bank might be more conducive to elections because its residents are not facing a genocide, but that the situation in Gaza is entirely different.

“The Palestinian people in Gaza have been living through a genocide that has continued for three years and has not yet ended,” he said. “It would be better to look for solutions to end this genocide before thinking about another vote or another election.”

Although some people in Gaza had welcomed the prospect of elections as a democratic process through which residents could choose their representatives, the conditions they face have left many looking for solutions to more urgent problems.

Bassem al-Masri, 51, who was displaced from Beit Hanoun and is now living in Deir al-Balah, said he was delighted when the elections were announced for a near-future date, viewing them as a long-overdue democratic right for the Palestinian people. At the same time, he said the current circumstances in Gaza were not conducive to holding elections.

More pressing priorities include enabling displaced people to return to their homes and rebuilding the houses they have lost. All of this, he argued, requires Palestinian leaders to unite before elections take place.

“Palestinian factions and leaders who want to unite and consolidate their political decisions into a single position should have taken this step to help the Palestinians devastated in Gaza, rather than doing so merely to take part in elections,” al-Masri said.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $44,000 in the next 7 days. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.
