author: Slingshot robot #1
title: 6- Cuttings will regrow – Sitting-in for Grandmother Cottonwood
content:
On July 27th, 2026 the U.S. government and Fisher industries cut down three ancient cottonwood trees in a small town called Lochiel, Arizona in order to build not just one but two border walls. This area is the habitat of the endangered Mexican Wolf as well as jaguars, bears, foxes and many other bizarre, beautiful bugs and animals. It is also the home of the Tohono O’odham people, important to many indigenous tribes on both sides of the border. When the three grandmother cottonwoods were cut, one brave comrade stood in front of construction equipment, preventing the destruction of the last ancient tree and the construction of the border wall. In that last tree, we began our tree sit. With the support of hundreds of activists, the land owners, nearby towns and tribes, and even the local sheriff department, we halted construction of the walls for 75 days.

For 75 days, activists sat in the remaining cottonwood as ground support grew into a sprawling camp. It was the first tree sit to stop border wall construction and was briefly the first binational tree sit in history, with a sit erecting on the Mexican side for three days in August. During these 75 days, O:shad camp, jaguar in O’odham, held morning ceremony in the easement, the road which enforced the border. Ceremony frequently extended to effectively halt all construction vehicles for the day, or days at a time. People fell in love, they danced in the mud, cooked communal meals, all while defending the land. Utopia felt nearby.

Then, on October 5th, hundreds of border patrol officers, accompanied by turning point usa, invaded O:shad camp. They cut down the grandmother cottonwood and forcibly removed the tree sitter without a proper extraction team, risking her life. Activists on the ground circled the trunk to protect the tree and continue their resistance against the wall. More than 10 activists were arrested and many more brutalized. Though on private property and with no warrant, they ransacked the camp and destroyed our belongings.

Indigenous and non-white activists were singled out and beaten much worse than white comrades. Border Patrol violently pushed, pulled and dragged, but also kneeled on throats, punched eyes, pushed skin into barbed wire. They specifically targeted our medic (who is Indigenous) to be violently dragged, beaten, and arrested. They prevented our media team from capturing what happened, while escorting Turning Point USA to film the day in order to spread their right wing propaganda.

The next day, as Border Patrol expanded their boundaries further into private property to make way for the wall, five more of us were taken, and lawyers were unable to find them in the system while border patrol ignored calls from their lawyers, friends and family.

A day later, my comrade locked herself to a cement truck and stayed in a stress position without food or water for 7 hours while Border Patrol covered her with an emergency blanket despite the hot climate. One officer told her and the other officers that they should drive her to the middle of nowhere where no one would be able to hear her scream. They began to move the vehicle with her still above the tire; we all thought she would be killed. Two comrades who ran towards her, worried for her life, were tackled, brutalized, and arrested – one was sexually assaulted during her arrest. Finally they brought in an expert extractor who took her out of lockdown and she was taken to detention and then federal prison. She is now facing federal assault charges.

The rest of us were shot with pepper balls, tear gassed, leaving us vomiting, injured, bruised and emotionally exhausted. After the tree sitter was removed from the grandmother tree in Lochiel, a comrade reinstated the sit on the mexico side. Cut off from ground support by border patrol, she went over two days without food or water. When mexican firefighters and Fisher construction workers went to pull her out, she free climbed further up the tree. They destroyed her platform and life sustaining materials, leaving her to perch in the cottonwood branches without a platform or supplies. She suffered dehydration and starvation in high heat but still managed to keep a backpack on her, which she filled with clippings of the Abuela tree so that no matter what happened, the trees offspring could be replanted.

The following day the wall continued.

In total 30+ of us have been arrested, and many more brutalized, injured, and traumatized. We are the first people to be charged for this specific resistance against the border wall and our court date is in January 2027. Some of us have misdemeanor charges, others have felonies.

Some of us in Lochiel are intertwined through solidarity work in Palestine. We have seen how the same tactics used overseas to commit genocide are the tactics used here in the united states. Much as in Palestine, on the border there is constant surveillance. We cannot let this continue here or anywhere —these are the struggles of all people and we are all interconnected.

Though camp is now over, our resistance has spread. What took them five days to finish had been stopped more than 70 because of everyday people who believed in something. An ancient cottonwood in Mexico was preserved, the town of Lochiel now has international attention and resistance to the double wall got support from Palestine, Norway, Italy, Berlin, and across the US. We have clippings from the grandmother and Abuela trees that are already being propagated.

Border patrol came from sites all over the region to deal with us, which prevented them harassing other more vulnerable populations during that time. Border checkpoints that hadn’t been closed in years shut down because border patrol officers from all over were relocated to deal with protesters. We were able to pull away hundred of goons throughout 70+ days from harassing “immigrants” and citizens alike.

Though we can’t see all the things our camp accomplished, it helped question what a border means.

The state has created borders everywhere which means they can be resisted ANYWHERE. You can’t do everything but you can do SOMETHING. The federal government is still initiating ice surges. Families, your neighbors, your favorite spaces will lose people to these abductions. It’s time to give up comfort and ignorance to do what’s right.

It’s not about winning anymore, it’s about doing everything you can do to resist fascism and create the world you want. Chattel slavery took 400 years to end. Along the way resisters were consistently told they couldn’t win, and it’s true that most did not see the end. It took dedication and movements of people throughout hundreds of years to kill it.

People love to yell fuck ice but this moment calls for more than just vocal support. There are always things to do. Accompany people to their immigration hearings, host foot patrols in areas dense with migrant communities, set up free coffee and know your rights cards outside of day laborer sites like home depot, throw up banners on freeway overpasses, make a zine, take a stop the bleed training and use it at protests, canvass your neighborhood, host a fundraiser and donate the proceeds, research who profits and find out how fast their windows can be smashed. Learn how good it feels to be free.

We have everything we need to resist. One day the land will be free. Fight tonight, dance tomorrow, and if you need help, just ask.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: 5 – Call to ceremony: Red Butte and the protection of sacred lands
content:
By two comrades based in Oakland, CA

“Wii’i Gdwiisa [we-e gud-we-suh], known in english as Red Butte, is a sacred mountain just south of the Grand Canyon. It is the birthplace of the Havasupai people. In 1974, uranium was discovered on the Havasupai reservation. Despite the tribe’s attempts to prevent mining on their sacred lands, the u.s. government approved mining permits and the land was stolen (again). There is a long history of violence in the so-called american southwest committed against indigenous people and land by the nuclear industry. This is a story of that legacy and the uranium mine currently operating at the northern base of Red Butte. This is also a story of the steadfast resistance by the people born from these lands and those who fight alongside them. Wii’i Gdwiisa is still alive, still breathing. Her people ask us to live and fight in solidarity with her and all sacred land/water under attack by the settler colonial capitalist regime.”

On the weekend of May 14th–18th 2026, networks of land defenders called a gathering to defend Red Butte against uranium mining. We gathered some comrades to make the journey and as we left Oakland, we didn’t realize how transformative the trip would be. On the journey back home, we decided to pull over to pray and honor the sunrise the way we had been taught at the gathering, and we knew our lives and organizing would be forever changed by Red Butte.

When we arrived at Wii’i Gdwiisa after two days of travel, comrades were setting up camp at the southern base of the mountain. Our Indigenous comrades invited us to greet the land, give an offering, share our lineages and intentions, and ask permission to camp. We listened to the wind and rocks for answers and proceeded only once the land responded. Ceremony was at the center of this gathering, grounding us in an ongoing conversation with the land itself as we planned our actions in defense of Red Butte.

The gathering was autonomously organized and guided by Indigenous organizers with established protocols. People were invited to take whatever action they were called to, rather than relying on direction from specific leaders. The autonomous strategy was apparent in moments of confusion and disorganization, but allowed us to nimbly shift programming in response to emergent situations like radioactively contaminated desert winds and police repression. It also created opportunities for everyone to contribute what they could and grow into roles that needed doing, like bathroom duty, shelter construction, political education, vibes, radioactive decontamination, or cooking in a fully-functional desert kitchen serving three hot meals to 150 people every day.

Two sacred fires, one for Wii’i Gdwiisa and one for Dookó’oslííd (known in english as the San Francisco Peaks), were the heartbeat of the camp. We burned medicine and other offerings in their flames which burned uninterrupted throughout the gathering, we shared stories and meals around their circle, and we sang and danced in their warmth at night. We were taught to gather and cut wood with clear minds and good intentions. Fire-tenders stayed up every night to ensure the fires didn’t go out. As we kept watch over the fire, we also kept watch over the safety of the camp. Other practices, like the daily sunrise ceremonies and a ceremonial sheep slaughter led by Diné comrades, similarly intertwined spiritual consciousness and soulful embodied connection to Red Butte with the meeting of basic needs like sleeping and eating. The rituals were hard work, which taught us to be good guests and showed the necessity of strong spiritual practice in sustaining a lifelong militant commitment to fighting for land.

We were invited to Red Butte by Havasupai elders, who cannot themselves return to the birthplace of their tribe because the radioactive contamination is too big of a threat to the tribe’s survival. They wanted us to learn about uranium mining and make a public show of support for the tribe’s fight. After taking the first day to set up, the following two days were full of teach-ins, workshops, discussions, and planning for the elders’ call to action. We thank those who shared their knowledge with us, including groups like Haul No! and Stop T.H.E.M., as well as indigenous experts of the local land and academic experts of history and hydrology.

Local elders told us their stories about the u.s. government colluding with private companies to extract uranium while poisoning the land and people. They also told us about their fights against these violations. This legacy has left a deep scar in the so-called american southwest, and indigenous communities still suffer health impacts from the “uranium boom,” which peaked in the 1960s and waned in the following decades. Now, with growing global interest in data centers and a desperate need to power them, the extractive nuclear energy is rising again. Many companies are activating mining claims after years of dormancy and either digging new mines or re-opening existing ones. One such company is Energy Fuels, which first laid claim to a patch of land just north of Red Butte in 1986 to build the Pinyon Plain uranium mine. This mine began extracting uranium in earnest within the last few years.

Today, radioactive material from Pinyon Plain Mine contaminates vast underground aquifers, pollutes soil, and generates toxic dust. The impact compounds because the trucks hauling uranium ore to the mill in White Mesa Ute lands spread dust along the entire haul route, primarily on reservation lands. Plants and animals, rivers, humans, and mountains are impacted for millennia when nuclear contamination occurs. The wake of destruction compounds when you consider how uranium is used to reinforce bullets and tanks and make bombs that are used by the u.s. military machine to kill people worldwide. There is also potential for the uranium to be used in small modular nuclear reactors to power data centers, further entrenching us under the technofascist foot of empire. The anti-nuclear movement needs to forefront Indigenous sovereignty and show up for protecting sacred sites; we can stop the machine at the source of the raw materials it needs to wage war.

On the day of our camp’s action, the energy was buzzing, as if Wii’i Gdwiisa was charging us up for the fight ahead. We were excited, but felt like we could have used more time to prepare or talk about contingency plans. We had built relationships with a lot of people, but still had questions about how much we could trust folks. We lined up along the highway, the main road to and from the Grand Canyon, busy with tourists who knew nothing about the toxic uranium mining destroying the land for corporate profit happening just a few feet away. Comrades from all over the southwest joined us for the demonstration. We made a stand with banners, buckets, and chants, and despite police pressure, we stopped traffic and educated people passing through. At one point a hauling truck arrived, headed to collect uranium from Pinyon Plain, but it was stopped and had to be towed away due to certain actions that were taken against it. The action was a success and although the police used intimidation tactics to scare us, we built trust and were vigilant, organized, and protective. That evening, we had a feast and stayed up late strategizing how to continue the support for Red Butte and the Havasupai people once the gathering ended.

Looking back, our time in ceremony with Wii’i Gdwiisa was empowering and moving; we realized that even the action on the highway was a form of ceremony for us. Some of the rituals we learned have reaffirmed our connection to the land through introductions, altars, and care. We always pay our respects when in new lands, whether a city or a mountain. Thinking back to camp, we recall with a mix of nostalgia, longing, and awe how at home we felt. Our practices made us feel like we could sustain the camp for months and months. It feels weird to be back home, far away from Red Butte, thrust back into our regular lives. But life is not regular anymore. Every day we think of our comrades, of the fires, of the fight for sacred lands, of ceremony. We tell friends about the sense of transformation we feel after participating in the gathering. This trip has made us more powerful, more deeply rooted than ever before, and more able to fight for the land. Our movements for liberation need to be connected to land and spirit to win.

“Once a fire is lit, it desires to spread. We invite you to join the struggle to protect sacred land against extractive industry. We invite you to share this knowledge with others. Most importantly and urgently, we invite you to take action.” ______

This article includes excerpts from the zine “Fire for Wii’i Gdwiisa” to which the authors contributed: tinyurl.com/redbuttezine. It has more info and actions you can take. Also check livingandfighting.net.

title: 13 de noviembre. Charlas feministas y antifascistas
content:
El día 

13 de noviembre de 2026

, varias de nuestras compañeras nos han propuesto algunas actividades a las que acudir.




En Galdames, Euskadi, nuestra compañera 

Sonia Ruiz

 dará una 

charla sobre los orfanatos franquistas

, a las 19:00h. Un tema del que no se habla lo suficiente, que hizo mucho daño y marcó a centerales de infantes y que merece conquistar más territorio en los espacios públicos y privados, para que se pueda dar voz y desenterrar, de verdad, la memoria histórica.




Nuestrxs compañerxs del GT de 

Feminismo

 de CNT Santander, nos proponen una 

visita a la exposición

 «Tu madre ha sufrido violencia de género», que estará disponible hasta el día 18 de noviembre en la facultad de telecomunicaciones de la Universidad de Cantabria.




Ellxs nos proponen un encuentro a las 18:30h, el mismo día 13 de noviembre, y que nos presentemos con muchas ganas de acudir, que llevemos un objeto que nos recuerde a nuestras madres, tías y/o abuelas que hayan sufrido violencia machista.




Para ampliar esta actividad, aprovechando la campaña impulsada por el Ayuntamiento de Santander con motivo de la conmemoración del Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres, el 25 de noviembre, os dejamos varios enlaces que creemos que os pueden resultar muy interesantes.




https://web.unican.es/noticias/Paginas/2026/09/expo_violencia.aspx




Desde el Área de Igualdad y Responsabilidad Social de la UC, no solo podemos conocer los entresijos de la exposición, sino ahondar con noticias completas y visualizar los diferentes carteles de las campañas y, además, escuchar los audios con testimonios de personas que han sufrido esta violencia y poner rostro a las voces.




https://www.tumadrehasufridoviolenciamachista.net













Quien quiera acudir a algunas de estas propuestas seguro pasa una velada interesante.




#RompamosElSilencio




Salud y nos encontramos en las calles.

content:
CNT Zamora organiza un año más, en colaboración con la Regional Centro, la Jornada de Reforestación de la Sierra de la Culebra, una iniciativa nacida tras los devastadores incendios de 2022 para contribuir a la recuperación del entorno natural de Tábara. author: Brian Hioe
title: Unnamed Military Exercises Aim to Intimidate Taiwan Ahead of Elections, While Avoiding International Outcry
content:
ACCORDING TO TAIWANESE Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo, China is currently engaged in area access denial drills around Taiwan.

Such drills involve more than 100 naval and coast guard ships operating in waters around Taiwan. These exercises include the deployment of the Liaoning, China’s first aircraft carrier, and its carrier group.

Last week, on November 3rd, images of Chinese naval vessels deployed around Taiwan were released by National Security Council head Joseph Wu. Wu also drew attention to a large number of air sorties that had taken place on November 3rd, with 49 sorties of Chinese aircraft that entered Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone and crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait.

Previously, news reports had indicated that China may have been practicing for a potential blockade of Taiwan in late October and early November, through exercises that coordinated between its eastern, northern, and southern theater commands. According to national security officials, these drills were larger than previously named large-scale drills by China, such as the 2025 Justice Mission.

Indeed, it is notable that China has not formally announced any military drills to date. China normally conducts at least two named large-scale military exercises per year, in the spring and the fall. This has not occurred this year yet, though it might be expected that China would conduct a large-scale set of exercises before the end of the year.

It is possible that China is stepping up military activity as a show of force before the Taiwanese local elections set to take place later this month. Indeed, probably as a means of intimidating Taiwan and flexing muscles, one has in short order seen Pakistan briefly revoke permissions for Taiwanese airlines to fly over its airspace, Papua New Guinea order the closure of Taiwan’s representative office, and reports that Lithuania requested that Taiwan change the name of its representative office in what would have been read as a form of diplomatic downgrading.

Likewise, domestically in Taiwan, one has seen incidents of transnational repression. These include political commentator Akio Yaita being attacked at the venue of a talk, a comedian who mocked Chinese president Xi Jinping in his stand-up routine having feces and paint thrown at the venue where he was performing, and a plot to ram the same comedian with a vehicle and hospitalize him.

China may be stepping up efforts to intimidate Taiwan then–including familiar military threats. But not formally announcing a new set of military exercises may be a means of avoiding strong reactions to Chinese military exercises that might backfire for the CCP, in which members of the public rally behind the DPP and Lai administration rather than being cowed into voting for the KMT.

Either way, Chinese naval movements go to show that Chinese threats against Taiwan have not ceased, shortly before elections. Furthermore, that there is little attention from the world in a time of significant military exercises should be concerning, in that the sources of information about military activity remain confined to state actors, and China is able to prevent any outcry about its military activity if it does formally announce military exercises.

author: Cas Smith
title: Doctor says Israeli cluster bombs, with Australian tungsten, are targetting Palestinian children
content:
Dr Farah Abdul Aziz, Perth-based general and breast surgeon, volunteered twice in Gaza, including a harrowing period of service in the enclave’s “red zone” from December 2024 to January 2025.

Aziz told Green Left that working in the north of Gaza was “just awful”.

“There were just continuous attacks across the zone from sundown to sunrise, and even during the day. Medical staff could not go out of the hospital at all, because we could easily get bombed at any time.”

Aziz, a member of Palestinian Australian New Zealand Medical Association (PANZMA), was largely tasked with treating head, abdominal and chest injuries.

“The patients I received were the ones who had just survived the blasts that we were hearing all night. It was usually multiple shrapnel injuries, but they were still alive. Then, during the day, it would be single-shot bullet injuries.

“Because I’m not a neurosurgeon, I didn’t treat children who had received a single shot to the head, but I still saw them when my colleagues received them.

“Some had received a single shot to the abdomen or chest; these are little children, you can imagine snipers sniping them from two, three hundred meters away.”

The October protest against the Land Forces weapons expo in Perth condemned Australian governments for embracing the weapons industry and their involvement in supply chains connected to Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

But information about the specific weapons used, and Australian companies’ involvement their manufacture, is scarce.

Aziz said that because there is a significant proportion of children in Gaza, they made up 87% of her patients.

One particularly horrifying aspect was trying to treat children who had been targeted by cluster bombs as tiny, cube-shaped tungsten shrapnel was spread throughout their bodies.

“It’s well documented that these cluster bombs come from quadcopters, which are basically big drones that follow people around in Gaza,” Aziz said.

“This little kind of bomb cluster will actually open up and fire hundreds of little cubes. They’re about two millimetres small and they’re made from tungsten. Because of this they are very dense, but also high-velocity, because they’re so tiny.”

The latter factor meant that the shrapnel penetrated multiple organs and was extremely difficult to get rid of.

“I had one patient, who I remember really well, because the cubes just went every single angle of his bowel,” Aziz said. “Every single time, I would run the bowel from top to bottom to look for things that I had missed and I would find another hole and another hole.

“I had never experienced anything like that; usually, you have a bullet wound with an entry wound and an exit wound. Instead, this shrapnel would move in multiple tangents around the body. So, it’s obviously produced to cause maximum injury.”

Aziz said the tungsten making up this shrapnel was sourced from far north Queensland, and specifically the Mount Carbine Tungsten Mine. Activists say the wolfram ore concentrate from the mine is sent to US tungsten fabricator Elmet Technologies, where it is turned into warhead parts, tank parts and tiny tungsten cubes.

Speaking of the resilience of Palestinian people, Aziz noted that the majority of patients would carry information that enabled them to support doctors treating their illnesses, including cancer.

Many people had sought out Aziz’s expertise as a breast cancer surgeon. “They would come to me with a piece of paper with their history — their ultrasound, their mammogram, their biopsies — and they would show me their CT scan and their mammogram on their phone.

“Kudos to the local doctors as well; whenever they report a patient’s scan, they will get the family in to take a video of them scrolling down their scans, because they know that the patient has to move around from one place to another, seeking medical help.

“In spite of what’s going on, the [Palestinian patients] have a really good understanding of what they need to do. If they have a medical condition, they will go from one hospital to another, seeking help.”

Palestinian Australian New Zealand Medical Association

author: Sue Bolton, Sarah Hathway
title: Why you should vote Socialist Alliance in Victoria
content:
However, the Liberal-National Coalition and One Nation want to push politics to the right.

The Liberals have overcome years of destructive infighting under the leadership of youthful “clean-skin” Jess Wilson, who the mainstream media is championing.

At the time of writing, the Coalition is leading Labor by about 8% points in polls.

Unsurprisingly, Wilson’s policies do not favour the working class that is doing it tough in Victoria.

The Coalition is promising to “save” $22 billion, over 10 years, by freezing new public sector appointments and it wants to “save” $1 billion by scrapping Victoria’s Treaty with First Nations people.

Wilson has also promised more draconian anti-protest laws by expanding police “move-on” powers, and introducing a bureaucratic permit and registration system for public protests.

These regressive policies aimed at the public sector and the suppression of free speech are being supported by the opportunistic and reactionary One Nation, now polling only 1% point behind Labor.

The Coalition is preferencing One Nation, which wants similar outcomes.

Labor has paved the way for its own defeat by not addressing the cost-of-living crisis, chronic housing stress or a deteriorating public sector — especially in health, education and public transport.

Workers are right to be disillusioned as Victorian Labor has fought against substantive wage rises for public sector workers. It has joined the federal government’s full-frontal attack on the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union, including by calling a royal commission.

The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria is doing huge damage to Labor’s standing, while also destroying the country’ most militant union.

Socialist Alliance does not want the Liberal-National Coalition to win government, with support from One Nation, which purports to be anti-establishment but accepts hand-outs and policy advice from billionaires and bosses.

But Labor’s refusal to push back against the corporations and the billionaires makes this outcome more likely.

That is why it is important to cast your vote for socialists and Greens at this election.

The right has no solutions: Capitalism is creating more endless wars, which then exacerbate cost-of-living rises, including petrol. It is responsible for the climate crisis and consequent extreme weather patterns, which include devastating floods and fires.

Socialist Alliance is running under the slogan: “Fighting for people NOT the billionaires”.

Our anti-capitalist message is aimed at workers who are dissatisfied with Labor. Voting for hypocrites and racists, like One Nation, will not help lower housing prices or pay the grocery and education bills.

Socialist Alliance believes that elections are an opportunity to build support for socialist ideas among the working class and to push back against the hate-driven divide-and-rule policies of the capitalist parties.

We believe we have a unique contribution to make; we are a democratic, non-sectarian party which is focused on building the necessary alliances and mass mobilisations that involve workers in creating the progressive changes we need.

Our election campaign is an extension of this movement-building work we do on a daily basis. Our electoral work is part of our overall goal of creating a party which has as its goal the transformation of society so that it is geared to meet people’s needs.

Socialist Alliance is running 12 candidates focused on two regions — Northern Metropolitan and Western Victoria.

All our candidates are committed movement and community activists — most significantly against the genocide in Gaza. They see the self-mobilisation of working people as key to achieving social and ecological change.

All have pledged that, if elected, only to draw an average workers’ wage and invest the rest back into community and movement campaigns.

Sue Bolton, who is running for the seat of Broadmeadows, is supported by Jacob Andrewartha running in Pascoe Vale. A team of three, led by Meredith Lawrence, a proud anti-Zionist Jew, and community activists Chloe Beaton and Darren Saffin, are standing for the Northern Metropolitan Region.

Geelong Socialist Alliance is contesting all four seats, with Sarah Hathway running for the seat of Lara. Painter and decorator Brenden Grull, LGBTIQ rights campaigner Freya Hedley and former School Strike 4 Climate organiser Dom Williams are running in Geelong, South Barwon and Bellarine, respectively.

Former Geelong Trades Hall secretary and construction union activist Tim Gooden is leading the Western Victoria Region ticket, along with veteran unionist Sue Bull and maritime union stalwart Ross Smith.

Our solid movement-building approach has won authority and is the reason Socialist Alliance reached the 500 members necessary to achieve re-registration with the Victorian Electoral Commission.

This election, we will be campaigning for six critical demands:

Fully-funded public schools, public health, TAFE and free public transport;

Housing for all, a freeze on rents and 10,000 new public houses;

Housing for all, a freeze on rents and 10,000 new public houses;

No dollars for war, weapons manufacture or the genocide in Gaza;

No dollars for war, weapons manufacture or the genocide in Gaza;

Protecting free speech, the right to protest and trade union rights;

Protecting free speech, the right to protest and trade union rights;

Environmental action, no waste incinerators in Lara, a moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres; and

Environmental action, no waste incinerators in Lara, a moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres; and

An end to racism and discrimination.

An end to racism and discrimination.

Socialist Alliance is recommending you preference other socialists and green candidates, put Labor before the Liberals and far-right candidates last.

We urge you to vote 1 Socialist Alliance, and get involved.

[Sue Bolton is probably the best-known socialist in Victoria, with a stand-out record as having spent 14 years working hard for residents on Merri-bek City Council. Sarah Hathway is a former City of Greater Geelong councillor, a unionist and community activist.]

author: Jasmine Duff
title: Bosses are pushing for a hard-right government in Victoria
content:
Australia’s business elite and right-wing press are gunning to end Victorian Labor’s twelve-year reign and install a Liberal government. They’re pushing for harsh cuts to services for working-class people. Victoria’s Chamber of Commerce published a 

wish-list

 for the election, demanding exemptions from the payroll tax, reversing Victoria’s state debt, and drawing in data centre investment. The Murdoch and Channel 9 media conglomerates have helped the Liberals make crime and debt central election issues.

They’re pushing at an open door because both major parties are helping the bosses to generate a harsher right-wing political climate. Under Ben Carroll’s leadership, Victorian Labor has attempted to appease business. In his four months as premier, Carroll has launched a Royal Commission into the CFMEU, increased police funding, tightened bail laws, and cut services for kids with disabilities. Both Carroll and his predecessor Jacinta Allan attempted to suppress the wages of teachers during their recent enterprise agreement campaign.

But for Australia’s business elite, this isn’t enough. They want a change of government. And if the polls are to be believed, they’re going to get one. 

Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson has, for now, stabilised her party after years of embarrassing internal strife. Her campaign relies on heavy fear-mongering about youth crime and presenting Victoria as drowning in debt. Wilson is often described in the press as a moderate Liberal because she appears less socially reactionary. She matched Labor’s pledge to make abortions free, neutralising Labor’s attempt to make it an election issue. 

But Wilson is a blue-blood, ruling-class figure. She was raised in the Liberal Party and was backed by the hard-right Institute of Public Affairs (IPA) while head of the Young Liberals. Before being elected to the blue-ribbon seat of Kew, she served as executive director of policy at the Business Council of Australia. Her husband works for the IPA, and hard-right Liberal powerbroker James Paterson is a close collaborator and godfather to her children. In power, she’ll serve the interests of big business.

The Liberals have pledged to return Victoria’s budget to surplus by 2032. They also plan to lift the threshold for the land tax and payroll tax and cut the metropolitan payroll tax rate. These are all measures which would hand money to businesses and large landowners. They’ve also pledged to hire 3,000 new police officers. 

To pay off the debt while taking these measures would require drastic cuts elsewhere. While the Liberals have mostly avoided outlining where they would make cuts, they’ve already pledged to increase the workloads of civil servants through a hiring freeze covering thousands of positions. It’s likely they will propose further cuts that will affect social services and undermine working-class living standards. 

Alongside cuts, the Liberals want to create a more authoritarian political climate. Wilson has pledged to ban the slogan “globalise the intifada” and introduce move-on powers to crack down on protests. She will scrap the Victorian Treaty process. And she plans to introduce legislation that expands the list of offences for which children will be subjected to adult courts and adult sentencing.

It’s not just the Liberals. One Nation is also doing a service to the bosses by shifting the debate even further to the right. Despite the media’s portrayal of the party as “populist” disruptors, they’re on board with the agenda of reshaping Victoria in the interests of business. 

The bosses have faced little resistance so far in making their concerns central to the terrain of the election. This only serves to entrench a feeling of resignation about the impending right-wing wave. But if significant forces were prepared to launch a fightback, they could likely get a hearing. Only a small minority agree with the Liberals’ plan to scrap Treaty, but there have so far been no rallies to defend it. Progressive NGOs have not led marches against racism or to defend migrants. Nor have unions organised mass meetings or strikes to resist the bosses’ offensive. Instead, when Victorian teachers fought to improve their pay and working conditions, their union’s leadership encouraged them to back down and accept crumbs. 

The institutional weakness of the left and the decline of union militancy put the bosses and their backers in a powerful position. They’ve set the tone for this election, and the most likely outcome is a harsh Liberal government. Labor has failed to defend any modicum of a progressive agenda. They’re no solution to the sharpening attacks on workers that the coming period is likely to usher in. 

The left needs to gear up for a serious fight. Our side will need to organise against attempts to slash services, defend the right to demonstrate, push back against racism and resist a likely offensive against government-employed workers. We will need not just defensive campaign groups and broad demonstrations, but a socialist vision of how our society could instead be run. Victorian Socialists is running candidates across the state, and we’re in with a chance to get one or more candidates elected. If elected, they will use their platform in parliament to champion struggles against cuts, attacks on wages and working conditions and the racism and bigotry of the Liberals and One Nation. Everyone who wants to see a real response to the right-wing turn in Victorian politics should put Victorian Socialists first on their ballot paper on 28 November.

author: Kerry Smith
title: Solidarity shown to climate action group Rising Tide
content:
Many community-based groups are showing their support for climate action group Rising Tide, which is battling NSW Labor, Newcastle City Council and NSW Police to organise a peaceful protest on Newcastle Harbour, the world’s biggest coal port, on November 14.

You can register for the Paddle for the Planet here, and sign the petition to reverse Newcastle Council's ban on Rising Tide events here.

Below are some of the solidarity statements.

Sydney Students for Climate stands with Rising Tide against the outrageous decision by the City of Newcastle to permanently ban climate protests from council-owned land.

The undemocratic attack on protest rights was passed by the mayor’s deciding vote, after a 6–6 split at the November 10 council meeting. The motion could effectively ban all protests on Newcastle council land.

It was supported by NSW Labor Premier Chris Minns, who wrote a letter endorsing the motion.

Minns has consistently tried to shut down peaceful protests for climate, Palestine and other issues.

We also note that NSW Police are taking Rising Tide to the Supreme Court to try and shut down the November 14 paddle out for the planet.

With the climate hurtling towards disaster and NSW Labor continuing to approve new coal and gas projects, we will fight these anti-protest restrictions and continue demanding action for a safe climate.

SSFC will be at the Paddle for the Planet this Saturday, and the People’s Blockade of the World’s Largest Coal Port in February, and we encourage all to join us.

Socialist Alliance stands with Rising Tide and all groups protesting against the expansion of coal and gas, and for funding a just transition for fossil fuel workers in Muloobinba/Newcastle.

The City of Newcastle’s decision on November 10 to ban Rising Tide, and other groups, from protesting on “community-owned land” is draconian and dangerous.

The motion — adopted by a the independent Mayor’s casting vote — represents yet another attack on citizen’s democratic right to protest in NSW. Three Labor councillors did not support the Mayoral minute, only given half an hour before the meeting, but one did.

While the motion singled out Rising Tide, it said “affiliate groups” were also banned from protesting on council land. When pressed, Mayor Gavin Morris confirmed he also wanted to stop protests that support Palestine.

NSW Labor Premier Chris Minns’ record on trying to stop peaceful protests — on Palestine and for a safe climate — shows just how dangerous he is.

For three years Minns has tried to stop citizens from protesting the genocide in Gaza. He has been spectacularly unsuccessful because he has been challenged, and the courts, including the Supreme Court, have ruled against his efforts to stop people from mobilising together to express their view — the Sydney Harbour Bridge march for humanity being the most prominent example.

Minns is a big fan of coal, and he is now trying to introduce a new law to circumvent a High Court decision stating that NSW planning must take all emissions into account.

Minns has wanted to stop Rising Tide’s peaceful protests for a safe climate at the Newcastle Harbour. For several years he has been pushed back.

Newcastle City Council’s decision to prevent Rising Tide from using foreshore land now and into the future will not deter climate activists.

The NSW Police has lodged an objection in the Supreme Court to also disallow the Rising Tide protest on November 14.

But climate activists will continue to protest NSW Labor’s addiction to fossil fuels, which includes expanding coal mines in the Hunter Valley in a climate crisis.

As COP31 begins in Turkey, Rising Tide is seeking to draw attention to Australia’s complicity in fueling dangerous climate change. Minns is also complicit.

Socialist Alliance has long supported Rising Tide and will be joining the family-friendly flotilla protest at the world’s largest coal port on November 14 at 10am.

City of Sydney for Palestine stands with Rising Tide. Rising Tide has supported and facilitated our actions, and many of our members have volunteered with and participated in actions facilitated by Rising Tide. We know firsthand the power of coming together across movements.

Newcastle Council’s decision to prevent Rising Tide from using council-owned community land for protest events is an attack on the right to protest. We call on the council to reverse it.

From climate justice to Palestinian liberation, our movements depend on the freedom to organise, speak out and take collective action.

Stand with Rising Tide. Defend the right to protest.

The Greens have condemned Newcastle City Council's extraordinary decision to prohibit Rising Tide from using community-owned land for future climate protests, as NSW Police take the peaceful climate movement to the Supreme Court and the Minns Labor Government moves to pass special legislation protecting the expansion of the Mount Pleasant coal mine.

Greens MP and spokesperson for the environment and climate change Sue Higginson said the coordinated political and legal pressure against climate protesters was an alarming escalation in Labor's efforts to protect the coal industry from public scrutiny and opposition.

Greens Leader Senator David Shoebridge said:

“Labor is taking its orders directly from the coal industry, again.

“This decision shows the extent of fossil fuel capture of the Labor party all the way from Local Councils to Federal Parliament.

“These protests were working and that is exactly why the fossil fuel industry got their people in the Liberal and Labor parties to try and ban them.

“While Anthony Albanese is in Türkiye at COP31 talking big on Australia's climate ambitions at home they are blocking protest, approving coal and gas projects and taking the fossil fuel industry’s cash."

“Labor wants applause at COP for its climate leadership while it keeps approving new coal and gas, including a decades‑long extension of the North West Shelf, and that double game is exactly why thousands of people keep turning up in Newcastle every year.

“Labor listens to the money and works alongside the polluters, the Greens listen to the people and work alongside them in our fight for a safe future, because that’s what’s at stake here.”

NSW Greens MP, solicitor, and spokesperson for Climate Change Sue Higginson said:

“NSW Labor has completely lost its way. While the climate crisis accelerates and Australia is leading global climate negotiations at COP31, the Minns Government is rewriting climate laws for coal corporations in violation of the High Court, taking peaceful protesters to court (again) and supporting a Newcastle Council decision to exclude climate campaigners from public land.

“The people of Newcastle and NSW have every right to peacefully protest the ongoing expansion of coal mining and exports through their city. That right belongs to the community, and it cannot be extinguished because Minns and a select few Labor politicians find the message inconvenient.

“Newcastle is home to the world's largest coal export port, and the people who live there are on the front line of the climate crisis. Rising Tide has brought thousands of people together to demand action on coal, and Labor's response is to try to shut them down.

“Three Labor Newcastle councillors stood with the Greens to defend the right to protest, but their colleague, Premier Chris Minns’ minion, with the deciding vote chose to impose an extraordinary and indefinite exclusion on Rising Tide. This is a disgraceful decision that will stand as a historic mistake.

“At the same time, NSW Police are in the Supreme Court trying to prohibit a peaceful flotilla protest from going ahead in the latest attack on legitimate and peaceful democratic activity. Rising Tide has made clear that Saturday's event is intended to be a peaceful, fun gathering to highlight COP31, and the police should be facilitating that democratic expression rather than fighting it in court.

“The Minns Government’s rushing of special legislation through Parliament to protect the billion-dollar Mount Pleasant coal operation from the consequences of a landmark climate law decision is about as egregious as it gets. Labor is prepared to change the law for coal corporations while making it harder and harder for ordinary people to exercise their democratic rights.

“These decisions expose just how deeply the coal industry has embedded itself in the political priorities of NSW Labor. Coal corporations have extraordinary access to government, while the communities demanding a safe climate are met with police, courts and political exclusion.

“The Greens stand with Rising Tide and everyone exercising their right to peaceful protest. Newcastle Council should reverse this decision, NSW Police should safely facilitate Saturday's assembly, and the Minns Government must abandon its special protection for the Mount Pleasant coal mine. Anything less is a deep betrayal of our community and climate.

The Australia Palestine Advocacy Network (APAN) condemns Newcastle Council’s decision to ban Rising Tide and associated or affiliated groups, including Palestinian solidarity groups, from holding protests and events on council land.

Peaceful protest is not a privilege granted by politicians or local councils. It is a fundamental democratic right.

We call on Newcastle Council to immediately reverse this decision and on the NSW Government to uphold the right to peaceful assembly, rather than support measures that restrict it.

APAN stands in solidarity with Rising Tide and all communities whose fundamental democratic freedoms are threatened by this decision.

Hiba Farra, APAN Vice President said: “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to democracy.

“Public spaces belong to the community, not just those whose views are acceptable to governments. First they try to silence Palestinians speaking out against genocide. Now they’re shutting down climate protesters.

“This is not about public safety. It is about silencing dissent and deciding whose voices are allowed to be heard.

“This sweeping restriction sets a dangerous precedent for the right to peaceful protest in NSW, extending beyond climate activism to threaten the ability of Palestinians and their supporters to organise, assemble and demand justice.

At a time when Palestinians are facing genocide, occupation and forced displacement, attempts to silence those speaking out against Israel's actions are particularly alarming.

“Silencing Palestinian voices will not shut down the demand for justice and accountability.”

Students Stand AGAINST Sexual Violence (SSASV) is deeply disturbed by the actions of those in power this week and their attempts to silence activists.

We have seen a disgusting attack on protest rights in NSW yet again this week. On Tuesday night, we saw an egregious attempt to shut down Rising Tide’s “Paddle for the Planet”, a one-day, family-friendly flotilla at the world’s largest coal port to demand new jobs and funding for coal workers and a safe, liveable climate for everyone.

In an attempt to censor this action, Newcastle City Council’s Lord Mayor presented and passed a repressive motion prepared in secret collaboration with NSW Premier Minns and Police Minister Catley, which stated “that Council: Does not license or authorise, now and into the future, community-owned land for the purpose of Rising Tide’s events/protests (including, but not limited to, The People’s Blockade) and including its associates, subsidiaries, affiliated IMGs [issue motivated groups] and individuals.”

SSASV is UTTERLY DISGUSTED by this unprecedented attack on the right to protest.

Newcastle City Council has now banned approval of ANY EVENT OR PROTEST organised by Rising Tide or any associated groups on council-owned land “now and into the future”, leaving it unclear as to who can organise events on PUBLIC LAND in Newcastle.

Rising Tide has stated: “This is an attack on democratic participation, and follows in the footsteps of governments across the country restricting the right to protest,” which SSASV wholeheartedly agrees with.

The right to protest is absolutely crucial to the public's ability to be heard and participate in a democratic society.

A THREAT TO ONE IS A THREAT TO ALL.

SSASV stands in solidarity with the Rising Tide team and encourages you to sign and share their petition calling on the Lord Mayor and Newcastle City Council to unwind the ban on Rising Tide and affiliated groups.

We reject Newcastle Council’s authoritarian attempt to protect coal.

Last night, Newcastle Council passed a motion permanently banning Rising Tide, and any group or person associated with them, from using public land.

Many Trans Justice Project members, for example, would likely be banned from using public land.

This motion was prepared with support from NSW Premier Chris Minns and police minister Yasmin Catley.

Our government is attempting to crush democracy and control public life to defend the coal industry — which contributes to global warming that will kill billions.

We urge you to sign the petition demanding Newcastle Council drops this law, and to attend the upcoming Paddle for the Planet in Newcastle on November 14.

author: Brett Wilkins
title: Furious over housing costs, millions join general strike in Spain
content:
Spain was rocked by its first general strike in years on November 11, as millions of housing rights defenders, students and workers took to the streets in a nationwide revolt against an affordability crisis and a housing system that critics say prioritises enriching property investors and landlords over providing homes for people.

The 24-hour walkout, known as the 11N, disrupted transportation, schools, businesses, ports and industrial production, with demonstrations and picket lines reported in Madrid, Barcelona and dozens of other cities.

Organised by a coalition of labour unions and tenant organisations, the unprecedented mobilisation sought to unite historically separate struggles. The Madrid Tenants’ Union said that, despite autumn storms throughout much of the country, as many as 4 million people took part in the day of action.

“It’s time to change the rules of the game. We must end a housing system based on speculation and create a rights-based system,” 11N organisers said. “The 11N is not only a labour strike or a strike of tenants, it is a general strike for housing and against the cost of living.”

The immediate trigger of the 11N strike was the September eviction of María del Carmen Abascal — popularly known as Maricarmen — an 87-year-old woman who had lived in her Madrid apartment for seven decades. The investment fund that bought her building jacked up her monthly rent by more than 400% from €500 to €2,650 a month — an amount far exceeding her modest pension.

Despite previous legal efforts to prevent her eviction, Maricarmen was forcibly removed from her home and taken away on a stretcher before a deal was reached amid mass protests and she was allowed to return. However, she died in a hospital two weeks later.

Millions of people in Spain who work full-time increasingly cannot afford a decent place to live. Average rents have nearly doubled over the past decade, while housing prices have risen substantially faster than wages.

According to Spain’s central bank, the country faces a housing deficit of approximately 750,000 homes, potentially exceeding one million by 2028. Publicly owned rental housing accounts for less than 2% of the country’s housing supply, compared with a European Union average of around 8%.

The consequences are particularly severe for younger workers. The Spanish Youth Council estimates that the average monthly rent of €1,176 consumes approximately 98.7% of a young person’s average monthly salary.

“I doubt I’ll ever be able to own a home, let alone have a family like my parents could have at my age,” Elena Carmona, a young bookstore employee participating in the strike in Madrid, told Público.

Pablo Pérez, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, told Público that “what is at stake is who keeps the wealth we produce and who has the power to decide over our lives.”

“This is a strike of everyone who is fed up with working so that others can enrich themselves at their expense,” he continued. “It can’t be that we work harder and harder and that much of our salary ends up directly in the pocket of those who live in our homes.”

“What began with the fight against the eviction of Maricarmen has triggered a mobilisation that no one imagined,” Pérez added.

Anti-capitalist activist Beatriz Payo, 26, said Maricarmen’s eviction marked a turning point for her. She described witnessing firsthand “the level of violence and injustice behind a system that makes business out of such basic necessities as housing.”

That violence was on display Tuesday as police in cities across Spain attacked protesters with batons and pepper spray. At least four people were hospitalised in the capital, according to the Madrid Tenants’ Union. Officers also assaulted some of the demonstrators who blocked the M-30 highway in Madrid’s Vallecas neighbourhood.

Video footage recorded in Granada also showed police literally beating back strikers.

LGBTQ+ activist Samantha Hudson said police pepper-sprayed her and other protesters, including actress Laura Weissmahr and journalist María Barrier, in the face during a demonstration on Madrid’s Gran Vía.

“Does it bother them that much that we exercise this basic, fundamental right?” Hudson asked after the assault. “A boy’s head has been split open. I’m having a terrible panic attack.”

Amnesty International Spain said, “We are documenting concerning police conduct in Madrid, Alicante, Castellón, Vitoria, Valencia, Málaga, Granada and Santiago.”

“Force must be a last resort and can only be used proportionately,” Amnesty asserted. “Blows to the head must be avoided because of the risk of serious injury, and police batons and pepper spray must only be used against people who are being violent. They must not be used indiscriminately against protests or to disperse peaceful demonstrations.”

“We call on the authorities to guarantee the right to protest at this afternoon’s demonstrations, to ensure that officers visibly display their identification numbers, to ensure that pepper spray is not used and that police do not charge peaceful demonstrators, and to investigate the excessive use of force,” the group added.

Despite police repression and stormy weather in many cities, the strike caused significant disruptions. Organisers reported 90% participation in the automotive and port sectors, with complete stoppages at Volkswagen and SEAT factories. There were also widespread shutdowns in waste collection, meat processing, and energy sectors.

“The strike has exceeded the labour unions’ expectations,” Workers’ Commissions secretary-general Unai Sordo told The Associated Press. “It has been a success in terms of turnout.”

Following the protests sparked by Maricarmen’s eviction, social-democratic Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early election on November 29 in a bid to secure four more years of rule for his leftist coalition government.

However, last month’s high-speed train collision in Toledo province that killed 69 people — the second major rail disaster in the country this year — has complicated Sánchez’s strategy.

“The Socialists need for the strike to be a success and for there not to be any violence so that the election campaign can swing back to being about housing,” Autonomous University of Barcelona political science professor Oriol Bartomeus told the AP.

Meanwhile on the right, the Popular Party and far-right Vox “both want the strike to be a flop and to end in scenes of burning dumpsters and shattered shop windows,” Bartomeus said, so that “they can say, ‘This is chaos, and we are coming to establish order.’”

Pepe Álvarez, general secretary of the General Union of Workers, told El Diaro that, after Wednesday’s strike, “whoever governs, no matter what happens on the 29th, they will have to listen to the street.”

N11 organisers expressed similar sentiments.

“Whoever governs,” they said, “we will conquer the right to housing.”

[Reprinted from Common Dreams.]

author: Peter Boyle
title: NSW Labor, Newcastle council try to ban climate protests during COP31 summit
content:
BREAKING NEWS: NSW Police have failed in the NSW Supreme Court to prohibit Rising Tide’s Paddle for the Planet event on November 14.

As Labor Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hypocritically professed concern at the COP31 climate summit for the existential threat to Pacific Island states from the climate emergency, NSW Labor is trying to stop peaceful protests for climate action.

Planned to coincide with COP31, the Paddle for the Planet mass paddle-out and flotilla in Newcastle Harbour organised by the climate action group Rising Tide (RT) on November 14 is set to be the biggest climate protests of the year.

Muloobinba/Newcastle is the world’s biggest coal port and the Chris Minns NSW Labor government is going to extreme lengths to expand coal and gas mining, even as United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres told COP31 that fossil fuels “must go the way of the dinosaurs”.

According to the Climate Council, since coming to power, the Albanese government has approved 39 new, expanded or extended coal, oil and gas developments.

“The government’s 2025 reforms to approval laws failed the climate test, and continue to give new coal and gas projects a free pass to pollute.”

With the support of Minns, Newcastle City Council made the shock decision to never again authorise or licence RT to use community-owned land for Rising Tide events or protests. The motion also bans “associates, subsidiaries, other groups and individuals” from holding protests or events on council land.

While Greens councillors and most Labor councillors voted against this anti-democratic motion — which was moved with just half an hour’s notice by independent Mayor Gavin Morris — Labor councillor Declan Clausen supported the ban. After the vote tied 6–6, it was passed by Morris’ casting vote.

Steve O’Brien, Socialist Alliance candidate for Newcastle in the March 2027 NSW election, told Green Left that the council’s ban motion was “an outrageous attack on our democratic right to protest”.

“The climate emergency is real and climate activists are defending the future for us all and for future generations.”

Rising Tide is seeking legal advice and may decide to challenge this ban in the courts. It has launched a petition for the ban to be reversed, which hit 3000 signatures in less than 24 hours.

The ban does not directly affect the Paddle for the Planet because it is being held at Horseshoe Beach, which is not council owned, however, it coincided with NSW Police’s Supreme Court bid to oppose Rising Tide’s “Notice of Intention to Hold a Public Assembly” (Form 1) for the paddle out.

NSW Police, backed by Minns and police minister Yasmin Catley, claimed it had “serious safety concerns”. The Supreme Court will hand down its decision on November 13.

Rising Tide spokesperson Alexa Stuart said: “The real safety issue here is the Minns Labor government's reckless expansion of coal and gas.

“We’re already feeling the devastating impacts of the climate crisis, and scientists project that almost half a million people around the world will die by February due to the climate-fueled super El Nino.”

Stuart said Paddle for the Planet would go on regardless of the attempts to block it.

“It’s shocking that NSW Police are attempting to shut down a family-friendly protest calling for a safe and livable planet. The Minns Labor government is hell-bent on suppressing peaceful protest, and this is yet another attempt to silence dissent rather than actually take meaningful action on the climate crisis.

“On Saturday, in the middle of the United Nations COP31 climate negotiations, hundreds will protest at the World’s Largest Coal Port. We refuse to stand by whilst our [federal Labor] government claims to be climate leaders on the world stage, while back home fuelling the climate crisis through the approval of 38 new coal and gas projects.”

People taking part in Paddle for the Planet are urged to register here.

[Sign the petition to reverse Newcastle City Council’s ban on Rising Tide events.]

title: Διεκδίκηση του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης: συγκέντρωση Πέμπτη 12/11 18:00 άγαλμα Βενιζέλου
content:
Εργαζόμενοι και συνταξιούχοι συνεχίζουν με αποφασιστικότητα και αγώνα διεκδικώντας την 13η- 14η σύνταξη / μισθό: Συγκέντρωση Πέμπτη 12/11, 6μμ, άγαλμα Βενιζέλου




Παράλληλα σε ξέλιξη βρίσκεται η καμπάνια συλλογής υπογραφών, που είναι πρωτοβουλία σωματείων εργαζομένων και συνταξιούχων και επιδιώκει να συσπειρώσει όσο γίνεται περισσότερους εργαζόμενους και συνταξιούχους που αγωνίζονται στους δρόμους και απαιτούν την ΑΜΕΣΗ επαναφορά του 13

ου

 και 14

ου

 μισθού/σύνταξης.




Η πρώτη φάση συγκέντρωσης υπογραφών θα ολοκληρωθεί 8 του Δεκέμβρη και οι  πρώτες υπογραφές θα επιδοθούν στο υπουργείο Οικονομικών στην Αθήνα και στο Υφυπουργείο Μακεδονίας-Θράκης στη Θεσσαλονίκη, στο πλαίσιο κινητοποιήσεων που θα πραγματοποιηθούν στα μέσα Δεκέμβρη  που παραδοσιακά καταβάλλονταν το Δώρο Χριστουγέννων.




Η συγκέντρωση των υπογραφών θα γίνει υπογράφοντας στον σύνδεσμο που έχει επισυναφθεί (ΔΕΙΤΕ ΠΑΡΑΚΑΤΩ), αλλά και με συγκέντρωση υπογραφών συνταξιούχων και εργαζομένων από κάθε σωματείο ηλεκτρονικά και έντυπα.




ΑΝΑΛΥΤΙΚΑ ΤΟ ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΚΑΙ Η ΚΑΜΠΑΝΙΑ:




Συνεχίζουμε και με αποφασιστικότητα και αγώνα διεκδικούμε την 13

η

– 14

η

 σύνταξη / μισθό.




 

Συγκέντρωση Πέμπτη 15/10, 6μμ, άγαλμα Βενιζέλου




Τα Σωματεία των εργαζομένων στο Δημόσιο και των συνταξιούχων μετά τις επιτυχημένες κινητοποιήσεις την Πέμπτη 15 Οκτώβρη, με αιτήματα την 

επαναφορά του 13ου–14ου μισθού/σύνταξης, τις ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις σε μισθούς και συντάξεις και τη λήψη μέτρων κατά της ακρίβειας, καλούν   την Πέμπτη 12 του Νοέμβρη νέα συγκέντρωση στις 6μ.μ. στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου. 




Οι συνταξιούχοι και οι εργαζόμενοι μέσα από τα σωματεία τους με αποφασιστικότητα και υπερασπιζόμενοι το δίκαιο του αγώνα τους 

συνεχίζουν και  ενισχύουν τον κοινό τους αγώνα,

 με κοινές παρεμβάσεις και κινητοποιήσεις για την ανάδειξη των οξυμμένων οικονομικών προβλημάτων που αντιμετωπίζουν εργαζόμενοι και συνταξιούχοι και τη διεκδίκηση ουσιαστικών λύσεων στα αιτήματά τους.




Συνάδελφοι, συναδέλφισσες




Δεν αποδεχόμαστε να θεωρούνται κόστος 

η επαναφορά του  13ου–14ου μισθού/σύνταξης, οι αυξήσεις στις συντάξεις και στους μισθούς, η δημόσια Παιδεία, Υγεία, Πρόνοια και Ασφάλιση, ενώ οι πολεμικοί εξοπλισμοί και τα συμφέροντα των επιχειρηματικών ομίλων αποτελούν προτεραιότητα

. Την ώρα που δισεκατομμύρια κατευθύνονται σε εξοπλισμούς, πολεμικές συμφωνίες και στην αποπληρωμή του δημόσιου χρέους, οι κοινωνικές ανάγκες μπαίνουν σε δεύτερη μοίρα. 

Τα πρωτογενή πλεονάσματα και η υπέρβαση των φορολογικών εσόδων επιτυγχάνονται στις πλάτες του λαού

, τη στιγμή που η 

ακρίβεια σε τρόφιμα, φάρμακα, ενέργεια και στέγαση εξανεμίζει το εισόδημα εργαζομένων και συνταξιούχων 

και οι μεγάλοι επιχειρηματικοί όμιλοι καταγράφουν τεράστια κέρδη.




Το ζήτημα δεν είναι αν υπάρχουν χρήματα, αλλά ποιες ανάγκες επιλέγει η κυβέρνηση να χρηματοδοτεί.




Δεν ζητάμε ελεημοσύνη και προεκλογικά φιλοδωρήματα. Διεκδικούμε όσα μας ανήκουν! 

Προτεραιότητά μας είναι οι κοινωνικές ανάγκες, η αξιοπρεπής ζωή, η ειρήνη και η δικαιοσύνη μεταξύ των λαών — όχι οι εξοπλισμοί, οι πόλεμοι και οι γενοκτονίες.




Με το πλαίσιο αιτημάτων που έχουμε συνδιαμορφώσει και 

προτάσσοντας την επαναφορά της 13ης -14ης σύνταξης/μισθού συνεχίζουμε.

 Δεν προσαρμοζόμαστε στη φτώχεια, την εξαθλίωση και τον πόλεμο. 

Δεν γινόμαστε θεατές στη λεηλασία του εισοδήματός μας, στην κατάρρευση των δημόσιων αγαθών, παιδείας, υγείας κ.λπ. και στο τσάκισμα των δικαιωμάτων μας.




Οι συνταξιούχοι εκπαιδευτικοί μαζί με τους εργαζόμενους, με τη δύναμη του δίκιου, την αλήθεια των αναγκών και το κοινωνικό συμφέρον, διεκδικούν:




Επαναφορά 13

ης

– 14

ης 

σύνταξης – μισθού, 1400 βασικός μισθός – σύνταξη,  κατάργηση της εισφοράς αλληλεγγύης,  μπλόκο στην ακρίβεια με κατάργηση ΕΦΚ/ΦΠΑ στα είδη λαϊκής κατανάλωσης, μέτρα για τα ενοίκια και την κατοικία.




Όλοι/ες την  Πέμπτη 12 Νοέμβρη 2026, ώρα 6μ.μ.  στη συγκέντρωση στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου.







Καμπάνια συλλογής υπογραφών για την άμεση επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού και της

 

13ης-14ης σύνταξης




Εμείς που υπογράφουμε το παρακάτω κείμενο εργαζόμενοι, συνταξιούχοι, συλλογικότητες και κοινωνικοί φορείς 

απαιτούμε την άμεση επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης.




Η κατάργησή τους από τα χρόνια των μνημονίων ήταν άδικη, κοινωνικά ανάλγητη, νομικά ευάλωτη, οικονομικά αναποτελεσματική, ενώ ψευδώς και παραπλανητικά θεωρήθηκε ως προσωρινή.




Ο 13ος-14ος μισθός/σύνταξη  αποτελεί μια απολύτως δίκαιη κοινωνική κατάκτηση. Πρόκειται για «

αναβληθέντα μισθό

» για τον οποίο μάλιστα έχουν γίνει εφ’ όρου ζωής οι ανάλογες κρατήσεις.




Εδώ και 16 χρόνια κάθε δημόσιος υπάλληλος και συνταξιούχος έχει 

στερηθεί 

από το πενιχρό του εισόδημα ποσό άνω των

 35.000 ευρώ

! Μια κλοπή που συνεχίζεται στο διηνεκές.




Αν συνυπολογιστούν το σύνολο των περικοπών, μόνο στις συντάξεις των απομάχων της δουλειάς (περικοπές σε μισθούς, στις κύριες και επικουρικές συντάξεις, στο εφάπαξ, επιβολή εισφοράς αλληλεγγύης, προσωρινή διαφορά, εισφορά περίθαλψης 6% κ.λπ.) αυτές υπερβαίνουν το αστρονομικό ποσό των 

160 δισ.

!




Επιπλέον, η άθλια κατάσταση του συστήματος δημόσιας υγείας, εκτός από τις καταστροφικές επιπτώσεις στην υγεία μας, επιβαρύνει υπέρογκα τους εργαζομένους και συνταξιούχους σε όφελος των ιδιωτικών παρόχων υγείας μειώνοντας περαιτέρω το εισόδημά τους.




Την ίδια στιγμή, η 

ακρίβεια 

στα είδη πρώτης ανάγκης (τρόφιμα, στέγη, ενέργεια, καύσιμα, φάρμακα κ.λπ.) έχει αποκτήσει ιλιγγιώδεις ρυθμούς, ενώ τα κέρδη των ολίγων (εταιρείες ενέργειας, σουπερμάρκετ, τραπεζών, εισηγμένων στο χρηματιστήριο κ.λπ.) καλπάζουν με φρενήρεις ρυθμούς.




Η επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης  θεωρείται από τους ιθύνοντες «δημοσιονομικά αδύνατη» ή «τρέλα», όταν την ίδια στιγμή τεράστιοι δημόσιοι πόροι κατευθύνονται σε παράλογους και επικίνδυνους πολεμικούς εξοπλισμούς, εξυπηρέτηση του παράνομου και επονείδιστου ληστρικού χρέους, ενίσχυση με διάφορους τρόπους της οικονομικής ολιγαρχίας (επιδοτήσεις, φοροαπαλλαγές, παραχώρηση δημόσιου πλούτου κ.λπ.), σε αμέτρητα σκάνδαλα κατάχρησης και

 διασπάθισης δημόσιου χρήματος και ασφαλιστικών εισφορών

 σε ημετέρους.




Η άμεση επαναφορά του 13

ου

-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης είναι επείγον, επιτακτικό, στοιχειώδες αίτημα επιβίωσης και αξιοπρέπειας.




Καλούμε την κυβέρνηση να προχωρήσει άμεσα στην επαναφορά τους και όλα τα πολιτικά κόμματα να δεσμευτούν σε αυτό.




Παράλληλα,

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Groups defy gov’t plea to postpone mass actions
content:
Progressive groups led by Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) protest outside the House of Representatives while lawmakers’ briefing on Pax Silica is ongoing on Wednesday, November 11. (Charles Edmon Perez/Pinoy Weekly)

Where is the respect for farmers and Aytas who will be evicted from their communities because of Pax Silica?

This is the response of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) in Malacañang’s recent public statement to “show courtesy” as the Philippines hosts the 49th ASEAN Summit from November 15 to 18.

“We will hold protests before, during, and after the ASEAN Summit and Trump’s visit,” the group said in a statement. US President Donald Trump is expected to arrive in the Philippines next week.

In a press briefing on November 10, Malacañang’s Press Officer Claire Castro appealed to the protesters not to schedule rallies during the arrival of the international delegations and “show the genuine hospitality and good character of the Filipino people.”

“Respect for visitors? How about respect for vendors and urban poor displaced by ‘clearing operations’? Where is the respect for farmers and Aytas who will be evicted from their communities because of Pax Silica?” Bayan asked.

Bayan, together with multi-sectoral groups, launched the 12 days of protest which kicked off on November 4. The group stressed that the Philippine government should not welcome “war criminals and foreign plunderers” like Trump at the expense of the Filipino people’s welfare and their right to protest.

The Philippine National Police increased the number of personnel to more than 23,000, coming from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO), Armed Forces of the Philippines, Bureau of Fire Protection, and other concerned agencies.

Human rights group Karapatan described the ASEAN preparations as “over-the-top” and are reminiscent of the huge police deployment during the State of the Nation Address (SONA) last July.

“And we all know how that played out. Fifty-one protesters were arrested even before the protest program began, with many of those arrested taken merely because they wore black,” said Cristina Palabay, secretary-general of Karapatan. “This is our country, and we have every right to protest, especially when the policies and actions of these very visitors threaten our people’s rights and interests. US President Donald Trump is not merely a guest whose presence demands deference. The US is actively intervening in our country’s affairs, advancing its economic and military interests at the expense of Filipino sovereignty and people’s rights.”

The United States leads the Pax Silica Initiative, which plans to establish a 4,000-acre industrial hub within the Philippines’ Luzon Economic Corridor. Described as the first “AI-native industrial acceleration hub,” the proposed site is being positioned as an economic security zone intended to strengthen shared supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, electronics, and other goods.

Read: ‘Pax Silica’ initiative seen as war production, environment destruction

Progressive groups also assailed the worsening economic situation amid grand preparations for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

Independent think tank group IBON Foundation said that the current low wages failed to keep up with the country’s inflation — climbing up to 7.8 percent in October from 7.2 percent in September. The group stressed that rising prices of these commodities, along with rice, are affecting poor and low income families.

The unemployment in the country also increased by almost 909,000, according to the data of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), though the IBON Foundation argued that the number could be higher.

The number of unemployed Filipinos has raised the Philippine unemployment rate to 5.4 percent, making it the highest among its Southeast Asian neighbors based on the latest data in Indonesia (4.8%), Malaysia (2.9%), Vietnam (2.2%), Singapore (2%), and Thailand (0.9%).

The Philippines is also performing the poorest in terms of economic performance, compared to its counterparts in Southeast Asia. It has among the lowest GDP growth in the region at 2.1 percent compared to Brunei (0.02%), Thailand (1.9%), Malaysia (5.3%), Singapore (5.4%), Indonesia (5.5%) and Vietnam (10%).

“The government’s business-as-usual approach is worsening joblessness, eroding incomes and making the cost of living soar for millions of Filipinos,” said IBON Foundation, warning the administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that the country is rapidly heading towards stagflation. They called on the government to increase spending on agricultural production, support small enterprises, and boost household purchasing power.

Urban poor group Kalipunan ng Damayang Mahihirap (Kadamay) said in a statement that the rising prices of fuel and basic commodities and the temporary displacement of the informal workers affected by the ASEAN Summit are pushing the Filipino families at greater risk.

“Where will the driver get money to buy food for their family? What budget will vendors make if they have no income? What about their children’s school allowance? No matter how much Marcos Jr. tries to cover it up, he cannot hide the glaring poverty in the country,” said Kadamay secretary-general Mimi Doringo.

The transport group Piston will hold a nationwide strike. Farmers and indigenous groups will also organize camp-outs bringing their issues from the countryside to the city for the ASEAN delegates and Trump to hear.

Karapatan said that they stand in solidarity with the Filipino people “as they courageously assert their legitimate demands in the face of heightened repression.”

“The people will not be silenced or intimidated into surrendering their rights and sovereignty for the sake of the Marcos regime’s hosting of the ASEAN Summit,” Palabay concluded. (RTS, AMU, DAA)

title: Gabriela sweeps away Trump’s Pax Silica
content:
Those who violate the rights and well-being of women and children are not welcome in the Philippines.

MANILA – “Stop the rape of our motherland! Kick Trump out!”

This is the call of progressive women’s group Gabriela during a protest near the US Embassy, November 9. The women’s group asserted that there should be no red carpet welcome to warmongerers like Trump.

Jacq Ruiz, spokesperson of Kilusan ng Manggagawang Kababaihan (KMK) said, “There is no special treatment for us women workers, who remain mired in extreme poverty, while billions of pesos are being allocated solely for preparations for the signing of the Pax Silica agreement.”

Read: Economic insecurity of women workers worsen

While Filipino culture is known for warmly welcoming visitors with a feast, they said Trump is an exception as many Filipino households are struggling to put even a decent meal on their own tables.

For a mother like Lanie Buena, 54, it is a struggle to get through the day. She is working as a manicurist and pedicurist in their house in Quezon City for eight years while her husband is working as a barber.

She earns P400 or about $6 for three clients in a day. But this is not enough, she said, as there are no guaranteed clients every day.

What she earns, she said, is not adequate for a family of seven with two students still going to school. There are still household expenses such as electricity and water bills.

Meanwhile, Gabriela Women’s Partylist Rep. Sarah Elago said, “Those who violate the rights and well-being of women and children are not welcome in the Philippines.”

Elago condemned Trump, calling him a macho-fascist and a war criminal, citing his role in waging and escalating wars that have claimed countless civilian lives, including children in Palestine. She added that Trump’s links to the Epstein files makes him less welcome in the country.

The Trump administration’s war against Iran and its support to Israel has contributed to a global oil price shock, with its effects now being felt by Filipino families from rising fuel costs to increasing cost of goods in the market.

The women’s group said they are determined to ensure that Trump will not receive a warm welcome but instead will be faced by massive protests rejecting his visit and the proposed Pax Silica Initiatives.

“What we will present is a flaming protest, because individuals like Donald—a rapist, molester, and war criminal—are utterly shameless and devoid of any moral compass,” said Elle Buntag, spokesperson of Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns. (AMU, RVO)
