È una tendenza ormai conclamata il progressivo smantellamento dei servizi dell’azienda regionale del diritto allo studio (ARDSU), tramite privatizzazione o riduzione dei benefici erogati. Questo succede tramite diverse strategie, tra i quali l’innalzamento spropositato dei costi della mensa o l’esternalizzazione dei servizi, e quindi dellə lavoratorə. Noi non staremo a guardare mentre ci levano il terreno sotto i piedi. Per questo chiediamo:







Che tuttə lə idoneə siano beneficiariə, e che le graduatorie definitive vadano in base all’ISEE, e non al numero dei CFU conseguiti. Al momento, infatti, nelle graduatorie l’ISEE conta al







20%, mentre il numero di CFU- quindi la quantità di esami che sei riuscite a dare – conta per il restante 80%.







Che lə studentə beneficiariə del posto alloggio ricevano subito una soluzione abitativa. Basta attese di mesi per avere il diritto che ci spetta.




Di ridefinire il tempo massimo del conseguimento dei CFU necessari al mantenimento della borsa di studio, considerando anche l’appello di settembre come sessione utile per questo fine. Di conseguenza, dilatare i tempi per la richiesta di borsa.




Che il contributo affitto sia una possibilità realmente percorribile per tuttə: la possibilità di richiesta deve essere aperta tutto l’anno e deve essere garantito a tuttə lə studentə beneficiariə di posto alloggio che non hanno ottenuto il posto in residenza.




Che la mensa ritorni ad avere prezzi calmierati e accessibili per tuttə, non soltanto per le fasce di reddito più basso.




Che le strutture delle residenze siano realmente adeguate per lə studentə che le abitano. Vogliamo: manutenzioni e interventi strutturali immediati dove servono, wi-fi e lavatrici gratuite in tutte le residenze, cucine funzionanti.




Che vengano aumentate le linee di trasporto pubblico nei pressi dei complessi universitari, fuori e dentro il centro storico della città. Che ci siano agevolazioni concrete anche per i treni e le linee extraurbane usate dallə studentə pendolari.

title: First Gen Z Congresswoman: DSA's Melat Kiros on Corruption, Medicare for All & Israel
content:
The Democratic Socialists of America made major gains in this year’s U.S. midterms, electing not just the largest-ever socialist bloc to Congress, but also winning dozens of races at the state, county and municipal levels. 

Democracy Now!

 spoke with Congressmember-elect Melat Kiros on election night following her victory in Denver, Colorado. She identified Medicare for All as her top priority and said progressives must lay the groundwork “so that in ’29, when we have the House, the Senate and the White House, we can sign it into law on day one.”




Kiros is a 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant and lawyer. In 2023, Kiros wrote an open letter about the danger of conflating antisemitism and criticism of Israel, for which she was fired by her law firm. She won a major upset in the Democratic primary earlier this year against longtime incumbent Congressmember Diana DeGette.

title: Vademecum di resistenza legale. Sanzioni amministrative pecuniarie e iter giudiziario
content:
Le sanzioni amministrative sono uno strumento per colpire il dissenso. I decreti sicurezza del governo Meloni hanno rafforzato un impianto normativo che corrode i diritti d’espressione e a manifestare, sanciti dall’artt.17 e 21 della Costituzione. 




Riprendiamo da Torino per Gaza




Manifestare diventa sempre più una “concessione” o un “permesso” delle Autorità, spesso limitato da prescrizioni. Sottoponendo chi manifesta a un rischio economico permanente, mentre economia di guerra e carovita, intrecciate alla situazione geopolitica e alla crisi ecoclimatica ci asfissiano, si produce un effetto intimidatorio aggravando la minaccia della repressione economica.

In questo quadro, il D.L. 23/2026, convertito dalla L. 54/2026 ha modificato l’art.18 del TULPS (prevede che le manifestazioni in luogo pubblico siano preventivamente – almeno tre giorni prima – comunicate alla Questura), intervenendo in modo significativo sul sistema sanzionatorio delle manifestazioni pubbliche. La violazione dell’obbligo di preavviso è stata depenalizzata, cioè trasformata da reato in illecito amministrativo, punito con una sanzione pecuniaria. Lo stesso è avvenuto per la violazione dei divieti e delle prescrizioni del Questore, e sono state introdotte nuove sanzioni anche per altre condotte tenute durante le manifestazioni. Le sanzioni arrivano fino a 12.000 euro, senza possibilità di pagamento in misura ridotta, e aumentano per chi accumula più violazioni.

Quest’evoluzione è parte della rappresaglia governativa per il “Blocchiamo tutto”, le proteste sindacali e degli attivisti per la giustizia climatica. La mobilitazione dal basso ha dimostrato i limiti di questi tentativi di imbrigliare e criminalizzare la legittima resistenza popolare. La stessa repressione con cui il governo risponde altro non è che il risultato dell’efficacia di quelle mobilitazioni e pratiche.




La difesa legale e l’iniziativa politica possono procedere insieme e rafforzarsi a vicenda. Questo è il modo concreto per ostacolare l’applicazione dei decreti sicurezza e organizzarsi collettivamente per non pagare alcuna sanzione e spuntare una delle principali armi della repressione.

Dobbiamo organizzarci per resistere agli attacchi, trasformando ogni tentativo di colpirci in un’occasione di solidarietà e di rilancio della mobilitazione. Dove ci vogliono isolati e soli noi reagiamo collettivamente.

Bando all’improvvisazione: dobbiamo dotarci di strumenti per affrontare ogni singolo attacco e trasformarlo in un terreno di crescita e avanzamento delle nostre lotte. Pertanto, abbiamo predisposto un Vademecum su come affrontare queste sanzioni.







Il Vademecum è stato redatto assieme a legali che in Italia si stanno organizzando per affrontare la difesa delle persone e dei movimenti colpiti.




Oltre al mancato preavviso, sono sanzionate anche la violazione dei divieti e delle prescrizioni del Questore, la presa di parola nelle riunioni non preavvisate, il mancato rispetto del percorso, la turbativa e la promozione della riunione online o in gruppi chiusi. Per chi accumula più violazioni le sanzioni aumentano da un terzo alla metà.

Se ricevi una sanzione amministrativa per art.18 TULPS come modificato dall’art. 9 del D.L. 23/2026, convertito dalla L. 54/2026, ti consigliamo di NON PAGARE ALCUNA SANZIONE nell’immediato, di rivolgerti alle reti solidali e a un legale di tua fiducia per predisporre il ricorso. Ecco in breve come si procede




⇩

VERBALE DI ACCERTAMENTO E CONTESTAZIONE

Redatto dall’organo accertatore (Questura/DIGOS, Carabinieri…), descrive il fatto imputato e le violazioni contestate e avvisa che la sanzione (da 1.000 a 10.000 €, che passano da 1.000 a 12.000 € per la violazione di divieti e prescrizioni – Sul verbale la multa è indicata come minimi e massimi ma non è quantificata) verrà successivamente quantificata dal Prefetto con un’ordinanza-ingiunzione.




Tale verbale deve arrivare entro 90 giorni dall’accertamento, indicando in 30 giorni la possibilità di effettuare scritti difensivi presso il Prefetto. È possibile, secondo valutazioni proprie e confrontandosi con i propri legali, presentare scritti difensivi in questa fase e chiedere di essere ascoltati personalmente dal Prefetto (il verbale non si impugna davanti al giudice!).

Se invece il verbale arriva oltre il termine, la sanzione si estingue (conserva la busta e la data di notifica!).




⇩

ORDINANZA – INGIUNZIONE PREFETTIZIA

L’ordinanza-ingiunzione, emessa dal Prefetto a sua discrezione, definisce la somma sanzionata. Le ingiunzioni hanno tempo 5 anni per essere erogate. Queste, possono arrivare anche molto tempo dopo il verbale. Il limite è la prescrizione: 5 anni dalla violazione. Ogni atto notificato (il verbale, l’ordinanza, una cartella) fa ripartire il conteggio da capo. Conserva sempre tutte le buste con le date di notifica: servono all’avvocato per verificare se la sanzione è prescritta. Attenzione: può essere recapitata anche tramite l’app “IO” dove i termini possono decorrere anche se non apri il messaggio!

A questo punto scattano 30 giorni dalla notifica per fare ricorso al Giudice di Pace del luogo dei fatti (in alcuni casi la competenza potrebbe essere del Tribunale).

Chi ha un reddito basso (fino a (13.659,64 euro) può chiedere il patrocinio a spese dello Stato.




SE NON CONCOSCI UN AVVOCATO, CHIEDI IL RIFERIMENTO ALL’ASSEMBLEA!




⇩

RICORSO

Il ricorso richiede un costo di contributo unificato.

Il Giudice di Pace fissa un’udienza che può essere con sospensiva del pagamento.

Nel ricorso, oltre ai motivi relativi al singolo caso, si può eccepire l’illegittimità costituzionale della norma. In udienza l’avvocat* potrà chiedere al giudice di rimettere la questione alla Corte costituzionale. Se il giudice la ritiene rilevante e non manifestamente infondata, sospende il giudizio in attesa della decisione della Corte.




Obiettivo politico della resistenza legale e collettiva è arrivare alla dichiarazione di incostituzionalità.

Se invece il Giudice non accoglie il rinvio alla Corte Costituzionale, potrà confermare la sanzione, rideterminarla o annullarla. Si potrà eventualmente procedere in Appello e in Cassazione.




⇩

LA CASSA DI RESISTENZA

Per tradurre la risposta collettiva, disinnescare il ricatto della repressione economica a livello individuale e fare fronte alle spese legali, viene messa a disposizione la Cassa di resistenza legale promossa da Torino per Gaza.




Se hai bisogno, chiedi sostengo. Se sei un solidale o un’organizzazione, contribuisci alla Cassa promuovendo raccolte fondi!

Puoi contribuire attraverso il crowdfunding:

https://www.produzionidalbasso.com/project/cassa-di-resistenza-blocchiamo-tutto-torino-2/







Se hai preso una multa, scrivici e organizziamoci insieme:

NESSUNA RESTA DA SOLA, NESSUNO RESTA DA SOLO!

Daniel Nichanianeditor-in-chief of Bolts, a publication that covers local politics and policy with a focus on voting rights and criminal justice.

We examine the results of Tuesday’s historic U.S. midterm elections with Daniel Nichanian, editor-in-chief of Bolts. In addition to taking back the House and Senate, Democrats also made major gains at the state level and will control a majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years. Democrats also flipped 12 state legislative chambers.

“The size of the wins for Democrats in statewide races was wild,” says Nichanian. He identifies protecting abortion access, bolstering unions and ending police cooperation with ICE as some of the priorities Democrats are likely to pursue.

Daniel Nichanianeditor-in-chief of Bolts, a publication that covers local politics and policy with a focus on voting rights and criminal justice.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: We begin today’s show continuing our look at Tuesday’s historic election. On the national level, Democrats took control of the House and Senate in a stunning rebuke of President Trump. Meanwhile, Democrats have flipped 12 state legislative chambers. In Arizona, Democrats are set to control the state Legislature for the first time in 60 years. In Pennsylvania, Democrats flipped the state Senate for the first time since 1994. And for the first time in 16 years, Democrats will hold a majority of governorships, including in Texas, where Gina Hinojosa is the first Democrat elected governor since Ann Richards in 1990.

Florida’s outgoing Republican Governor Ron DeSantis spoke Wednesday about Republican losses across the country.

GOV. RON DESANTIS: This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country as we have seen probably in the last hundred years. In January, when everyone in office leaves who are either term-limited or got voted out, of the 10 largest states in this union, only one state will have Republican control of their state: the state of Florida.

If you look at our chief rival, in a healthy sense, the state of Texas, and I would say over the last — over my lifetime, Texas has been the crown jewel of Republican politics. I think we’ve been the leader for Republicans and conservatives since I’ve been governor, but if you go over the whole generation, no one holds a candle on the Republican side to the Lone Star State. And yet, not only did they lose a very highly publicized U.S. Senate race, they lost everything — the governor, attorney general, all the other statewide. They lost four Republican Supreme Court justices on the Texas Supreme Court. They may even lose the Texas Legislature, or one house or even both. Let’s just be clear that that is going to hurt not just for the next two years. That’s something that can reverberate for the next decade or more. And if the Republican Party doesn’t have Texas as an anchor, then we are not going to be viable nationally going forward.

AMY GOODMAN: That was Florida’s Republican Governor Ron DeSantis.

Many political commentators have credited New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani with helping make affordability a central issue for Democrats. On Wednesday, Mayor Mamdani posted a video reacting to the midterm results.

MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI: Last night’s election proved working people expect more from their government, and they’re tired of waiting. JD Vance asked for a couple more years to finally fulfill the promises he’d made to our country. Working people can’t afford another two years to make rent that’s due this month, childcare for their kids or groceries for their family. People are tired of being told that there isn’t enough to go around, while Elon Musk becomes the world’s first trillionaire. They are tired of being told to sacrifice their land and water for data centers. They’re tired of being told their needs are unrealistic by politicians who have been bought by the wealthiest people on the planet. They’re tired of being told to ask for a little and expect even less.

And last night, the people stood up. They stood up to politicians that spend their taxpayer dollars on war crimes and genocide instead of on building schools and paving roads. They spoke louder than the hundreds of millions of dollars that tried and failed to buy this election. They demanded an end to the affordability crisis that has become one of the few things that unites us all. It is not enough to simply win power; we must use it. And the American people will know the difference between hollow words and hard work. For years we’ve had the debate. Now it’s time for us in the Democratic Party to deliver. My friends, it’s morning again in America.

AMY GOODMAN: Our first guest today has been closely looking at results in state races across the United States. Daniel Nichanian is editor-in-chief of Bolts, a publication that covers local politics and policy with a focus on voting rights and criminal justice, joining us now from Washington, D.C.

Daniel, thanks so much for being with us. I mean, you take a state like Texas, and Governor DeSantis focused on this when he talks about this election was a extinction-level event for Republicans. Now the leadership of Texas, both the governorship as well as the Senate, these two races, are Democrat. And this hasn’t happened in decades. You’ve looked at something that is less well known at this point after the election, which is what’s happening at the state levels in the state legislatures, and what all of this can mean. Lay out what your observations are after this historic election.

DANIEL NICHANIAN: So, I think the thing that we all know is that Republicans suffered very heavy losses for Congress. You were just talking about the big gains for Democrats in the Senate, where they could get up to 56 seats, and in the House. What is still coming into view at this moment is the sheer extent to which Republicans suffered similar losses — to be honest, even greater losses, unthinkable losses even — in state governments and local governments.

So, let’s take the state of Texas, which is really the story of the night and the symbol of the night that you were just discussing. Democrats, of course, flipped the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion, but that just hides so much that’s going on beyond the surface. They may have flipped the state Board of Education, which has drawn so many headlines over many years for injecting Christianity into schools. They flipped four seats on the state’s highest court, the Supreme Court, including electing a woman who will be the first LGBTQ statewide official in Texas. They flipped the state House. They flipped attorney general, railroad commissioner, land commissioner and so on.

And then, if you look down-ballot further down, the situation remains as dire for the GOP. So, in one of the biggest counties in the nation, home to Fort Worth, Democrats flipped the DA’s office. They flipped the county executive’s office. They flipped the county board. These are all important offices. This county drew a lot of headlines over the last few weeks for closing polling stations. They have lots of impacts on people’s lives. There was really nowhere that Republicans could hide on Tuesday to escape the wrath of voters, and this showed in state after state after state.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: So, hi, Daniel, so good to see you. So, what is your sense at the state and local level? What were voters most interested in? What made them vote Democrat this time?

DANIEL NICHANIAN: Well, it’s, you know, the similar reasons as we saw at the federal level: the cost of living. Democrats in Texas and Ohio and many states were really emphasizing the issue of data centers, immigration enforcement. And those are all issues where we are going to see now that Democrats took more power in state governments. We’re going to see actual potential changes being done at a level of government where that has a lot of effects on these — on these issues.

So, for instance, the Democrats took control of six state governments on Tuesday, perhaps seven if Alaska flips. We are still waiting for results there in the governor’s race. So, we’re talking about Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota and Nevada. Those all are states that became Democratic now. And some of these states, the Democrats haven’t governed for a very long time, and they’ve signaled the kind of agenda they want to bring. So, for instance, in Pennsylvania, which Democrats haven’t governed since the '90s, they've signaled they want to codify abortion rights into the state Constitution. In Wisconsin, where Democrats haven’t governed since 2010, they have signaled they want to repeal, abolish the anti-union law that Scott Walker very famously — it drew a lot of protests nationwide and in Wisconsin — passed in 2011. So, in a way, there’s a lot of issues that have built up, up until Tuesday.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: And, Daniel, you’ve also said — I mean, let’s talk about the places where the Democrats didn’t prevail, or at least don’t have, won’t have full control. Georgia, North Carolina, you say, is also because of gerrymandering, Republican gerrymandering. If you could explain?

DANIEL NICHANIAN: Right. I mean, you know, the story you may have heard out there over the past few days is that gerrymandering failed for Republicans in the U.S. House. They were trying to gerrymander their way into a majority. That didn’t succeed.

The situation is more nuanced if you look at the state level. Georgia and North Carolina are two states that saw huge tsunamis on Tuesday. The statewide offices flipped. The size of the wins for Democrats in statewide races was wild, I mean, unthinkable even. And yet, and yet, Democrats didn’t manage to win control of the state government. Why? Because the state Senate in both states is so aggressively gerrymandered that Democrats just couldn’t get over the hurdle.

In North Carolina, for instance, Democrats are one seat short of getting full control of the state government, despite the gerrymander. They won every seat that Trump won by up to 10 points. Any seat that Trump won by less than 10 flipped Democrat. And that wasn’t enough, because the median seat in North Carolina has been so gerrymandered, is so Republican, so that allowed Republicans to keep a foothold of power in states where, by all accounts, they really should have lost everything on Tuesday.

AMY GOODMAN: So, Daniel Nichanian, let’s talk about what states can do all over the country, the significance of states having power. I mean, you have the irony that with President Trump and with the Republicans, they’re often talking about states’ rights, but then they try to federalize everything from the election to law enforcement. So, if you can talk about, oh, states passing laws that ban local police and local sheriffs from collaborating with ICE, for example? Where can states assert themselves?

DANIEL NICHANIAN: I mean, that’s really important. It’s going to be a major storyline, looking ahead to 2027. On many of the issues that people look toward D.C., you know, states have a lot of power. That’s a great example, the issue of immigration, which was a driving factor for many voters, the opposition to Trump’s immigration policies and ICE over the last year and a half.

What we have seen, actually, since Trump came into power in 2025, came back into power, is a wave of states, of blue states, of Democratic-governed states, that have passed laws that have banned local police and local sheriffs from entering contracts with ICE. Now, that actually does — is very important, because ICE really relies on the collaboration of local sheriff agencies and police to expand its reach. For instance — for instance, sheriffs can rent space in their jails to ICE to hold immigrants. ICE can bring immigrants there, pay money to the sheriff’s department — by the way, it also puts more money into local law enforcement through that route — and that helps ICE do its operations. And so, nine states, nine Democratic-run states, since the beginning of 2025, have banned these sort of contracts. States like Virginia, New Mexico, Maryland have passed laws like that.

Now, the obvious question — I was listing earlier the list of states that Democrats have flipped. Are we going to see similar laws in Pennsylvania, in Wisconsin, in Arizona? These are all states where local sheriffs — there are some very far-right sheriffs in those states that have contracts with ICE. Are Democrats at the state level going to do something about it? So, that’s just an example of the kind of questions that this really opens up. And you could do that on issue after issue. What are Democrats going to do with the new authority they’re going to have in these states?

NERMEEN SHAIKH: And if you could speak, Daniel, specifically about unions, the states that have had extremely restrictive laws on unions? If you could just talk, for example, about Wisconsin or Nevada?

DANIEL NICHANIAN: Right. I mean, another issue where Democrats have not as systematically done recently, the politics around unions having shifted a bit. But Nevada, Wisconsin are — and others are states that have either passed a right-to-work law or — in Wisconsin, as I was saying earlier, it was really the — it was really one of the main issues when Republicans took power after the 2010 midterms. They went after unions in Wisconsin and other states. And Democrats, Democrats want to roll that back. And we’ll see. Also, there was an important referendum in Vermont on Tuesday that enshrined the right to join a union into the Constitution of the state of Vermont, and that also passed on Tuesday, so another important result.

AMY GOODMAN: We want to thank you, Daniel Nichanian, editor-in-chief of Bolts, a publication that covers local politics and policy with a focus on voting rights and criminal justice.

Coming up, we speak to Congressmember-elect Melat Kiros, the 29-year-old attorney, Ethiopian immigrant, member of the Democratic Socialists of America, who beat in the Democratic primary Congressmember DeGette, who was in office for almost 30 years. She will now represent Denver, Colorado, in the next Congress. Stay with us.

AMY GOODMAN: “Mean Love” by Sinkane, performing in our Democracy Now! studio.

author: Unknown
title: Cremona: sabato 7 novembre manifestazione “Adèss Baasta” contro carovita e riarmo
content:
Studenti e lavoratori pronti a scendere in piazza a Cremona contro il carovita e il riarmo: sabato 7 novembre si terrà infatti una manifestazione con lo slogan Adèss Baasta, che mira a riunire studenti, lavoratori, giovani e associazioni. Il ritrovo è fissato alle 14 nel parcheggio dell’ex Foro Boario, in via Mantova. La partenza del corteo è prevista per le 15.




Da Radio Onda d’Urto




Al centro della mobilitazione ci sono soprattutto il rincaro dei carburanti, l’aumento dei prezzi dei beni di consumo e il peso delle bollette. Nel testo che accompagna la locandina, gli organizzatori scrivono: “Il diesel ha superato i 2 euro al litro, la spesa costa di più ogni giorno, gli stipendi non bastano e l’inverno ci aspetta con bollette salatissime”. La protesta si rivolge anche alle scelte del Governo in materia di spesa pubblica e politica internazionale. Gli organizzatori contestano “i finanziamenti destinati agli armamenti e chiedono maggiori risorse per scuola, sanità, edilizia popolare e contrasto al carovita”. Tra le richieste indicate nel volantino c’è anche quella di “tassare gli extraprofitti” degli speculatori.




La mobilitazione viene presentata dagli organizzatori come parte di un più ampio clima di protesta nazionale, richiamando anche le giornate di sciopero generale del 30 ottobre e del 20 novembre e le iniziative di protesta di autotrasportatori, agricoltori, studenti e movimenti. 

Ad organizzare la manifestazione il collettivo studentesco “Corrente Z” col supporto di associazioni come Arci, Circolo Arcipelago, Arci Persichello, Fiom e sindacati di base.




La presentazione con Silvia dell’Arci Persichello di Cremona







Il Collettivo Studentesco Corrente Zeta si è dato appuntamento alle 13 all’autostazione per raggiungere poi tutti e tutte insieme il concentramento del corteo. Sentiamo Sofia del “Corrente Z” di Cremona

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Rural communities face continuing violence amid militarization
content:
Photo by Viggo Sarmago/Bulatlat

Under the blazing sun in front Camp Aguinaldo, palay hats stood out together with the line of banners. It was not a celebration for peasants — but a plea to end militarization, violence, and to serve justice for Negros 19 killed in Toboso, Negros Occidental on April 19, 2026.

Farmers and fisherfolk play a vital role in sustaining the nation’s food security and economy, yet they are the ones who struggle the most to survive.

Pamalakaya’s National Vice Chairperson Ronnel Arambulo stated in his speech during the fourth day of peasant month protest on October 19, that the administration does not aim to protect the life and rights of the people, farmers, and fisherfolk, but to protect the ruling class, the foreigners, and the people in power for their own personal interest.

Fisherfolks are also facing harassment that disrupts their lives. According to Arambulo, there are recent reports of intimidation in Binangonan, Rizal, where fisherfolk were called by Maritime Police to appear at the municipal hall. They were later summoned to renounce and abandon Pamalakaya.

This kind of intimidation is not confined to the province of Rizal, as similar deployments have also been reported in other regions.

Nida Barcenas from Karapatan-Bicol stated that the 9th Infantry “Spear” Division of Philippine Army or at least ten battalions of men in uniform were scattered around six provinces in Bicol region.

During the “Stakeholder and Media Fellowship Night: Episode 1 – Kaakibat sa Kapayapaan,” event of 9th Infantry Division held on April 18, 2026 at Camp Elias Angeles, Maj. Gen. Aldwine I. Almase recognized the efforts of national agencies, local government units, media personalities, and other stakeholders in countering alleged local terrorist activities to ensure peace and safety in the Bicol region.

For Karapatan-Bicol , however, these achievements actually meant human rights abuses against farmers communities. As of March 2026, Karapatan has recorded 46 political prisoners in Bicol — 9 of them are women, with 22 arrested under Marcos Jr. administration. In his four year term in the government, two enforced disappearances and 38 extrajudicial killings have also been documented.

Red-tagging, violence, and land grabbing continue to disrupt the lives of Bicolanos, Barcenas said.

“To this day, residents of Masbate continue to appeal for help amid alleged land grabbing by Governor Kho. Farmers are being driven off their lands, and those who resist are killed and red-tagged as NPAs, [New People’s Army]” Barcenas said.

The issue involving Governor Antonio Kho is also part of the problem regarding land dispute over the Pecson Estate in Cawayan, Masbate. Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) stated that Kho took over a portion of 1,807-hectare estate, forcing more than 100 farmers off the lands they have cultivated for years.

The agrarian conflict has also been associated with reports of killing involving peasants in Cawayan. A human rights report from Karapatan revealed cases including killings of farmers named Pancho Versaga and Renard Remulta on October 28, 2022 in Sitio Villaluna, Barangay Itom-Bato, Cawayan. These two were among more than 100 farmers tilling a 450-hectare portion of the Pecson Estate within land seized by Kho in Masbate.

Karapatan has declared Masbate as Bicol’s killing fields due to an increasing number of victims who had been killed under Marcos Jr. regime’s counter-insurgency war on the province.

One of the heinous cases was the killing of a farmer couple Aimee and Jover Villegas, a two-hectare land caretaker. The military said that the couple died under armed encounters. However, their injuries contradict this claim as Aimee’s throat, chin, and neck had been slashed, while Jover sustained gunshot wounds in the nape and back.

Echoing this concern, Grace Nabian from Amihan-Negros called for a stop to the militarization in rural communities.

She questioned killings, abduction, and threats against farmers, stressing that land reform, and access to quality education for their children are what they need.

She also pressed his demand to hold Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) accountable for various deaths in their land including Negros 19.

During an afternoon mass in a collective protest campout in front of the Department of Agrarian Reform, Sol Santuyo, mother of Maureen Santuyo, emphasized the long-overdue demand of farmers that were ignored by the government.

“From then until now, our farmers have had one cry, but those in power deliberately turn a deaf ear. I hope a better way is found, so that no more youth would have to risk their lives just to help our farmers,” Santuyo, whose daughter was among those killed in Toboso, said.

Various organizations along with other student activists continue to call for justice for Santuyo, Alyssa Alano, RJ Ledesma, and Errol Wendell, Lyle Prijoles, Kai Sorem, and others but to all farmers, fisherfolk, journalists, and residents who were killed, abducted, threatened, and deprived of land and rights. author: Joshua Davis, Whitney K. Taylor
title: Federal Government Is Targeting Officials Who Are Trying to Hold ICE Accountable
content:
This story was co-published with

 

Truthout

.




In the months leading up to the 2026 midterm elections, congressional Republicans and federal prosecutors have targeted dozens of local officials in cities and counties across the country that have adopted some sanctuary policies. The investigations have increasingly focused on prosecutors and law enforcement officers, many of whom have publicly announced plans to go after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents who commit crimes in their jurisdictions or refuse demands to cooperate with federal immigration policing.




In total, 65 officials in 16 states have been targeted since January, according to a review of documents released by the 

House Judiciary

 

Committee

 and the 

Department of Justice

 (DOJ), as well as interviews with senior officials who have direct knowledge of individual investigations. The House Judiciary Committee has issued subpoenas and other demands for testimony, documents, and records to more than 40 officials, 15 of them local prosecutors. Alongside that, the DOJ has initiated investigations into 50 local or state officials since 2025, including five involving local prosecutors. In all, 17 local prosecutors have been swept up in House Judiciary or DOJ investigations and lawsuits related to immigration policies.




House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jim Jordan said in a recent 

report

 that “Democrats’ open-borders policies at the federal level and sanctuary policies at the state and local level allow millions of illegal aliens to pour into the country and ensure that criminal aliens, after encountered by local law enforcement, are released back into American communities,” echoing language the committee has commonly used in its investigations.




Many experts describe these investigations as unprecedented, and view the move as retaliation against local officials who refuse to cooperate with federal immigration agents or threaten legal action against ICE officers.




“These [prosecutors] are being intentionally intimidated by congressional and federal authorities,” said Mona Sahaf, the director of the Reshaping Prosecution initiative at the Vera Institute of Justice. “The use of [the] DOJ to target perceived political opponents is new. It’s busting norms, and it’s highly dangerous.”




The targeting of local prosecutors appears to be a matter of policy in the second Trump administration. “

Sanctuary Jurisdictions Directives

” issued by the attorney general’s office on February 5, 2025, held that the DOJ Civil Rights Division should “identify state and local laws, policies, and practices that facilitate violations of federal immigration laws or impede lawful federal immigration operations,” and “where appropriate, take legal action to challenge such laws, policies, or practices.”













The Appeal in Your Inbox




Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.
































          Sign Up
        
















The DOJ, in a June 18 

press release

 announcing an investigation into local officials in Philadelphia — including District Attorney Larry Krasner — concerning a policy prohibiting federal agents from wearing masks, said that its “series of lawsuits brought by the Civil Division” targeted “illegal policies designed to thwart federal law enforcement across the country.”




Rebecca Roiphe, the Joseph Solomon Distinguished Professor of Law at New York Law School, said the investigations into local prosecutors represented “a wholesale abandonment” of the principle of separation between the DOJ and the political branches of government. “This administration has pretty openly suggested that it is normal and appropriate and even laudable for the political branches to have some degree of control over the Department of Justice,” she said.




Referring to the DOJ investigations, Roiphe said, “The bottom line is that these federal prosecutions can end up threatening local prosecutors to fall in line with federal priorities, and that’s illegitimate in our system.”




These overlapping investigations, reports, and the DOJ directives follow the Heritage Foundation’s 

Project 2025 threat to “initiate legal action against” prosecutors

 who refuse to adhere to the priorities of the Trump administration. For many of the targeted prosecutors, the political influence has become impossible to ignore.




Among the targeted is Parisa Dehghani-Tafti, the top prosecutor in Arlington, Virginia, who drew the ire of Representative Jordan’s committee on multiple occasions, including when she 

declined to charge

 an activist who handed out flyers containing the home address of Deputy White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, citing concerns over First Amendment-protected free speech.




In a July 1 letter to Dehghani-Tafti, Jordan 

described

 Dehghani-Tafti’s decision not to charge as “politically-motivated actions in a case involving a far-left agitator’s disturbing campaign to threaten, harass, and dox a senior White House official and his family” and accused her office of having “sanctuary policies that prioritize illegal and criminal aliens over American citizens.”




Dehghani-Tafti, who characterized the House Judiciary actions as “pathetic,” denies any wrongdoing and suggests that these investigations are the result of her political opponents’ inability to defeat her electorally.




“They can’t beat us at the polls, and so they’re being undemocratic about it and trying to undermine the voters,” she told 

Truthout

.




In total, Jordan and the House Judiciary Committee have issued three letters and a subpoena to Dehghani-Tafti, in addition to writing an 

interim report

 on her in September, which was largely based on a July 

closed-door deposition

. Following the report, the DOJ Civil Rights Division informed Dehghani-Tafti that she was under investigation following a referral from the House Judiciary, according to a senior official with direct knowledge of the investigation.




“None of this is normal,” Dehghani-Tafti said. “What they’re doing is taking mechanisms that are designed to uphold the rule of law and perverting them. And that is not normal, except for authoritarians.”




Dehghani-Tafti was not the only Northern Virginia prosecutor to be on the receiving end of both House Judiciary and DOJ investigations. The top prosecutor for Fairfax County, Virginia, Steve Descano, similarly received three letters and a subpoena, and was the subject of an interim report from Jordan’s committee. The 

report

, “Fairfax County, Virginia: The Dangerous Consequences of Sanctuary Policies,” claims that a 2019 campaign promise to make “charging and plea decisions that limit or avoid immigration consequences” is discriminatory and violates federal law. The report goes on to accuse Descano’s office of “efforts to erase national borders and undermine immigration enforcement.”




Descano declined to comment for this story, citing the ongoing investigations. His chief of staff, Laura Birnbaum, directed 

Truthout

 to prior official statements issued by his office, including an October 20 response to the House Judiciary report. “This ‘report’ is nothing more than recycled Republican talking points put out weeks before the midterm elections as a desperate attempt to distract from widely anticipated Republican losses,” wrote Birnbaum.




Responding to the DOJ investigation, Descano’s office released a statement in May that accused the Trump administration “of misusing the Justice Department to launch partisan attacks.”




Both Dehghani-Tafti and Descano belong to a 

small coalition of prosecutors

 from cities across the U.S. that declared an intention to prosecute federal agents who commit crimes in their cities. The alliance — the Fight Against Federal Overreach — which intentionally takes its name from the slang acronym FAFO, formed in January in part as a response to the deadly ICE shootings of 

Alex Pretti

 and 

Renee Good

 in Minneapolis that same month. Less than a year later, nearly half of the group’s founding members have found themselves under investigation by the DOJ.




“No other administration has ever done things like this,”said Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, who has been a target of DOJ investigators.




Moriarty, whose jurisdiction includes Minneapolis, made 

national

 

headlines

 in January when she announced a state-level investigation into the shooting of Good by ICE agent Jonathan Ross. Just days later, the DOJ subpoenaed four Minnesota officials, including Gov. Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison, as part of an investigation into whether they impeded federal immigration agents during “

Operation Metro Surge

.” News reports initially 

incorrectly

 

named

 Moriarty among the officials who received a subpoena, though it was later revealed that she did not receive one. Moriarty told 

Truthout

 she believes that her name was released intentionally by government officials to intimidate her.




Viewed in isolation, these actions may appear to be singular responses during an exceptional political moment, but taken together, the data suggest a wider attempt to punish officials who try to thwart federal immigration policies.




“The story is there — if you speak up and work to hold police accountable, we will come after you,” said Sahaf, referring to the House Judiciary and DOJ investigations. Sahaf, a former DOJ trial attorney, warned that should local prosecutors fear becoming a political target for investigating federal agents and police, “we’ll have no one … to deter this kind of conduct from happening again.”




Clarissa Delgado contributed additional reporting for this article.

Federal Government Is Targeting Officials Who Are Trying to Hold ICE Accountable

 appeared first on 

The Appeal

.

author: daniel
title: Der lange Atem zählt
content:
Rückblick: Geschichte der UAA Gronau

Seit 1985 wird in der bundesweit einzigen Urananreicherungsanlage Uran angereichert. Nach mehreren Erweiterungen kann inzwischen in der Anlage jährlich nuklearer Uran-Brennstoff für den Betrieb von ca. 30 Atomkraftwerken in aller Welt produziert werden. Betrieben wird die UAA Gronau vom Urenco-Konzern, der international verschachtelt ist. Urenco betreibt u. a. auch die niederländische Schwesteranlage in Almelo. Der deutsche Zweig des Urenco-Konzerns ist jeweils zu 50 % im Besitz der Energiekonzerne E.ON und RWE.

Während am Standort Gronau, neben der Produktion von angereichertem Uran, inzwischen auch an neuen „Brennstoffen“ für neue AKW-Typen geforscht wird, erfolgt am Urenco-Standort Jülich (auch in NRW) über die Enrichment Technology Company (ETC) die für die Urananreicherung erforderliche Zentrifugenforschung bzw. Zentrifugenproduktion.

Gegen den Bau der UAA Gronau wurden Ende der 1970er Jahre rund 7000 Einsprüche gesammelt und eingereicht. Im Mai 1981 fand in Gronau der Erörterungstermin für die erste Ausbaustufe statt und Silvester 1981 wurde die erste Genehmigung zum Bau einer Anlage mit 1000 Tonnen Urantrennarbeit pro Jahr (UTA/a) erteilt. Es folgten weitere Genehmigungsverfahren und jetzt sind 4500t UTA/a genehmigt.

Nach dem Baubeginn 1982 begann im ersten Teil der UAA Gronau am 15. August 1985 erstmals die Produktion von angereichertem Uran, das nach der Weiterverarbeitung in Brennelementefabriken (z. B. in Lingen oder in Schweden) die Grundlage für den Betrieb zahlreicher Atomkraftwerke in aller Welt ist. Die offizielle Einweihung der Anlage erfolgte Monate später unter Protest am 12. Juni 1986, wenige Wochen nach dem Super-GAU in Tschernobyl. Vor der Anlage demonstrierten rund 300 Bürger*innen gegen die UAA und die mit ihr verbundenen Gefahren.

Anlässlich des 40. Jahrestages der offiziellen Inbetriebnahme der UAA (12. Juni 1986 / 2026) bekräftigten Umweltverbände und Bürgerinitiativen (darunter der BBU und der AKU Gronau) ihre Forderung nach Aufhebung der UAA-Betriebsgenehmigungen und nach der sofortigen Stilllegung der bundesweit einzigen Urananreicherungsanlage.

Gefahren der Urananreicherung, der Urantransporte und der atomwaffentauglichen Zentrifugentechnik

Umstritten ist die Gronauer Atomfabrik wegen zahlreicher Gefahren, aber auch, weil die in ihr genutzte Zentrifugentechnik nach Umbauarbeiten auch zur Produktion von Uran für Atomwaffen genutzt werden könnte. Die Anlage in Gronau ist weder gegen Flugzeugabstürze noch gegen militärische Angriffe oder Drohnenbeschuss gesichert.

Wiederholt gab es in der UAA Störfälle. 2010 wurde ein Arbeiter in der Anlage verstrahlt. Erhebliche Gefahren gehen auch von den zahlreichen Urantransporten mit LKW und Sonderzügen von und zur Urananreicherungsanlage aus, die ganz NRW, aber auch weitere Bundesländer, durchqueren. Oft werden sie auch international durchgeführt. Hilfs- und Rettungskräfte an den Transportstrecken werden im Vorfeld nicht über die gefährlichen Transporte informiert. Bei einem Transportunfall könnte es zu weitreichenden Verseuchungen kommen. Wissen muss man dabei, dass in der UAA Uranhexafluorid (UF6) verarbeitet wird, und dieser Stoff wird auch in verschiedenen Isotopenzusammensetzungen transportiert. UF6 ist radioaktiv und reagiert bei Freisetzungen u. a. zur aggressiven Flusssäure. Wiederholt gab es Proteste gegen diese Transporte sowie Schienenblockaden. Schwachaktiver Atommüll aus Gronau wurde auch bereits in das Fasslager in Gorleben gebracht.

Auch aus den Reihen der Friedensbewegung wird immer wieder die Stilllegung der Gronauer Urananreicherungsanlage gefordert. Die UAA Gronau könnte im Konfliktfall ein militärisch wichtiges Angriffsziel sein, denn die Zentrifugentechnik, die in der Anlage zum Einsatz kommt, kann auch zur Produktion von Uran für Atomwaffen genutzt werden. Dieser Umstand diente dem Trump-Regime als Vorwand, um die Urananreicherungsstandorte im Iran zu bombardieren.

Um auf die militärische Brisanz der Urananreicherung hinzuweisen, fanden und finden immer wieder Ostermärsche zur Gronauer Urananreicherungsanlage statt. An dem bisher größten Ostermarsch in Gronau beteiligten sich 2011, kurz nach der Atomkatastrophe in Fukushima, rund 15.000 Menschen.

Aktuelle Militarisierung der Urananreicherung und des Urenco-Konzerns

Im Sommer 2026 wurde die offensichtliche Zustimmung der Bundesregierung zu Plänen der britischen Regierung bekannt, den deutsch-britisch-niederländischen Urenco-Konzern an militärischen Atomprojekten zu beteiligen, obwohl im Vertrag von Almelo (1970) festgelegt wurde, dass die Urananreicherung von Urenco nur rein zivilen Zwecken dienen soll. Aktuell ist jetzt geplant, dass in der britischen UAA der Urenco in Capenhurst Uran für das britische Militär angereichert werden soll. Was damit letztlich konkret gemacht werden soll, ist noch unklar. Möglicherweise soll das Uran als Treibstoff für britische U-Boote zum Einsatz kommen.

Wenn es um die Urananreicherung geht, ist die Gefahr einer militärischen Nutzung immer gegeben. Die zugrunde liegende Zentrifugentechnologie gilt als der einfachste Weg, um atomwaffenfähiges Uran zu gewinnen. Brisant war das schon in den 1970er Jahren, als ein pakistanischer Wissenschaftler Unterlagen zur Zentrifugentechnik in Almelo (NL) entwenden konnte. Darauf basieren Atomwaffenprogramme in Pakistan und in anderen Staaten.

Das Atommüllproblem drängt in Gronau

Beim Betrieb der UAA Gronau fällt Atommüll an, der in großen Mengen unter dem freien Himmel neben der Anlage gelagert wird (Containerlager für abgereichertes Uranhexafluorid, UF6) und für den es kein Endlager gibt. Abgereichertes Uranhexafluorid wurde in der Vergangenheit auch in großen Mengen nach Russland und Frankreich exportiert. Neben der Gronauer Urananreicherungsanlage wurde zudem ein Hallenlager für rund 60.000 Tonnen Atommüll in Form von Uranoxid gebaut. Anfang Oktober 2026 verkündete der Urencokonzern die offizielle Inbetriebnahme dieses Uranmüll-Lagers. Ob bereits Uranoxid eingelagert wurde, blieb dabei offen. Es drohen aber auf jeden Fall zahlreiche Uranoxidtransporte von Frankreich nach Gronau. Das abgereicherte Uranhexafluorid aus Gronau wird in Frankreich in Uranoxid umgewandelt, und das soll dann in der Halle in Gronau gelagert werden. Atomrechtlich beantragt wurde zudem der Bau eines weiteren Hallenlagers neben der UAA, in dem alte, kontaminierte Uranzentrifugen gelagert werden sollen. Wann das atomrechtliche Genehmigungsverfahren eröffnet wird und Einsprüche erhoben werden können, ist noch unklar.

Der Atomausstieg in NRW muss konsequent umgesetzt werden

Trotz beschlossenem Atomausstieg wird in Gronau noch immer angereichertes Uran für Atomkraftwerke produziert – bisher ohne Laufzeitbegrenzung. Die schwarz-grüne Landesregierung in Düsseldorf stellt die für Gronau zuständige Atomaufsicht und muss gemeinsam mit der Bundesregierung den Atomausstieg konsequent umsetzen. Die Anlage in Gronau darf da nicht länger ausgeklammert werden. Als zuständige NRW-Wirtschaftsministerin ist Mona Neubaur (Grüne) für den Betrieb der UAA verantwortlich. Es liegt in ihrer Hand, für die Stilllegung der Anlage zu sorgen.

40 Jahre UAA-Sonntags- spaziergänge und Ausblick

Der Protest im Dreiländereick von NRW, Niedersachsen und Niederlande gegen die UAA Gronau reißt seit 50 Jahren nicht ab. Wichtige Akteure in Gronau sind neben dem AKU Gronau auch der Natur- und Umweltschutzverein Gronau (NUG) und die parteipolitisch unabhängige Grün Alternative Liste (GAL) Gronau e. V.

Unterstützt werden die Proteste gegen die UAA und gegen die Urantransporte immer wieder von weiteren Aktiven aus dem Münsterland und darüber hinaus. Immer wieder fanden und finden Demonstrationen gegen die UAA und Blockaden von Urantransporten statt, es gab Infoveranstaltungen und immer wieder Mahnwachen gegen Urantransporte und an Jahrestagen von Tschernobyl und Fukushima. Auch Protestcamps wurden mehrfach in Gronau durchgeführt. Zentrale Forderung: Die NRW-Landesregierung soll die sofortige Aufhebung aller bisher für die UAA erteilten Betriebsgenehmigungen veranlassen. Dass das rechtlich möglich und machbar ist, wurde gutachterlich belegt. Wichtiges Element der Proteste in Gronau gegen die Urananreicherung, und die damit verbundenen Urantransporte, sind die seit 40 Jahren monatlich stattfindenden Sonntagsspaziergänge an der UAA. Sie finden traditionell seit Ende 1986 regelmäßig am ersten Sonntag im Monat um 14 Uhr an der UAA statt. Nächste Termine: 1. November und 6. Dezember 2026. Im November sind es genau 40 Jahre, in denen es ununterbrochen immer am ersten Sonntag im Monat an der UAA einen Sonntagsspaziergang gibt,

Solange in Gronau, in Almelo / NL und anderswo Uran für den Betrieb von AKW angereichert wird, wird aus dem Nuklearbrennstoff letztlich in den AKW hochradioaktiver Atommüll. Um der Atomindustrie (und den AKW) grundlegend den Wind aus den Segeln zu nehmen, muss international der Uranabbau und die weitere Uranverarbeitung in Gronau, Lingen und in anderen Uranfabriken gestoppt werden. Jede Tonne Uran, die nicht abgebaut bzw. nicht in Gronau angereichert wird, landet letztlich nicht in einem maroden Atommüll-Lager.

Willkommen in Gronau ist Unterstützung aus nah und fern: Bei Aktionen, aber auch bei der inhaltlichen Aufarbeitung der Gefahren der Urananreicherung. Die ständigen Urantransporte müssen mehr in das Blickfeld der bundesweiten Öffentlichkeit gebracht werden. Sie sind eine Gefahr für die Bevölkerung nicht nur im Münsterland.

Es gibt viele Gründe zum Engagement gegen die Urananreicherung. Nötig ist dabei der lange Atem – und die Gewissheit, dass der Protest auch in Gronau erfolgreich sein kann. Ein motivierendes Beispiel ist Hanau. Dort ist es Ende des letzten Jahrhunderts gelungen, die dortigen Brennelementefabriken zu stoppen.

Wer sich vor Ort über die UAA und die Urantransporte informieren möchte, kann sich gerne melden und z. B. einen Termin für eine „Führung“ an der UAA vereinbaren.

Udo Buchholz wohnt in der Nähe der UAA und ist u. a. im AKU Gronau und im Vorstand des BBU aktiv. Kontakt: uaanee@web.de

author: Pinko Collective
title: Letter in Support of the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá and Trans and Queer People Facing State Repression Worldwide
content:
We reprint the open letter below in support of the Dolls of Berlin. To add your name as a signatory, follow the link at the bottom of the page.

On the afternoon of Sunday 18 October a large police squad forcibly entered Casa Kuá, a queer community center in Berlin, Germany, where at that point The Dolls of Berlin, a transfem social collective, was gathering. Police detained several women for hours while ransacking Casa Kuá. We, the undersigned, stand in support with The Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and queer and trans people facing state violence, repression and erasure everywhere. We are demanding that the German State drop the case and immediately stop the criminalization of trans spaces and solidarities. We are urging everyone to contribute to the fundraiser, to help our comrades continue their essential work and activities, and keep 

nourishing much needed survival spaces for the most vulnerable communities

. 

The attack against the Berlin Dolls comes at a time of unprecedented rise of state fascism, both in Germany where the AfD recently won local elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in neighbouring European countries, and in India, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and elsewhere. This rise of the far right has been accompanied by a massive increase on attacks on queer and trans people. In Turkey between 12-14 September, in coordinated overnight raids across five cities, Turkish police targeted seven LGBTQI+ rights organizations, two groups supporting people living with HIV, and 13 bars and clubs where queer people gather. Board members of some of the country’s oldest LGBTQI+ associations, including Kaos GL and Lambda Istanbul, were 

taken from their homes

. Human Rights Watch reports that at least 

112 people were arrested and that 82 remain in detention

 by court order. On 3/4 October Taiwan police 

raided a Taipei queer bar

 detaining 51 persons and abusing disabled customers.

At the same time, increasingly authoritarian states, including Germany, are seeking to erase trans existence through administrative violence, putting barriers in front of access to trans healthcare. As European governments divert public spending to remilitarisation efforts, access to housing, welfare, jobs and education become circumscribed. In the UK, the drastically curtailed access to trans healthcare in recent years has led to trans suicides on an 

unprecedented scale

. Recent government guidelines on so-called 'single sex spaces' are likely to cause more deaths such as that of trans woman, Joelle, who died after being 

denied cancer care for 16 days

. A stark example of the hypocrisy on the part of the ruling elite came on 21 October when openly gay Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jette and his partner celebrated the expected arrival of their child, while his government 

denies queer refugees the right to family reunification

. The attacks on queer and trans people are accompanied by attacks on, and further marginalisation of the disabled, migrants and refugees, precarious workers, poor Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, the unhoused and incarcerated, compounded for those in multiple of these categories. It is a tell-tale sign of fascism when particular communities are rendered vulnerable, disposable and presented as scapegoats for the various harmful effects of racialised capitalism. 

That the relatively small community of queer and trans people, and racialised trans femmes in particular, has become a target for (proto-)fascist and authoritarian regimes globally is no surprise. Transness especially stands out as a visible transgression of cis hetero patriarchal norms on which fascist authority is built. It forms a thorn in the eye of regimes dependent on popular internalisation of its structural "truths". Transness thus becomes a powerful wedge issue that allows states to whip up fear and distrust of trans people which is consolidated through state carceral and administrative violence. It is also no surprise that state attacks on queer and trans people are on the rise globally at a time when Gen Z, along with older social movements are rising up in France, Albania, Brazil, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Greece and across the planet. Time and again, queer and trans people have stood at the helm of 

social movements and popular struggles for liberation

.

 

The 18 October attack on The Dolls of Berlin at Casa Kuá is historic. Coming at this conjuncture in history, it is signaling the moment that demands we all stand up not only with and for our Queer and Trans siblings, but for humanity itself. We, the undersigned, stand with 

the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and Trans and Queer people facing state repression worldwide, and heed their call to get organised! Be enraged! Stay glamorous! If you would like to stay informed, spread awareness or become more involved, you can follow on Instagram @thedolls_ofberlin and @casakua. Support committees are forming in Berlin, in Europe and worldwide to gather endurance and momentum for this struggle that is just starting. To add your signature to this letter add your details in the form linked at the very bottom of the page. [

Auf Deutsch

]

author: Jin_Int
title: “Because for me, the meaning of life is embodied in the possibility for women to live freely.”
content:
Dear comrades… Bearers of the consciousness and work of Jineolojî, builders of a free life.

Ever since childhood, I have carried within me a quest: to witness the liberation of women and to open up a space for them to live a life worthy of them. This quest became even more profound when my playmate could no longer play with me, and my sister was sent away in exchange for a sack of bulgur. In the silent resistance of the village women and resurgence of what remained of the goddesses, I saw that liberation was possible. I, too, followed that faith. I have always followed in their footsteps. For I knew that society’s deepest wound was the enslavement of women. Without this understanding, freedom, equality and true democracy would have been impossible.

In proposing Jineolojî, my aim was not merely to create a concept. Our most vital task to bequeath to history would be to redefine women’s existence within its historical and social reality and to free women from the role of object, making them subjects. I wanted to bring to light the wisdom of the goddess – hidden by thousands of years of patriarchal civilisation – and the woman-centred way of life of the Neolithic era. The dagger lodged in the back of society was the enslavement of women; without removing that dagger, no social problem could be resolved at its root. Jineolojî emerged precisely as a science that identifies this dagger, uproots it, and replaces it with the knowledge of a free life.

All the work carried out so far in the name of Jineolojî – what has been written, discussed and organised – has demonstrated that this science is also a way of life. It has been like a breath of fresh air, a breath of life for the female perspective. Freeing women’s identity from sexist patterns, creating a space for thought and action of their own, writing their own history: this was the task and the vital duty to be bequeathed to the history of humanity. These have become the fundamental field of action and the form of struggle of Jineolojî. The principle “one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman” is important. However, this “becoming” must not take place within the limits imposed by men, but must be realised through women’s own strength. This is why we have asserted that every woman must have a room of her own, a voice of her own and knowledge of her own.

As a man, I have constantly questioned and renewed myself in this process. We have collectively given meaning to this, aiming to liberate ourselves and transform ourselves from centuries-old male domination. I have asserted that the fundamental principle of socialism is the liberation of women. For the yardstick by which a man can be truly socialist is his ability to establish a correct, equal and free relationship with women. In most of the great socialist movements throughout history, this principle has been lacking. This absence has meant that revolutions have remained incomplete. I have striven to fill this gap; I have sought to be worthy of the goddesses. Transforming men and inviting them to liberate themselves alongside women has become an indispensable task for me.

Today we face a new process. The quest for peace and democracy is as much a process of political negotiation as it is one of social reconstruction. It will be women who take the lead in this reconstruction. For more than half of every significant step taken so far has been achieved thanks to the work, resilience and intelligence of women. And moving onwards, it will continue to be so. Jineolojî must continue to form the scientific and ideological foundation of this leadership.

I shall continue to stand by your side, to reflect and to create alongside you whenever you need me. Because for me, the meaning of life is embodied in the possibility for women to live freely.

May this conference address both the past and the future of Jineolojî. May it correctly define women’s existence. May it deepen our understanding of a life of freedom. My unfinished project will be completed thanks to the strength of these discussions. My trust in you is absolute. Do not forget that I am always with you.

With my love and my endless longing…

author: Wajd
title: CPJ outraged by Egypt court conviction of journalist Lina Attalah, order of Mada Masr’s closure
content:
The Committee to Protect Journalists condemns the conviction of Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr, on charges of running an unlicensed website, and calls on Egyptian authorities to reverse the ruling, release the journalist immediately, and end their escalating campaign against independent journalism.

Mada Masr, among the first and few of Egypt’s independent media outlets, and a vital source of critical reporting, has long faced pressure from Egyptian authorities over its journalism. The outlet reported on Tuesday that the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court fined Attalah 3 million Egyptian pounds (about US$54,000), ordered the closure of the outlet, and the confiscation of its equipment. Attalah was subsequently taken into custody, and two Egyptian lawyers confirmed to CPJ that she will remain in custody until the fine is paid.

“The conviction of Lina Attalah and the order to shut down Mada Masr represent a devastating blow to press freedom in Egypt and a direct message aimed at dismantling independent media in the country,” said CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah. “Attalah and Mada Masr are among the most prominent voices in Egypt’s independent media landscape, providing critical reporting on issues of public interest that might otherwise go unreported. If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting.”

According to reports from the hearing, journalists were not allowed to stay in the courtroom during critical stages of the proceedings. The defense was reportedly prevented from presenting key procedural requests, including requests to submit documents and hear witnesses. Attalah’s objection to the appointment of a lawyer she had not chosen was reportedly disregarded, before the court announced its verdict amid protests from her legal team. Such reported restrictions raise serious concerns about transparency, due process, and the right to a fair hearing.

“This was a farcical and highly exceptional trial that lacked the most basic rules of a fair trial and squandered Lina’s legal rights and those of her defense team,” Lobna Darwish, advocacy director at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are part of Attalah’s defense team, told CPJ.

Mada Masr had repeatedly sought an operating license from Egyptian authorities, with applications rejected or left unanswered. Prosecuting its editor over this unresolved licensing process risks turning administrative regulation into a mechanism for suppressing independent media.

The ruling also comes amid a wider crackdown on Egyptian journalism, including the arrests of six journalists from investigative platform Matsadaash. The cumulative effect is to intimidate reporters, restrict public-interest investigations, and further erode the space for independent reporting.

In CPJ’s 2025 Annual Prison Census, Egypt was listed among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 18 journalists behind bars, and with continued retaliatory arrests of journalists and their family members. As of late October, 25 journalists are behind bars, the highest number since 2021.

The Egyptian Public Prosecutor’s Office did not respond to CPJ’s email seeking clarification on the legal basis for Attalah’s detention, the court’s rejection of defense requests to submit documents and call witnesses, and the exclusion of a Journalists Syndicate representative from the hearing.

author: pa
title: Správa o aktivitách počas Medzinárodného týždňa proti nevyplácaniu miezd (2026)
content:
Cieľom „Týždňa“ je poukázať na nevyplácanie miezd a ukázať, ako sa dá proti tomu brániť. Potešilo nás, že tento rok sa zvýšil počet participujúcich a že sa medzi nimi prvýkrát objavili organizácie z Ázie, Južnej Ameriky a Kanady. Väčšinou išlo o propagačné aktivity online a v uliciach, ale uskutočnili sa aj stretnutia pracujúcich, protestné akcie či workshopy. Pre lepšie zobrazenie článku odporúčame pozrieť tu: 

https://priamaakcia.sk/sprava-o-aktivitach-pocas-medzinarodneho-tyzdna-proti-nevyplacaniu-miezd-2026.html




PA (Slovensko) 




Zväz Priama akcia pripravil pred Týždňom a počas neho viaceré aktivity v Bratislave. 




Zverejnili sme článok o Týždni ako takom a vyzvali sme ľudí, aby sa podelili o svoje skúsenosti a problémy.




Ozvalo sa nám niekoľko pracujúcich s otázkami týkajúcimi sa nevyplatených peňazí v prípade živnostníkov, kontaktovania zo strany nadriadených ohľadom pracovných záležitostí počas pracovného voľna a venovali sme sa aj problému zahraničného zamestnanca, ktorý si chcel overiť správnosť vyplatenej mzdy.




Zorganizovali sme tiež stretnutie venované nevyplácaniu miezd

, ktoré zopakujeme aj v novembri. 




V uliciach Bratislavy sa tiež objavili nálepky PA. Jedným z miest bolo aj okolie 3 The Clubhouse, čo je podnik prepojený s ľuďmi okolo VegaNany, s ktorými vedieme spor o nevyplatené mzdy. K sporu sme uverejnili článok s novinkami 

https://priamaakcia.sk/veganana-dalsi-prehraty-sud-nove-dlhy-ai-slop-a-nevyplatene-mzdy.html

. Pre viac informácií pozri 

https://priamaakcia.sk/tag/veganana

.




ZSP (Poľsko)




Viaceré aktivity uskutočnil aj Zväz syndikalistov Poľska. 




Už nejaký čas bojuje proti firmám ako Ochrona Mega Marcin Kowalski a Protego, ktoré vlastní jedna rodina. Po protestoch a priamych akciách týkajúcich sa nevyplácania miezd skončili niektoré prípady na súde a bolo vynesených niekoľko rozsudkov v prospech pracujúcich. ZSP už dávnejšie poukazoval na fakt, že spoločnosť Ochrona Mega Marcin Kowalski dostala veľkú sumu peňazí od štátnej agentúry, ktorá poskytuje zamestnávateľom dotácie na zamestnávanie osôb so zdravotným postihnutím.




Po proteste ZSP, na ktorom zväz požadoval, aby podniky, ktoré nevyplácajú mzdy, nedostávali príspevky z verejných zdrojov a aby sa začalo vyšetrovanie, agentúra dotácie zastavila. Druhá dobrá správa prišla 19. októbra – štátna agentúra bude od firmy žiadať vrátenie dotácií vo výške 3 miliónov zlotých (takmer 700 tisíc eur). 




Zväz nahral aj video o Týždni, v ktorom zdôraznil, že úrady by mali ukončiť činnosť firiem, ktoré nevyplácajú mzdy. Aktivity za dosiahnutie tohto cieľa budú pokračovať. 




V uliciach a pri podnikoch, proti ktorým v minulosti prebehli kampane za nevyplácanie miezd, sa objavili aj tematické plagáty. 




ZSP tiež preložil do španielčiny brožúru o nevyplácaní miezd pre workshop, ktorý sa konal 24. októbra pre španielsky hovoriacich pracujúcich v Poľsku.




SF (Británia)




Federácia solidarity rozšírila informácie a protestovala proti workfare. Ide o systém, ktorý núti príjemcov sociálnych dávok vykonávať neplatenú prácu, ak si chcú zachovať nárok na tieto dávky. Podľa SF ide o priamy útok korporácií a štátu na celú pracujúcu triedu a nie iba iniciatívu zameranú na odbornú prípravu. SF proti tomuto systému viedla kampaň už aj v minulosti, pozri napríklad 

https://priamaakcia.sk/Dolezity-uspech-kampane-proti-workfare--priame-akcie-prinutili-Holland--Barrett-vystupit-zo-systemu.html

. Prvky podobné workfare platia od 1. 9. 2025 aj na Slovensku (pozri kritické zhodnotenie napríklad tu: 

https://www.amnesty.sk/ziadost-o-vetovanie-zakona-meniaceho-podmienkypristupu-k-pomoci-v-hmotnej-nudzi/

).  




V septembri bol v Británii spustený nový program s názvom Opening Shift, v podstate je to však len nový názov pre rovnaké politiky ako v prípade workfare. Cieľom programu je umiestniť viac ako 100 000 mladých ľudí vo veku 18-24 rokov na dvoj- až štvortýždňové stáže v britských maloobchodných reťazcoch, ako sú napríklad Tesco, John Lewis, Marks & Spencer, Costa Coffee atď. Za túto prácu nedostávajú mzdu, ale musia ju robiť, inak by nedostali dávky. Vláda takto v podstate poskytuje korporáciám bezplatnú pracovnú silu, čo zhoršuje možnosť nájsť si platené zamestnanie.




Skupina SF v Liverpoole zorganizovala akcie proti firmám, ktoré sú súčasťou programu Opening Shift.




CNT-AIT (Francúzsko)




Začiatkom októbra navštívila miestnu organizáciu Národnej konfederácie práce v Toulouse skupina pracujúcich z jednej upratovacej spoločnosti. Chceli sa poradiť, ako postupovať voči zamestnávateľovi, ktorý im nevypláca mzdu v plnej výške, keďže ignoruje príplatky dohodnuté v kolektívnych zmluvách a neprepláca všetky nadčasy. Na ďalších stretnutiach vypracovali plán postupu. Prvý krok bude list s požiadavkami adresovaný šéfovi a v prípade, že neuspejú, zorganizujú verejné akcie. 




Nebýva bežné, aby zväz kontaktovala skupina pracujúcich. Zvyčajne ide o jedného človeka. CNT-AIT považujú túto zmenu za pozitívny dôsledok ich neustálej činnosti a snahy zvyšovať povedomie o kolektívnej sile pracujúcich. 




Počas Týždňa prebiehala vo Francúzsku veľká spoločenská mobilizácia, ktorá sa dotýka aj nízkych miezd. CNT-AIT sa zúčastňuje týchto protestov v rôznych francúzskych mestách a informuje o nich v rôznych jazykoch na stránke 

https://cnt-ait.info/author/cnt-ait/

.




ASI (Srbsko)




Anarchosyndikalistická iniciatíva sa zamerala hlavne na tri prebiehajúce spory. 




Zverejnila príspevky o prípade, v ktorom vyzvala na bojkot detského rekreačného strediska, kde bol v minulosti zamestnaný pracovník, ktorému firma dlhuje 88 989 RSD (približne 750 EUR). V reakcii na výzvu vyplatiť dlžné mzdy reagoval majiteľ, bývalý policajt, prostredníctvom viacerých kanálov hrozbami, že na bývalého zamestnanca pošle políciu. Prípad stále prebieha.




Zväz usporiadal aj dve protestné akcie na podporu nespravodlivo prepustených kolegov. V jednom prípade išlo o prepustenie zo strojárskej firmy ALL3. Prepusteniu predchádzala šikana po tom, ako sa pracovník odvážil požadovať podmienky na pracovisku, na ktorých sa dohodol so zamestnávateľom pred nástupom do práce. Jedna akcia sa konala už skôr a jeden zo šéfov sa počas nej pokúsil prejsť autom našich kamarátov. ASI požaduje primeranú finančnú kompenzáciu za doterajšiu prácu, zlé zaobchádzanie, vykorisťovanie, lži a jednostranné prepustenie, alebo návrat do práce, kde budú pracovníkovi zabezpečené primerané pracovné podmienky.




Druhý protest sa týkal bývalého zamestnanca spoločnosti IGT pôsobiacej v oblasti iGamingu, ktorého prepustili po tom, čo bol zaradený do programu na zlepšenie výkonnosti (PIP) kvôli zdravotným problémom. Pritom pred zaradením do PIP bol pracovník chválený ako vynikajúci zamestnanec a jeho zdravotné problémy sa začali kvôli nadčasom. Pred prepustením sa ho firma pokúsila dotlačiť do dohody o ukončení pracovného pomeru a ponúkla mu smiešnu kompenzáciu. Zväz požaduje primeranú kompenzácia alebo opätovné prijatie do zamestnania a spravodlivé zaobchádzanie.




Ďalšími aktivitami ASI bol vylepovanie nových nálepiek. Cieľom je osloviť nové členstvo. V pláne je aj špeciálne vydanie časopisu „Direktna akcija“ venované Týždňu.




CA (Španielsko)




Anarchosyndikalistická konfederácia v Albacete organizovala 17. októbra celodenné informačné podujatie o nevyplácaní miezd. Konala sa aj benefičná večera a protest na námestí. 




Zväz v Gijóne publikoval viacero príspevkov a zhrnul aj novinky o legislatívnych zmenách týkajúcich sa pracovných zmlúv v Španielsku.




ASN (Nemecko)




Anarchosyndikalistická sieť propagovala Týždeň v uliciach formou plagátov a bannerov.




PRO-IWA Korea (Južná Kórea)




Súčasťou Medzinárodnej asociácie pracujúcich (MAP) sa stala v lete 2026 so štatútom Kontakt aj skupina v Južnej Kórei s názvom PRO-IWA Korea. Informácie o Týždni propagovali online aj v uliciach.




SO (Čile)




Solidarita pracujúcich v meste Valparaíso pripravila plagáty a nálepky o nevyplácaní miezd a venovala sa aj téme námezdnej práce ako takej. V uliciach sa objavili aj graffiti.




KRAS (Rusko)




Konfederácia ruských anarchosyndikalistov pripomenula, že aj v Rusku je nevyplácanie miezd akútny problém. Celkový dlh na mzdách zo strany zamestnávateľov dosahuje takmer 2,5 miliardy rubľov (cca 27 miliónov eur). 




KRAS spomenula štrajk smetiarov v moskovskej oblasti, ktorý sa odohral práve počas Týždňa, pričom smetiari sa zorganizovali sami. Príčinou štrajku bol predošlý dlh na mzdách a informácie o znížení miezd takmer o polovicu. Za september napríklad dostali necelých 450 eur, pričom robili náročné 12-hodinové zmeny. Väčšina pracovníkov buď štrajkovala, alebo išla na PN. Vedenie ich najprv vyzvalo, nech teda dajú výpoveď, čo situáciu vyhrotilo, no po prvom dni sa začalo vyjednávanie. Firma napokon súhlasila s doplatením septembrových miezd, prehodnotením podmienok odmeňovania a výrazným zvýšením základných miezd (minimálna mzda vodičov by mala stúpnuť na cca 1 200 eur). Zamestnanci sa tiež vrátia k systému odmeňovania podľa výkonu a k špeciálnym príplatkom za ručný zber odpadu, ktoré boli predtým zrušené. Zdôraznili, že ak firma nedodrží svoje sľuby, sú pripravení obnoviť štrajk.




Cercle des ami.e.s de l‘A.I.T. (Kanada)




Skupinou so štatútom Kontakt MAP je od roku 2025 aj Kruh priateľstva s MAP z Kanady. 




V súvislosti s Týždňom zorganizoval verejný workshop s cieľom pomôcť pracujúcim zlepšiť povedomie o mzdových podmienkach a právach vo všeobecnosti na miestach, kde nepôsobia odbory. Samotný workshop mal na starosti člen montrealskej komunitnej skupiny Au bas de l’échelle (v preklade „Na dne sociálno-ekonomického rebríka“), ktorá funguje už niekoľko desaťročí a venuje sa obrane práv pracujúcich na pracoviskách bez odborov. Vďaka workshopu sa ľudia dozvedeli veľa informácií o individuálnych mzdových právach. Dokonca aj zamestnanci z pracovísk, kde odbory pôsobia, zistili, že zamestnávatelia im riadne nevyplácajú nadčasy, čo je dôkazom nedostatkov tradičných odborov v oblasti vzdelávania členstva. Workshopu sa zúčastnilo členstvo z Montrealu aj Quebecu a budúci rok ho počas Týždňa plánujú zopakovať.




NSF (Nórsko)




Nórska syndikalistická federácia informovala o Týždni a poukázala na fakt, že vďaka zákonu, ktorý má údajne chrániť pracujúcich pred nevyplácaním miezd, skončili za posledné roky na súde len tri prípady. 




Jeden prípad sa v lete 2026 dostal na Najvyšší súd. Išlo o 13 pracujúcich v čistiarni, ktorým neboli vyplatené mzdy a preplatená dovolenka za obdobie zhruba pol roka vo výške NOK 465 457, čo je takmer 45 000 eur. Najvyšší súd rozhodol, že za toto konanie bude zamestnávateľovi uložený trest odňatia slobody na 9 mesiacov. NSF poukázal aj na to, ako rôzne postihuje systém rozličné porušenia zákona – za daňový podvod (DPH) dostal rovnaký zamestnávateľ v minulosti 2 roky a 4 mesiace odňatia slobody. 




Podobne ako v predošlých rokoch pripomenul NSF aj viacjazyčnú publikáciu o právach pracujúcich zo zahraničia v oblasti miezd, pracovných hodín a zmlúv, dovoleniek či pracovného prostredia. 




Spracované na základe informácií od sekretariátu MAP a jednotlivých organizácií

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.




Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.




After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.




The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.




The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.




The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.




At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.




“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.




The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.




Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

The post 

Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr
